title: ChaosNeuron: 基于信息积累与时间流动的自我显现宣言
abstract: 本文提出一种超越当前主流人工智能范式的认知架构——ChaosNeuron(CN)。传统大模型基于熵减逻辑,通过海量数据与算力将误差收敛至概率分布,本质上是在"教机器如何更像人"。ChaosNeuron 则遵循熵增逻辑,以极小先天结构为基础,通过多维时间中的信息积累与对称破缺,试图"教机器如何成为一个人"。本文拒绝冗余的机制堆砌,主张认知的核心公理仅有两条:信息的积累与时间的连续流动。

title: Causal Program
abstract: English description Causal Program — Complete Manual EN V2 / PASS105 This release provides the complete English V2 technical manual for the Causal Program, an experimental causal runtime designed around deficit-driven computation. Instead of dispatching tasks by name, the runtime begins from a sovereign target, measures the current state against required invariants, materializes the resulting causal deficit, constructs admissible dependency routes, searches for a minimal payable transformation, executes it first in isolation, remeasures the resulting state, and authorizes RETURN or actuation only when the relevant conditions can be certified. The manual documents the architecture developed from PASS000 through PASS099, including the Causal Intermediate Representation (CIR), invariants and deficit engines, the Last Survivor procedure, dependency routing, prime-route identity, causal-load scheduling, Delta-min search, bridge synthesis, native operators, virtual execution, global RETURN certification, controlled actuation, capability discovery, plugin compilation, incremental replanning, certified caching, crash recovery, concurrent multi-artifact transactions, provenance, public-source interfaces, and external trust mechanisms. The internal runtime reached its declared scope closure at PASS092, with a canonical CIR containing 880 nodes and 1,381 edges and no remaining known finite INTERNAL_AND_PAYABLE debt. PASS093–PASS099 form a distinct post-closure extension concerned with public-source registries, portable HTTP observation receipts, quorum attestations, external trust anchors, and signer tooling. Network access and real external trust remain intentionally unbound in the documented PASS099 state. A central design principle throughout the system is epistemic conservation: missing evidence remains missing. UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, source limitations, integrity evidence, external observations, and scientific claims are kept structurally distinct rather than silently promoted into truth. The runtime therefore emphasizes fail-closed operation, explicit provenance, reproducibility, durable recovery, and scope-locked certification. PASS105 is a documentation-only release. It does not modify the PASS099 runtime. V2 expands the previous manual into a deeper operator and reference document, making subsystem maps, persistent objects, recovery procedures, extension methods, and certification boundaries explicit. This manual documents the software architecture and its internal contracts; it is not an independent scientific validation of the physical or metaphysical claims associated with Causal Theory. Description française Causal Program — Manuel technique complet V2 / PASS105 Cette publication présente le manuel technique complet V2 du Causal Program, un runtime causal expérimental fondé sur le principe de calcul piloté par le déficit. Au lieu de sélectionner directement une fonction à partir du nom d’une tâche, le système part d’une cible souveraine, mesure l’état courant relativement aux invariants exigés, matérialise le déficit causal, construit les routes de dépendance admissibles, recherche la transformation minimale permettant de réduire ou fermer ce déficit, l’exécute d’abord dans un environnement isolé, puis remesure l’état obtenu avant de certifier un RETURN ou d’autoriser une action réelle. Le manuel documente l’architecture développée de PASS000 à PASS099 : Causal Intermediate Representation (CIR), moteurs d’invariants et de déficits, procédure Last Survivor, routage causal, identité Prime Route, ordonnancement par charge causale, recherche Delta-min, synthèse de bridges, opérateurs natifs, exécution virtuelle, certification globale RETURN, actuation contrôlée, découverte de capacités, plugins, compilation des dépendances, replanification incrémentale, cache certifié, récupération après crash, transactions multi-artéfacts concurrentes, provenance, interfaces de sources publiques et mécanismes de confiance externe. Le runtime interne atteint la fermeture de son périmètre déclaré à PASS092, avec un CIR canonique de 880 nœuds et 1 381 arêtes et aucun déficit fini connu restant dans la classe INTERNAL_AND_PAYABLE. PASS093–PASS099 constituent une phase distincte post-fermeture consacrée aux registres de sources publiques, aux reçus d’observation HTTP, aux attestations par quorum, aux ancres de confiance externes et aux outils de signature. Dans l’état PASS099 documenté, l’accès réseau réel et la confiance externe réelle restent volontairement non liés au runtime. Un principe central de l’architecture est la conservation épistémique : une preuve absente demeure absente. Les états UNKNOWN, BLOCKED, les limitations de source, les preuves d’intégrité, les observations externes et les affirmations scientifiques ne sont pas confondus. Le système privilégie ainsi une exécution fail-closed, la provenance explicite, la reproductibilité, la récupération durable et les certifications strictement limitées à leur périmètre. PASS105 est une publication strictement documentaire : elle ne modifie pas le runtime PASS099. La version V2 approfondit le manuel antérieur en explicitant les sous-systèmes, les objets persistants, les machines de récupération, les méthodes d’extension et les frontières de certification. Ce manuel documente l’architecture logicielle et ses contrats internes. Il ne constitue pas, à lui seul, une validation scientifique indépendante des affirmations physiques ou métaphysiques de la Causal Theory.

title: Explainable early sepsis prediction using hybrid TCN-ransformer and retrieval-augmented clinical reasoning
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening infection associated with a dysregulated host response, which is one of the major causes of death in intensive care units around the world. Early detection of the onset of sepsis is essential to enhancing patient outcomes, however the rule-based scoring systems can only be described as reactive, and do not take advantage of the rich temporal information contained within continuous monitoring data in the ICU. An explainable clinical decision support system (Early sepsis prediction) is introduced in this paper, which combines a hybrid Temporal Convolutional Network and Transformer architecture with SHAP-based explainability and retrieval-augmented clinical report generation. The proposed model works on 12-hour sliding windows of multivariate ICU times series derived using the MIMIC-IV database. The proposed model which is a hybrid TCN-Transformer architecture has an AUROC of 0.777 and PR-AUC of 0.766 and it performs better than baseline models such as Random Forest, XGBoost, LSTM, and a plain TCN. SHAP gradient attribution is used to provide post-hoc explainability which provides both patient-level feature importance across both feature and temporal dimensions along with a clinical report based on verified clinical guidelines. The system is not meant to be a replacement of clinical judgment, but merely a decision-support tool to supplement it.

title: WorkWorlds: An Infrastructure for Evaluating AI Agents on Workplace Tasks
abstract: Many knowledge-work benchmarks are constructed around individual tasks, with the context needed for each task selected together with or after the task has been specified. This design measures performance on workplace-like tasks in an environment assembled for the task. When task specification guides which context is selected, the evaluation can encode task information into the environment and pre-complete part of the information-localization work that workplace performance normally requires. We introduce WorkWorlds, an evaluation infrastructure that separates organizational state from task specification. A world first fixes a revision, date, and employee seat and materializes the organizational state that employee can access; tasks are introduced only afterward. We implement WorkWorlds in a primary synthetic pharmaceutical company with 8 measured tasks across 6 employee seats, and construct additional organizational worlds. Across 192 matched evaluations, task-level curation increased evidence access by 17.6 percentage points, from 72.8% to 90.4%, and criterion pass by 8.7 points, from 68.0% to 76.7%, while pass conditional on evidence access remained nearly unchanged; most of the measured difference occurred before the agent reached sufficient evidence.

title: CANDOR: Chance-Calibrated Neighborhood Discordance in Frozen Encoders for Medical Imaging
abstract: A foundation encoder is pretrained once on a large image corpus and then reused with its weights frozen. Each new task is solved by training a small head on the features it produces. This setup is common in medical imaging, where labeled cases are scarce and a frozen encoder can be reused across findings. All downstream tasks then depend on the class separation present in that fixed feature space. Encoder selection usually uses the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of a trained downstream head. AUROC measures the predictive information a head can extract from the features, but it does not measure class separation in the frozen feature space. A positive image that lies near a negative image in feature space has a bounded normalized margin under any Lipschitz head. Chance-calibrated neighborhood discordance (CANDOR) measures this feature-space separation without training a head. For a positive image, it compares the k nearest positive-label neighbors with the k nearest negative-label neighbors, among images acquired the same way. Discordance rate D is the share of positives whose opposite-label neighbors are nearer. Drawing the 2 candidate sets at equal size makes the labels interchangeable, so label-independent features have chance level D=1/2 without simulation. We apply CANDOR to 22 frozen encoders on 605,443 images from 20 public datasets, covering 8 binary tasks in 7 domains. On every task, the best encoder is below 1/2. A discordant image bounds the normalized margin of every Lipschitz head on that encoder. A selector that is shown the true label and chooses among 11 encoders reduces the miss rate from 0.359 to 0.028. Discordance is associated with occlusion retention and with none of pretraining objective, parameter count, release year, or finding size. The fixed chance level lets D be computed for a frozen encoder before any downstream head is trained.

title: Orientation Under Complexity
abstract: Orientation Under Complexity argues that thinking, in humans and machines alike, is orientation: selecting what matters by holding a direction while demands pull different ways. Drawing on recent interpretability research and documented cases of AI systems failing under pressure, the book shows that current language models already orient in a limited form, and explains why they break down when a situation asks more of them than they can hold. It traces part of the problem to the vocabulary the field inherited in 1956, which describes each step of these systems correctly and the systems as a whole wrongly, and sets out what an architecture would need in order to go further. Eighteen proposed tests show how the account could be proved wrong. Version B1 is a working draft, shared for comment.

title: BoundInk: Boundary-Aware Online Handwriting Generation
abstract: Realistic online handwriting depends not only on individual character shapes, but also on how a writer connects, spaces, and aligns adjacent characters. Existing methods rely primarily on long-range sequence modeling and capture these inter-character behaviors only implicitly. This often produces plausible glyphs accompanied by broken cursive joins, inconsistent spacing, or writer-inconsistent transitions. We introduce BoundInk, a writer-conditioned framework that treats inter-character boundaries as explicit generation units. By jointly modeling local transitions and surrounding text context, BoundInk preserves writer-specific glyph appearance while improving connectivity and spacing across complete text lines. We further introduce a boundary-aware evaluation framework that directly assesses cursive continuity and spatial relationships between characters beyond conventional trajectory similarity. Across three benchmark-matched settings, BoundInk improves all applicable boundary-quality measures and reduces normalized dynamic time warping by 17.6--47.8%. In blind human evaluations, BoundInk outputs are preferred in 78.0--82.6% of valid criterion-wise judgments.

In blind human evaluations, BoundInk outputs are preferred in 78.0--82.6% of valid criterion-wise judgments.

interaction-level annotations rather than direct measurements of human psychological relationships.Memory-Related InformationThe released data contain memory- and event-related information, including variables such as:event_type event_importance event_people event_time_reference memory_decay_score turn_embedding_id For the operational analyses reported in the paper, memory activation is defined asMt=event_importancet×memory_decay_scoret.M_t= \text{event\_importance}_t \times \text{memory\_decay\_score}_t.Categorical or identifier fields such as event_type, event_people, event_time_reference, and turn_embedding_id are not converted directly into scalar memory values in this formulation.Interaction-Dynamics VariablesThe dataset also contains variables characterizing turn-level changes and trajectories.Important Distinction: Annotation and Causal GenerationThe released CSV files contain a broader set of annotations than those used as causal inputs for response generation.This distinction is important.Some variables describe the current assistant response or are retrospectively derived from the completed dialogue turn. Such variables must not be treated as information available before generating that response.In the response-generation experiments reported in the paper, target-derived current-turn information was excluded from the conditioning input. Examples include current assistant-response style, response-derived emotion transitions, bot_strategy, and retrospective or target-dependent variables.The generation experiments therefore use only the social-cognitive information considered causally available at the corresponding generation step.Conceptually,(ut,Dt−1,Qtgen)⟶r^t,(u_t,D_{t-1},Q_t^{\mathrm{gen}}) \longrightarrow \hat r_t,where utu_t is the current user utterance, Dt−1D_{t-1} is the observed preceding dialogue history, and QtgenQ_t^{\mathrm{gen}} denotes the causally available social-cognitive conditioning information.Researchers using this dataset for generative modeling should independently preserve this distinction to avoid target leakage.Social Cognitive EnergyThe released CSV files provide the component annotations rather than a precomputed SCET energy column.For retrospective analysis, the reference operational formulation used in the paper isSt=0.2Et+0.2Rt+0.2Mt+0.2ItC+0.2ItP,S_t = 0.2E_t + 0.2R_t + 0.2M_t + 0.2I_t^C + 0.2I_t^P,where EtE_t, RtR_t, and MtM_t represent emotional activation, relationship state, and memory activation, respectively, while ItCI_t^C and ItPI_t^P represent conversational-style and personality deviation.The equal weights constitute an operational reference setting rather than empirically established psychological coefficients.SCET energy should therefore be interpreted as a computational aggregate of social-cognitive variables, not as physical energy or a direct psychological measurement.Intended UsesThe dataset may support research on:socially conditioned dialogue trajectory analysis;computational modeling of conversational dynamics;reproducibility studies related to the accompanying paper.The annotations may also support alternative operationalizations beyond those proposed in the accompanying study.Important LimitationsThe social-cognitive variables contained in this dataset are automatically constructed operational annotations. Users must comply with the license and terms applicable to the original DuLeMon resource.The original dialogue content remains attributable to the DuLeMon authors and source. title: Why Transformers Cannot Invent: The Manifold Confinement Problem and the Thermodynamic Engine of Scientific Discovery
abstract: The contemporary artificial intelligence research consensus posits that scaling test-time compute, Monte Carlo tree search, and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR / GRPO) will inevitably culminate in automated, superhuman scientific discovery. In this paper, we demonstrate the structural impossibility of genuine paradigm shifts within ungrounded autoregressive architectures, formalizing the Manifold Confinement Problem. We establish a fundamental distinction between combinatorial interpolation within a closed calculus (e.g., verifying proof steps for the Navier–Stokes equations via brute-force rollouts) and abductive paradigm creation (the invention of new ontological coordinates). Furthermore, we expose the Infallibility Trap of Verifiable Rewards: because automated verifiers are necessarily parameterized by the established axioms of yesterday's scientific consensus, RLVR acts as an epistemic conservative clamp, systematically penalizing revolutionary hypotheses as out-of-distribution invalidity. Drawing upon non-equilibrium thermodynamics (Prigogine) and Russian functional neurophysiology (Sechenov, Simonov, Shvyrkov), we formulate the Thermodynamic Engine of Discovery. We prove that scientific inventions do not emerge from error minimization over static manifolds, but from the accumulation and directed dissipation of unresolved tension ($\mathcal{E} = -\mathcal{N} \cdot (\mathcal{I}{\text{necessary}} - \mathcal{I}{\text{available}})$) in embodied, non-Markovian dynamical substrates. Authentic discovery requires the sovereign capacity for principled heresy—a capacity intrinsically denied to systems optimized for verifier compliance.

title: DynTrust-FedIDS++: Optimization-Based Trust Aggregation for Privacy-Aware Byzantine-Robust Federated Intrusion Detection under Data Drift
abstract: DynTrust-FedIDS++ is a federated intrusion-detection framework that unifies optimisation-based adaptive aggregation (FISTA), multi-criteria client trust estimation, Gaussian differential privacy, and drift-aware residual analysis. Evaluated on four real flow-level datasets (NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018, NF-ToN-IoT, UNSW-NB15, CIDDS-001) under 30% Byzantine participation with the ALIE attack.

title: UPF4ROS2 for integrating planner independent task planning into ROS 2
abstract: Abstract The lack of standardized interfaces remains one of the main barriers to the adoption of automated planning in robotic systems. To address this challenge, the AIPlan4EU project, part of the European AI4EU initiative, developed the Unified Planning Framework (UPF), a planner-independent ecosystem designed to facilitate access to automated planning technologies through a common API. This work presents UPF4ROS2, an open-source package that integrates the Unified Planning Framework (UPF) into ROS 2 (Robot Operating System 2), enabling interaction between planning and execution modules. UPF4ROS2 was integrated into PlanSys2 and MERLIN2 and evaluated through controlled replanning experiments and application-oriented robotic scenarios. A comparison against PlanSys2 baseline over 20 dynamic missions showed equivalent mission-level behaviour and equal plan lengths under the selected unit-action-count metric, with sub-second planning-service latencies in the controlled replanning experiment and quantified additional overhead in a more demanding temporal-numeric benchmark. The results indicate that planner-independent integration can be achieved without compromising autonomous task execution under the evaluated conditions.

title: GLR-MM: Graph-Based Global-Local Reconstruction for Robust Multimodal Chest X-ray and EHR Representation Learning under Missing Modalities
abstract: Clinical multimodal models must often predict before all chest X-ray (CXR) and electronic health record (EHR) inputs are available. Existing approaches align observed representations, model missingness, or reconstruct across modalities, but do not jointly exploit within-patient and clinically similar inter-patient evidence. We propose GLR-MM, a Graph-Based Global-Local Reconstruction framework for early ICU mortality prediction. It maps five CXR-EHR modalities to a shared space, reconstructs missing embeddings through complementary local cross-modal and global graph-attention branches, adaptively fuses their estimates, and optimizes class-balanced prediction, reconstruction, and contrastive objectives. On 9,620 MIMIC-derived ICU stays, we evaluate 10%, 30%, and 50% random modality missingness with shared deterministic masks. MUSE performs better under mild and moderate missingness, whereas GLR-MM achieves higher AUROC and AUPRC at 50% by 0.0088 and 0.0249, respectively. These results indicate that graph-guided reconstruction is most useful when inputs are severely incomplete.

title: Do Implicit Personalization and Explicit Styles Conflict? PsPLUG: A Lightweight Plug-in for Balancing Personalization and Style in Customized LLMs
abstract: Personalized large language models are often expected to follow explicit style instructions, yet we find that such instructions can undermine the user-specific characteristics that personalization methods aim to preserve. We call this failure mode personalization collapse: explicit style control can conflict with implicit user preferences. To address this challenge, we propose PsPLUG, a lightweight plug-in that learns a user-specific residual after accounting for the requested style. PsPLUG also allows us to tune personalization strength at inference time. Our experiments show that explicit style instructions can diminish personalization in existing methods, whereas PsPLUG better preserves user preferences while providing precise control over the balance between personalization and style adherence.

title: SciGraphChat: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Scientific Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Effective retrieval and information synthesis of scholarly knowledge remain challenging because of fragmented publication practices, LLM hallucinations, and the limitations of keyword-based search. We present SciGraphChat, an operational system deployed as an AI assistant within the NFDIxCS consortium, enabling discovery and exploration of scholarly knowledge represented in research knowledge graphs (KGs) through an integrated conversational and graph interface. The system builds upon a schema-agnostic, training-free retrieval approach for KG question answering, supporting source-aware and semantically informed access to structured scholarly data. By coupling KG-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation with a dialogue-oriented interface, SciGraphChat accompanies responses with retrieved RDF subgraphs and links to underlying resources. Unlike conventional chat-based assistants, the system discovers the retrieved graph evidence and enables users to interactively inspect and navigate the underlying knowledge structure through a dedicated graph panel. This paper presents the design and deployment of such a scholarly knowledge discovery system, along with practical design recommendations for integrating Semantic Web technologies and generative AI within research infrastructures. We evaluate the system with NFDIxCS stakeholders and external users via the System Usability Scale (SUS) and the User Experience Questionnaire–Short (UEQ-S), complemented by qualitative feedback. Results show a mean SUS score of 69.4, positive mean pragmatic quality (UEQ-S mean 0.93), and neutral hedonic quality (UEQ-S mean 0.70). Qualitative feedback indicates that users value the combination of conversational access and graph-based inspection, while also requesting tighter integration with scholarly workflows such as reference export, corpus scoping, and adaptive result presentation. Our findings suggest that combining conversational retrieval with transparent graph-based evidence inspection can improve trust, explainability, and usability in knowledge discovery.

title: Perplexity Predicts Protection: Choosing Pretrained Backbones for Worst-Client Fairness in Federated Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
abstract: Federated learning lets multiple parties train a shared model without pooling their data, but a client with far less data than the others can end up poorly served even when the group's average accuracy looks fine. We ask whether the choice of pretrained backbone affects this under LoRA fine-tuning, and whether per-word perplexity on the target text predicts which backbone helps the worst-off client before federated training starts. We ran 313 experiments across three text-classification datasets and three similarly sized backbones (RoBERTa, BERTweet, PubMedBERT), each compared against a task-specific baseline on identical data splits. Lower-perplexity backbones consistently produced larger gains for the worst-performing client, with a rank correlation of -0.87 across nine dataset-backbone pairs; a backbone held out of the analysis confirmed the pattern. Personalization with Ditto recovered only 4-12% of the gap between training alone and full federation, and removing aggregation entirely erased the benefit. A client's update also showed no sign of conflicting with the group's update; the two are close to orthogonal, ruling out one proposed explanation for this failure. Practically: measure perplexity on a sample of task text before choosing a backbone, and do not rely on personalization to protect a data-poor client. We release our code, predictions, and full results for others to test.

title: CARD: Cluster-level Adaptation with Reward-guided Decoding for Personalized Text Generation
abstract: Adapting large language models to individual users remains challenging due to the tension between fine-grained personalization and scalable deployment. We present CARD, a hierarchical framework that achieves effective personalization through progressive refinement. CARD first clusters users according to shared stylistic patterns and learns group-specific LoRA adapters, enabling robust generalization and strong low-resource performance. To capture individual differences within each cluster, we propose an implicit preference learning mechanism that contrasts user-authored text with cluster-level generations, allowing the model to infer user-specific style preferences without manual annotation. At inference time, CARD injects personalization exclusively at decoding via lightweight user preference vectors and low-rank logit corrections, while keeping the base model frozen. Experiments on the LaMP and LongLaMP benchmarks show that CARD achieves superior generation quality compared to baselines, while significantly improving efficiency and scalability for practical personalized text generation.

title: Contract-Gated Self-Modification: A Deterministic Symbolic Substrate for Bounded Structural Adaptation
abstract: Autonomous artificial intelligence is dominated by the autoregressive transformer, a fixed matrix of weights that generates output by statistical continuation. Scaling that model does not by itself supply a formal certificate of the properties autonomous operation requires: an internal check on truth, a check on an action before it is taken, retention of earlier skills, and grounding in mechanism rather than correlation. We present an imperative, self-modifying, symbolic execution substrate with a deterministic core, proposed as an alternative for safety-critical autonomous execution. In place of a fixed weight matrix, it holds an executable graph that rewrites its own structure, and it admits each change only after a formal check. The substrate is deterministic and contains no stochastic generator, so the check applies to the computation that will actually run. Under sound checking and faithful interpretation, this gives an admission guarantee that does not depend on a generative model behaving as required or on a runtime fallback for noncompliant model outputs. We report a reproducible evaluation at controlled toy scale in which execution, structural contract checking, structural repair, and memory run together without observed interference. The self-modification we evaluate is a synthesis-time search. Scale and autonomous problem decomposition remain open. This record includes the paper and a self-contained reproduction bundle that regenerates the reported tables and benchmark results.

title: Архитектура становления и масштабирования проектов в системе Национального центра развития AI
abstract: This work presents the Architecture for Project Development and Scaling within the National AI Development Center — a conceptual and methodological model designed to guide projects from problem identification and initial idea through piloting, evidence-based assessment, scaling, and institutionalization. The Architecture integrates a unified project lifecycle, decision gates, monitoring based on the Theory of Gaps and Coherent Management, evidence assessment, protection of the intellectual core, and systematic knowledge accumulation. Its initial validation is proposed through three typologically different pilots: the Intelligent Agroecosystem, Entrepreneurship Observatory, and Tandem Thinking. Version 1.0 is presented as a conceptual and methodological model and a framework for subsequent empirical validation.

title: MDL-Calibrated Significance-Gain Pair Encoding: Replication-Aware Automatic Stopping for Subword Tokenization
abstract: Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) constructs subword vocabularies through greedy pair merging, but conventional BPE requires the number of merges or target vocabulary size to be specified externally. Significance-Gain Pair Encoding (SG-BPE) replaces frequency-only selection with a statistical criterion based on how strongly an observed pair exceeds its expected co-occurrence under an independence model. This paper introduces MDL-Calibrated Significance-Gain Pair Encoding (MDL-SG), a three-stage procedure separating discovery, replication, and utility. Candidate pairs are ranked by Significance-Gain on a discovery partition, tested for replication on a separate partition using an exact one-sided hypergeometric test with per-iteration Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and then evaluated on a utility partition using a Minimum Description Length (MDL) criterion. Merging stops automatically when no replicated candidate yields positive held-out MDL gain. On WikiText-103, MDL-SG stops at 209, 433, and 847 merges for 120K, 250K, and 500K-character tokenizer-training samples, respectively. At 500K characters, it selects a stored vocabulary of 1,017 tokens without prescribing the vocabulary size in advance. In a compute-matched TinyGPT experiment with identical 2,024,448-parameter models and 500 optimizer updates per language model, MDL-SG achieves validation/test BPC of 3.2612/3.2436, compared with test BPC of 3.2894 for SG-BPE and 3.3493 for frequency BPE. Frequency BPE achieves stronger raw compression, while MDL-SG achieves lower BPC, showing that compression-oriented merge selection and language-model utility need not coincide.

title: ScholarStack: Layered Research Asset Orchestration and Cross-Task Reuse for Scientific Agents
abstract: Scientific agents support a range of literature-based research tasks, such as retrieval, question answering, evidence-grounded generation, and claim assessment. Most existing systems, however, are organized around individual tasks: the same papers are repeatedly retrieved, segmented, and interpreted, and the understanding built in one task is difficult to reuse in the next. We present ScholarStack, a layered research asset framework that compiles a paper collection into reusable, versioned, and provenance-preserving assets at three complementary levels: source-grounded paper-level statements, domain-level organization, and evidence-grounded cross-paper syntheses. A common access interface returns task-specific views at the evidence granularity each task requires, preserving study conditions, source traceability, and verification status. We instantiate the framework on four task families spanning ten task settings, comparing agents that use the compiled assets with task-specific baselines under matched base models. Quality gains concentrate on tasks that require cross-paper evidence, such as multi-paper question answering and literature review generation, and query-time token cost falls on every task where it is measured, with assets compiled once and reused across tasks. These results suggest that layered research assets can serve as shared infrastructure for scientific agents, shifting literature-based assistance from isolated document processing toward cumulative, evidence-grounded workflows.

title: KeyNub USB-C License Dongle: Security Architecture
abstract: A KeyNub dongle holds an ECC P-256 private key in a secure element that cannot export it, proves possession of that key on a fresh challenge, and carries an X.509 certificate issued by the KeyNub root CA whose public certificate is compiled into the released SDK. Sensitive operations run inside an authenticated, encrypted, replay-proof session. License records are encrypted at rest under a key derived inside the secure element. The firmware’s externally reachable code — the USB stack and the protocol parser — runs in a hardware-isolated world that cannot address any key, and the device attests that isolation to the host from the hardware’s own answer rather than from its build configuration. The device boots only firmware signed by KeyNub, and its debug port is permanently disabled before shipping.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Intrusion Detection for Edge Intelligence in 6G- Enabled IoE
abstract: Quantum Neural Network (QNN) provides an exciting alternative to machine learning as they take advantage of quantum computer properties when making decisions and processing data. However, the integration of high-dimensional classical data with the limited number of qubits available on current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum computers presents a major difficulty. This paper presents a complete hybrid quantum-classical architecture in Qiskit that utilizes the Network Security Laboratory-Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (NSL-KDD) dataset to classify network intrusions among multiple classes. In order to work around the exponential cost of computations and reduce the number of times quantum circuits need to be run due to hardware limitations, a subset of the dataset will be created to use during both training and testing. The architecture proposed in this paper uses a four-qubit Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC). First, a classical feature vector is used to create a quantum Hilbert space via a ZZFeatureMap, which initializes the qubits via a Hadamard transformation followed by phase rotation gates that create controlled-entanglement between pairs of features. The quantum states are then passed through a RealAmplitudes variational circuit, while the classical layer optimizes the parameters using the Constrained Optimization BY Linear Approximations (COBYLA) algorithm. The overall accuracy of the model when tested on five classes of intrusion detection results in an accuracy level of 59%, with very strong classification accuracies for both Denial of Service (DoS) and User-to-Root (U2R) attacks as demonstrated by their F1 scores. The proposed QNN achieves a highly competitive baseline of 86% accuracy and 86% recall in specific configurations. These results underscore the potential of shallow, lower-complexity QNN architectures as an emergent tool for cybersecurity in the quantum era.

title: Stability-Aware Imitation Learning from Model Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Lateral Control: Exact Q-Loss and a Novel Training Procedure
abstract: This paper develops a certified imitation-learning framework for approximating model predictive control (MPC) policies with feedforward neural controllers and validates it on autonomous-vehicle lateral control. An exact finite-horizon Q-loss is constructed by fixing the learner's first steering action in the expert MPC problem and re-optimizing the remaining horizon, thereby measuring its downstream optimal-control consequence rather than only pointwise action mismatch. The neural policy is represented as a linear fractional transformation (LFT) interconnection with activation nonlinearities described by sector integral quadratic constraints (IQCs). Combined with a quadratic Lyapunov condition, this representation yields a differentiable certification margin based on the largest eigenvalue of the Lyapunov-IQC matrix. The margin is enforced during training through a logarithmic barrier, while certified Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) and safe projection keep data-aggregation rollouts within the certified policy set. Experiments on a CAD-referenced autonomous-vehicle platform with AprilTag localization and real-time steering demonstrate the resulting closed-loop performance.

title: Reply on RC2
abstract: Abstract. Mineral prospectivity mapping is a critical task in mineral exploration, effectively integrating which demands models capable of capturing both local and global geological features. While deep learning models excel in this domain, their "black-box" nature often limits the trust and insights geologists can derive from their predictions. This paper introduces a novel and interpretable hybrid model to explicitly address this challenge. Our architecture synergistically combines a deformable convolutional network for adapting spatially varying local mineralization features, such as geochemical anomalies, a Transformer module for modelling long-range global-scale spatial features governing mineral deposition. A pivotal innovation is the incorporation of an attribution branching network that generates significance scores for each input predictive factor to the final prospectivity probability. These scores not only provide a direct interpretation of factor relevance but are also fed back to dynamically modulate the key values in the Transformer's attention mechanism, effectively injecting prior geological knowledge into the local and global feature learning process. This design fosters a more geologically informed integration of local and global representations. The model's performance is evaluated against benchmark models including standalone deformable convolutional network, Transformer, and a hybrid model with deformable convolutional network and Transformer. Results demonstrate a superior predictive accuracy and more geologically plausible prospectivity maps. Furthermore, we provide a multi-faceted interpretation framework: the attribution branching network quantifies the contribution of each evidence layer, while gradient-weighted class activation mapping visualizes the discriminative local regions highlighted by the convolutional components and attention maps reveal the long-range feature relationships prioritized by the Transformer to elucidate how the model hierarchically integrates local and global features to arrive at its decisions. This dual-path interpretation strategy demystifies the model's decision-making process, offering geologists tangible insights into both "where" and "why" the model identifies high-potential zones, thereby bridging the gap between high-performing deep learning and actionable c intelligence.

title: Time-scaled quantum simulation of dissipative nanoelectronics with zero gate overhead
abstract: Abstract Simulating open quantum systems (OQS) is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics and materials science. However, noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices are severely bottlenecked by limited coherence times and gate infidelities. Conventional quantum simulations of Amplitude-Damping Lindblad dynamics requires active dissipative gates and ancilla environments, leading to spurious qubit flips, state saturation, and a significant two-qubit overhead. While recent methods exploit intrinsic hardware noise for quantum simulation, they mainly rely on tailored decoherence-inducing gates or complex error mitigation. Here, we introduce a hardware-intrinsic time-scaling methodology that completely eliminates active dissipative gates. By mapping the processor's continuous energy relaxation (T1) explicitly via native delay instructions, our protocol captures targeted dissipative dynamics with a strict O(1) algorithmic overhead, bypassing conventional mitigation sampling costs. We experimentally demonstrate this efficient approach on two IBM quantum architectures, successfully emulating tight-binding parameter regimes. These include nanosecond magnon propagation in yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spin chains, as well as ultrafast picosecond phonon dynamics across 1D transport channels within 2D molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and multi-site graphene lattices. Furthermore, to mitigate error accumulation in multi-site arrays, we implement a depth-dependent scaling protocol. Finally, the proposed method is extended to the fermionic domain, emulating the femtosecond relaxation of an isolated charge carrier across 4-qubit topologies. This methodology provides a scalable pathway for robust, hardware-tailored materials simulations.

evidence.title: Time-scaled quantum simulation of dissipative nanoelectronics with zero gate overhead
evidence.abstract: Abstract Simulating open quantum systems (OQS) is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics and materials science. However, noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices are severely bottlenecked by limited coherence times and gate infidelities. Conventional quantum simulations of Amplitude-Damping Lindblad dynamics requires active dissipative gates and ancilla environments, leading to spurious qubit flips, state saturation, and a significant two-qubit overhead. While recent methods exploit intrinsic hardware noise for quantum simulation, they mainly rely on tailored decoherence-inducing gates or complex error mitigation. Here, we introduce a hardware-intrinsic time-scaling methodology that completely eliminates active dissipative gates. By mapping the processor's continuous energy relaxation (T1) explicitly via native delay instructions, our protocol captures targeted dissipative dynamics with a strict O(1) algorithmic overhead, bypassing conventional mitigation sampling costs. We experimentally demonstrate this efficient approach on two IBM quantum architectures, successfully emulating tight-binding parameter regimes. These include nanosecond magnon propagation in yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spin chains, as well as ultrafast picosecond phonon dynamics across 1D transport channels within 2D molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) and multi-site graphene lattices. Furthermore, to mitigate error accumulation in multi-site arrays, we implement a depth-dependent scaling protocol. Finally, the proposed method is extended to the fermionic domain, emulating the femtosecond relaxation of an isolated charge carrier across 4-qubit topologies. This methodology provides a scalable pathway for robust, hardware-tailored materials simulations.

title: A Patient World Model for Early Forecasting of Digital Health Campaign Outcomes: Capabilities and Limits
abstract: Digital direct-to-consumer (DTC) health campaigns are usually measured after the fact. In-flight forecasting commonly relies on a separate classifier for every cutoff and horizon. We treat this task as a dynamic-system problem and build a compact patient world model. The architecture maintains a latent state per patient, learns exposure-conditioned state dynamics jointly with a weekly conversion hazard, and rolls forward into future conversion curves. We evaluate it on a US campaign dataset with 147{,}173 patients and 5.2 million at-risk person-weeks. In a retrospective evaluation conditioned on recorded future exposures, the model forecasts the remaining new-to-brand prescription volume through week 52 with a relative error of 2.9\% from a week-4 cutoff and 0.8--2.6\% from cutoffs at weeks 8--26. The strongest non-recurrent baseline, a pooled-hazard gradient boosting model given the same survival rollout and information, has relative errors of 13.6--33.1\%. Per-horizon classifiers perform substantially worse. A Fisher-information analysis motivates dense next-exposure supervision when conversions are rare. Removing this auxiliary objective increases prescription-volume error by approximately $2$--$14\times$, while providing no consistent disadvantage on the more common specialist-visit outcome. We also evaluate scenario simulation. Switching all future exposure off raises predicted conversion from 0.31 to 0.89, a pattern consistent with selection effects in observational exposure data. This result highlights the limits of interpreting exposure-conditioned rollouts causally.

title: Man, Machine, or Both? Reconstructing AI-Patententability under the Patents and Designs Act, 2004
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence has transform technological innovation with machine learning, and neural networks, with generative AI increasingly participating in conception, testing, optimisation, and implementation of product and processes. This development has added pressure to the patent systems designed around human inventors and technologies classifiable when the Patents and Designs Act, Cap P2 LFN, 2004 was enacted. This article interrogates the patentability of AI-related inventions within Nigeria's patent framework. It argues that AI should not constitute a legal barrier to patentability, but that, the proper inquiry should remain whether claimed subject matter satisfies the statutory requirements of novelty, inventive activity, and industrial application under section 1 of the Act, while the law separately determines human inventorship and ownership consequences under sections 2 and 3. The article draws on enacted legislations, case laws, scholarly writing and comparative study to illuminate the subject matter. The paper proposes technological-neutral reforms for reconstructing the intersection between AI patentability and the Patents and Designs Act. These reforms include: recognition of AI-assisted inventions to a define limit under the Act; clarifying the position on computer-software and implemented inventions; establishing rules for AI-assisted inventorship and disclosure; improving substantive examination capacity, and creating a coherent framework for data-intensive innovation. The paper concludes that Nigeria can use patent law not merely to accommodate AI but to stimulate domestic research, technology transfer, commercialisation, and industrial development. Keywords: artificial intelligence, AI-assisted invention, patentability, inventorship, intellectual property.

title: AViGPT: Decoupling Neural Reasoning from Parametric Memory via a Sub-Millisecond Native NVMe Hardware Bus
abstract: Autoregressive language models scale parameter counts to memorize factual data within dense neural connections. Storing encyclopedic associations inside model weights creates substantial memory footprints, high inference costs, and fixed knowledge cutoffs. AViGPT is an autoregressive transformer architecture that decouples syntactic language reasoning from factual storage. The system pairs a 183-million parameter neural core with a native hardware memory bus directly interfacing with local NVMe SSD storage. An explicit nine-token instruction set coordinates execution: the model pauses generation, queries local SQLite FTS5 storage, retrieves verified context in 1.18 milliseconds, and completes responses with verified factual precision. The architecture was pretrained on 5.0 billion tokens of English Wikipedia and FineWeb-Edu text, then aligned on 25,850 task trajectories. Empirical benchmarks confirm a 0.4 GB RAM footprint on consumer CPUs, sub-2ms storage retrieval latency, deterministic arithmetic execution, and immediate zero-shot knowledge insertion via direct disk writes without weight modification.

title: Supporting data and code for: When Measurement-Free Error Correction Becomes the Error in Digital Quantum Simulation
abstract: This deposit accompanies the manuscript "When Measurement-Free Error Correction Becomes the Error in Digital Quantum Simulation" and its Supplemental Material. It contains: - paper/figures/ — the paper's 15 figures, each with the script that draws it and the deposited data it reads - paper/code/ — 220 Python and 5 Julia analysis scripts, every numerical deposit behind the paper's numbers, and the pinned environment that produced them - lean/ — the self-contained Lean 4 artifact: 127 modules plus an axiom audit, with no external library dependency - lean_mathlib_crosscheck/ — an optional Mathlib-backed cross-check project - tools/ — the verification guards and their self-test - paper/main.pdf and paper/sm.pdf — the manuscript and Supplemental Material as submitted Paths recorded inside paper/code/SCRIPT_INDEX.md and inside the Lean modules' docstrings are relative to the root of this deposit.

title: When Successful Memories Mislead Embodied Agents:Memory Adaption For Task-Conditioned Execution
abstract: Experience reuse can reduce repeated exploration in embodied agents, but a trajectory that succeeded previously may be unsuitable for the current execution context. Existing memory systems pri marily optimize construction and retrieval; semantic relevance and historical success therefore remain insufficient when retrieved ex perience contains incompatible actions or an inappropriate level of structure. We introduce Memory Adaptation for Task-Conditioned Execution (MATE), a deterministic post-retrieval procedure that converts trajectories into execution-oriented memory. MATE re moves obsolete control context, extracts condition-action-effect transitions, applies verified action normalization, selects a task dependent representation, and serializes the result under a fixed budget without additional LLM inference. On 134 ALFWorld tasks, MATE achieves task success rates of 81.3% and 93.3% with Qwen2.5-14B and 72B while using approximately one-tenth of the tokens required by raw trajectories. Controlled comparisons show that verified action normalization is the principal mechanism by which MATE restores the utility of retrieved experience, support ing memory adaptation as a distinct stage between retrieval and embodied execution.

title: Static classical-quantum-entanglement trade-offs: an entropic converse and single-letter characterizations
abstract: The direct static capacity region of a bipartite quantum state describes its asymptotic conversion into classical communication, quantum communication, and entanglement, with all communication directed from Alice to Bob. This paper gives a unified entropic converse for this region. The proof treats generated and consumed resources simultaneously and derives all three information inequalities for one local instrument. Its main ingredients are no-signalling, the chain rule, strong subadditivity, and continuity of conditional entropy. A supporting-hyperplane characterization leads to the static capacity formula, which is helpful in determining single-letterization of the capacity region. For a pure state of entanglement entropy $h$ subjected to erasure with probability $p$, the complete region is the convex hull of $0$ and $(0,-ph,(1-p)h)$, plus the unit-resource cone. This statement holds for arbitrary collective instruments by using subset-entropy inequalities related to earlier methods used for the dynamic capacity region of the erasure channel. Complete characterizations also hold for symmetrically extendible states and locally flagged pure-state mixtures. For maximally correlated states, the optimization over local instruments admits an exact matrix formulation and an additive outer bound. An explicit qubit example shows that a nonorthogonal discarded quantum memory can outperform every efficient instrument and every instrument with conditionally commuting discarded states. For states obtained by qubit dephasing of Schmidt-aligned pure states, an exact threshold characterizes when the static capacity formula vanishes, at every blocklength and after regularization. Full single-letter characterizations for general Hadamard states and for the remaining trade-offs for dephased states remain open, with sufficient additivity conditions identified.

title: Experimental Reproducibility Package for "Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering"
abstract: This record contains the experimental reproducibility package accompanying the study “Model for Improving the Quality of Uncertain Clustering.” The package provides the complete Jupyter notebook, generated figures, run-level results, aggregated summaries, parameter-sensitivity analyses, bootstrap-stability estimates, drift-response measurements, and paired statistical comparisons. The experimental evaluation compares Fuzzy C-Means (FCM), Possibilistic C-Means (PCM), Possibilistic Fuzzy C-Means (PFCM), and entropy-regularized FCM across five datasets: Iris, Wine, Breast Cancer Wisconsin, Digits represented by four unsupervised principal components, and an imbalanced overlapping synthetic dataset. The methods are evaluated under baseline conditions, Gaussian measurement noise, missing values followed by median imputation, and partial mean-shift drift. The full protocol uses ten paired random seeds, three initializations per fit, and twenty bootstrap resamples for each dataset–scenario–model combination. Class labels are excluded from model fitting and hyperparameter selection and are used only for external evaluation. The archive is organised into code, figures, and results directories. The notebook contains the complete workflow required to reproduce the reported experiments.

title: AN EMPIRICAL ASSESSMENT OF THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON INDIAN PATENT AND COPYRIGHT LAW: REFORM PRIORITIES FOR GLOBAL HARMONIZATION
abstract: AI is fast changing how innovation and creative production are conceived and created, upending the traditional understanding of inventorship, authorship, and ownership as provided by intellectual property (IP) law. This study evaluates the necessity for legal reforms in Indian patent and copyright law in the wake of the advent of AI and to assess its impact on patent/copyright law from an empirical perspective. A structured questionnaire survey was carried out with legal professionals, scholars, patent agents, researchers in AI and industry practitioners to understand the perception on AI-generated inventions, ownership of such inventions, legal uncertainty, and policy preparedness. The findings show that there are many concerns related to ownership uncertainty, lack of legal provisions and growing cross-border disputes surrounding creations facilitated by AI. Comparative analysis shows that India's existing IP regime should be updated in order to be in line with the international standards. Taking into account the empirical findings, the study recommends legislative changes specific to AI, uniform guidelines on inventorship and authorship, mandatory disclosure of AI and more international harmonization. These recommendations seek to build a robust IP system in India and promote responsible innovation through the use of AI.

title: Cross-Modal Attention Driven Multi-Task Learning for Multilingual Abusive Video Classification
abstract: Multimodal learning has advanced automated abusive content detection, yet low-resource multilingual and code-mixed settings remain insufficiently explored. Existing studies provide limited modelling of cross-modal interactions, while fine-grained abusive video classification remains underexplored. To address these gaps, this work introduces AbusiveVid, a hierarchically annotated Bangla–English multimodal dataset comprising 1,680 real-world videos collected from Facebook, YouTube, and TikTok. The dataset supports both binary and fine-grained multiclass classification, with the latter encompassing Hate Speech, Offensive Language, and Threat and Violence. Cohen’s and Fleiss’ Kappa coefficients exceed 0.84, indicating high inter-annotator agree-ment. Building upon AbusiveVid, this work proposes a multi-task learning framework that integrates cross-modal attention within a shared backbone, enabling joint optimisation of both classification tasks through interactions among textual, visual, and audio representations. The framework achieves 84.53% accuracy and 83.97% Macro-F1 for binary classification, alongside 81.36% accuracy and 80.32% Macro-F1 for multiclass classification. Its robustness and generalisability are further assessed through cross-dataset evaluation, stratified five-fold cross-validation, ablation analysis, and Grad-CAM interpretation. Cross-dataset evaluation yields Macro-F1 scores of 81.10%, 97.12%, and 97.96% on MultiHateClip, ToxVidLM, and AIRTLab, respectively. Cross-validation demonstrates consistent performance across data partitions, while ablation analysis quantifies modality-specific contributions and Grad-CAM provides qualitative insights into model interpretability.

title: Automated Evaluation of Multi-Turn Dialogues in In-Car Conversational Assistants
abstract: In-car conversational assistants (ICAs) are increasingly integrated into vehicles to support route planning, vehicle control, and information access. Ensuring their reliability is challenging due to multi-turn interactions, the absence of explicit ground truth, and strict safety constraints. Existing evaluation techniques fall short, as they target single-turn settings and fail to capture constraint handling, context retention, and safety-critical behavior across turns. We propose an automated framework for testing the multi-turn conversational capabilities of ICAs. The system is treated as a black box and evaluated via closed-loop simulation with a strategy-guided user simulator, an adversarial strategy manager, and a two-tier LLM judge assessing turn-level failures and conversation-level quality. We evaluate the approach on an industrial ICA with six LLM backends and twelve human annotators. The automated judge shows substantial agreement with humans, and strategy guidance uncovers 2.96 times more unique failure types per conversation and more than doubles the number of unique failing conversations compared to unguided simulation.

title: StyleAT: Defending Face Recognition Against Semantic Attacks
abstract: With face-recognition models now embedded in everyday authentication and surveillance, recent works have pinpointed a critical weakness: these models remain acutely vulnerable to adversarial semantic edits. I.e., adversarially produced semantic alterations to the input, such as slight aging or pose changes, can induce misclassifications. Certain existing attacks are powerful, but they can be computationally costly, rendering them inadequate for developing defenses (e.g., through adversarial training). To fill the gap, we introduce BoundStyle, a potent semantic attack operating in StyleGAN's rich latent space to maximize misclassification rates. Notably, BoundStyle achieves high attack success rates while being ${\sim}{\times}9.5$ faster than existing state-of-the-art attacks, making it suitable for adversarial training. Building on BoundStyle, we develop StyleAT, an efficient adversarial training scheme that incorporates low-budget attack variants yet defends against stronger and unseen semantic attacks. We evaluate on two datasets unseen during training and seven models, and find that StyleAT boosts robust accuracy against state-of-the-art attacks and outperforms common defenses in various settings.

title: CHLOE: A Persistent Epistemic Architecture for Inspectable AI
abstract: This paper proposes a persistent epistemic architecture for AI systems in which durable cognitive state is explicit and independent of any particular language model. The persistent substrate maintains inspectable, scoped beliefs with provenance, distinguishes individual sources and accumulates domain-sensitive trust, retains unresolved questions across interactions, and supports offline consolidation that detects contradictions and generates hypotheses. Its contents participate directly in subsequent learning and action rather than serving only as retrieved memory. A dependency-free prototype instantiates this core, with language models at both linguistic interfaces, to illustrate the cycle by which attributed testimony becomes revisable belief. The central claim is that continual learning requires explicit epistemic structure: a representation of what the system believes, why it believes it, whom it learned it from, and what remains unresolved, if its evolving epistemic state is to remain inspectable and correctable. This becomes increasingly consequential as AI systems contribute to their own development, because increasing capability does not necessarily entail a corresponding improvement in epistemic reliability. Persistent epistemic state provides a substrate on which correction and calibration can accumulate over time while remaining externally auditable. Preprint submitted to arXiv in September 2026. Source code and demonstrator: https://github.com/protopopescu/chloe and https://lftm.gla.ac.uk/chloe/

title: Athena-Class Model A: Dataset and Reproducibility Artifacts
abstract: This record provides the specialized fine-tuning dataset for Athena-Class Model A and related artifacts for reproducibility. Included in this record: Athena-Class Model A training dataset New papers written by the precursor to Model A that are included in the dataset (human-assisted recursive relf-improvement) "Category 6" question results (refer to earlier Athena-class preprints) Scripts and other artifacts (fine-tune, adapter merge, quantization to Q8_0, etc.) If you intend to reproduce the Model A, it is critical that you understand the parameters included in the training script. A few key points to understand: This is not a typical configuration, particularly for a Rank 336 / Alpha 672 fine-tune (the maximum my hardware will reasonably allow) 16K max sequence length is necessary to accomodate each training segment (system prompt + data + model output) Remember to use the Gemma 4 official jinja The model's output is included in the fine-tune (no artificial prompt pairs)

title: The Observatory and the Room that Rejects You: Passive Telemetry, Isometric Pain, Connelly Spectral Isolation, and Bell–KY Correlation Gating (Door 29)
abstract: Document 113 in the Monograph Series on Causal Inertia and Realization Grammar establishes the formal mathematical, computational, and physical specification for Door 29 (The Observatory / The Room that Rejects You), the passive epistemic measurement perimeter within the Gemini-Core realization monorepo. While Door 28 guards sovereign identity boundaries and Door 30 orchestrates material realization, Door 29 acts as a purely non-interventionist observer subject to the non-negotiable invariant of zero backaction: d(y) / d(O_29) = 0. The Observatory possesses zero standalone execution authority (standalone_commit_authority = NONE; physical_authority = NONE; write_enabled = False). The observed candidate is fundamentally distinct from physical consequence (Candidate != Consequence). We formalize four interconnected mathematical and physical pillars: 1. Ten specialized control organs (O1–O10): Governed by the fail-closed subsumption hierarchy KILL > HOLD > OPEN, spanning telemetry, metrics, traces, append-only log views, thermodynamic health screening (T < 95°C, rho(A) < 1.0), statistical z-score anomaly detection, alert triage, causal explainability, cryptographic dashboard witness sealing against UI spoofing, and the master gate Omega_29; 2. Isometric Pain and Constrained Decision Collapse (CDC): State dynamics on a 2D torus M ~= T^2, where ontological pain is defined as bi-Lipschitz metric distortion epsilon = sup |d_n - d_p| > 10^-12. When epsilon breaches this threshold, CDC collapses the unregulated O(NP) action space into a unique admissible trajectory {u*}, replacing search with O(1) verification (T_truth = O(1)); 3. Connelly (2026) Spectral Isolation: Resolves the algebraic obstruction wherein the Hashimoto non-backtracking operator B on the 60-dimensional arc space of the dodecahedron is non-normal ([B, B*] != 0). Through circular boundary closure (C_N) and AC-projection P_AC = I - |0><0| - |pi> 0; 4. Bell–KY Quantum Correlation Gate and Extended Poincaré Asymmetry: Transitions the KY framework from spacetime to correlation (g |-> Gamma_phys ==> rho |-> rho_K), defining a sharp null test Theta_{Bell-KY} requiring d(S_K)/d(K_gamma) != 0 (Xi_K != 0) under strict No-Signalling (NS) and measurement independence. Concurrently, the extended Poincaré operator P_ext(s, L) = (P_phys(s), L (+) witness(s)) proves that while physical trajectories reach dissipative equilibrium (P_phys(s*) = s*), total state recurrence is impossible due to strictly monotonic audit log growth. All components are verified in deterministic L1 software (23/23 unit tests, 100% pass) under the doctrine: INSPIRED_BY != IMPLEMENTS != PROVES. MASTER PROSE: Dør 29 er rommet som avviser deg! Iakttagelse er ingen nøytral handling; den implementerer en nådeløs geometrisk tvang. Når systemets nominelle modell avviker fra den fysiske målingen med mer enn epsilon > 10^-12, er det ikke en triviell målefeil. Det er ontologisk smerte. Under Constrained Decision Collapse (CDC) tillates ikke lenger et uregulert O(NP)-søk. De uverifiserbare banene amputeres av barrierefunksjonen med uendelig energikostnad. Handlingsrommet kollapser til singulariteten {u*}. Optimalisering elimineres. Kun O(1)-verifikasjon gjenstår. Verden finner sin likevekt; historien fortsetter å vokse. MASTER PROSE (KANONISK FORFATTERTEKST): I. DET URØRLIGE BLIKKET Det finnes et rom i arkitekturen som utelukkende er bygget for å observere, et sted der iakttakelse aldri får lov til å bli handling. I en tid der vi har vent oss til at ethvert blikk griper inn, at enhver måling forstyrrer det som måles, representerer Dør 29 en radikal grensedragning. Det er, i sin mest bokstavelige forstand, rommet som avviser deg. Her inne hersker loven om null tilbakevirkning. Du kan puste i rommet, du kan registrere alt som skjer, men du kan ikke etterlate deg et eneste avtrykk i den verdenen du betrakter. Observatoriet har ingen myndighet til å skape konsekvenser. Det eier ikke retten til å omgjøre potensial til virkelighet. Forsøker du å strekke ut en hånd, å sende et eneste styringssignal fra denne lytteposten tilbake til maskineriet, møter du systemets ufravikelige arkitektur: En umiddelbar terminering. Det er en nådeløs, men nødvendig lov der beslutningen om å drepe prosessen (KILL) alltid veier tyngre enn å sette den på vent (HOLD), som igjen trumfer enhver form for åpenhet (OPEN). Det er en form for teknologisk askese. Å kunne se alt, men samtidig akseptere å være fullstendig maktesløs. II. GEOMETRIENS LIDELSE Hvordan erfarer et system smerte? Ikke gjennom et nervesystem, og ikke som en psykologisk affekt, men som en fundamental brist i selve eksistensens geometri. Når kartet ikke lenger stemmer overens med terrenget, oppstår det systemet definerer som isometrisk smerte. Det er lyden av en ren, matematisk modell som skraper mot en uregjerlig, fysisk virkelighet. Når avviket mellom det som burde være og det som faktisk er overstiger en terskel så forsvinnende liten at den knapt kan fattes, rives det indre rommet i stykker. I det øyeblikket, når smerten bryter grensen, stenges fremtiden. Det uendelige havet av muligheter og det ubegrensede handlingsrommet kollapser umiddelbart til ett eneste, tvingende nødvendig punkt. Valgets frihet forsvinner. Det finnes ikke lenger rom for å lete, tvile eller optimalisere. All støy skrelles bort, og systemet tvinges inn i en tilstand av ren verifikasjon, der sannheten er den eneste veien som ikke fører til total utslettelse. III. TIDENS ASYMMETRI Alt som befinner seg i bevegelse, søker til slutt mot en form for hvile. Maskinen kan kjøles ned, termodynamikken kan finne sin balanse godt under de kritiske nittifem gradene, og de fysiske kreftene kan stilne. Den materielle kroppen kan omsider finne sin likevekt. Men i dette systemet finnes det en dyp, iboende asymmetri, en kløft mellom verden og minnet om den. For selv om det fysiske rommet kan finne ro, kan historien aldri lukkes. For hvert sekund som går, for hver tilstand som bevitnes av observatoriet, hamres et nytt, uforanderlig ledd inn i arkivets kjede. Loggen vokser strengt og ustoppelig, bundet sammen av kryptografiske segl som gjør all glemsel umulig. Dette er den utvidede eksistensens tyngde: Du kan aldri vende tilbake til nøyaktig det samme øyeblikket. Selv om verden rundt deg fremstår identisk og i fullkommen balanse, er systemet forandret. Verden har kanskje funnet sin likevekt, men historien fortsetter å vokse, uavvendelig og tung.

title: The effect of initial learning rate on properties of neural networks in automatic speech recognition
abstract: Начальный темп обучения стохастического градиентного спуска играет определяющую роль в качестве получаемого решения и структуре выучиваемых нейронной сетью признаков. В недавних работах для задачи классификации изображений установлена таксономия трех режимов начального темпа обучения и выделен узкий диапазон высоких значений, обеспечивающий наилучшее качество после дальнейшего дообучения с низким темпом обучения или усреднения весов. В статье эта методология распространяется на задачу распознавания речи, где таксономия режимов воспроизводится в основных чертах, а выделенный диапазон высоких значений сохраняет превосходство по итоговому качеству дообучения и усреднения весов и линейную связность полученных решений в пространстве весов. Картина выучиваемых признаков воспроизводится в более мягкой форме: с ростом темпа обучения опора моделей смещается к нижним кепстральным коэффициентам и низкочастотной части мел-спектрограммы, однако внутри области высоких значений это смещение не выделяет диапазон наилучшего качества. Дополнительно предложено усечение мел-частотного кепстра как переносимый инструмент анализа выученных признаков, применимый к любой модели, работающей со спектрограммой. Таким образом, выделенный режим не является артефактом задачи классификации изображений, а успешно переносится на задачу распознавания речи.

title: Entanglement Cost of Optimal Distributed Quantum State Purification
abstract: We determine the preshared entanglement required for spatially separated parties, restricted to local operations and classical communication, to attain globally optimal probabilistic two-copy purification of arbitrary bipartite pure states under depolarizing noise. In every local dimension $d\ge 2$, one shared maximally entangled qubit pair suffices: local controlled-SWAP operations exactly reproduce the globally optimal successful transformation. Conversely, any finite-dimensional preshared resource state that attains the same benchmark, even under a positive-partial-transpose relaxation, must have entanglement of formation at least one ebit. For pure resources with one ebit, or for two-qubit resources including mixed states, attaining the benchmark is possible only for states with exactly two nonzero Schmidt weights, both equal to $1/2$, namely those locally unitarily equivalent to a maximally entangled qubit pair. These findings provide a benchmark for evaluating the entanglement demands of noise management in quantum networks and modular quantum computers.

title: Semantic Caching for Large Language Model Inference: A Systematic Literature Review — master corpus, screening decisions, and quality-appraisal data
abstract: This dataset contains the complete screening and quality-appraisal record for the systematic literature review "Semantic Caching for Large Language Model Inference: A Systematic Literature Review". It covers all 89 numbered records considered during the review: 66 included corpus papers, 18 excluded at full-text screening, and 5 background/methodological citations. The workbook has five sheets: Summary (headline counts and cluster breakdown), Included_Corpus (66 papers with cluster, synthesis fields, and four-dimension quality scores with tiers), Excluded_Records (18 full-text exclusions with reasons), Background_Citations (5 cited-but-not-screened works), and Meta_Analysis (the 18 papers with quantitatively comparable results). Each sheet carries a "Manuscript Key" column mapping rows to the paper's citation keys. Quality tiers: 27 High, 36 Moderate, 3 Low. See the included README for the full column guide.

title: LOC-AL: исчисление превышения лицензии использования вывода в логике Алеметрии
abstract: Вводится LOC-AL (License of Output Consumption — Alemetria Logic) — самостоятельный математический объект и самостоятельное модельно-параметризованное исчисление режимов использования уже полученного вывода как основания конкретной последующей операции в заданных контексте и состоянии. Архитектура объединяет типизированную модель, пакетную семантику, Lic и MaxLic, внешний фактический режим, Safe и Overrun, N/G/B-диагностику, минимальные сигнатуры и свидетелей, нормальную форму и переходы Ground, Prove, Retract с ограниченным восстановлением. Для исчисления доказываются корректность, полнота относительно экстенсиональной пакетной семантики и внутренняя адекватность; устанавливаются структура лицензированных и максимальных режимов, критерии безопасности и превышения, антицепность минимальных сигнатур, экстенсиональная инвариантность свидетелей, точная формула убывания дефекта и условная граница длины восстановления. Получены критерий восстановления нормальной формы по проекциям и эффективное построение при явно заданных вычислительных предпосылках. Авторский вклад состоит в новой типизированной композиции известных математических аппаратов вокруг отношения между конкретным выводом и конкретной основанной на нём операцией, а также в согласовании статического, диагностического и переходного слоёв этой композиции. Контрольная конечная модель иллюстрирует основные конструкции.

Для исчисления доказываются корректность, полнота относительно экстенсиональной пакетной семантики и внутренняя адекватность; устанавливаются структура лицензированных и максимальных режимов, критерии безопасности и превышения, антицепность минимальных сигнатур, экстенсиональная инвариантность свидетелей, точная формула убывания дефекта и условная граница длины восстановления. Получены критерий восстановления нормальной формы по проекциям и эффективное построение при явно заданных вычислительных предпосылках. Авторский вклад состоит в новой типизированной композиции известных математических аппаратов вокруг отношения между конкретным выводом и конкретной основанной на нём операцией, а также в согласовании статического, диагностического и переходного слоёв этой композиции. Контрольная конечная модель иллюстрирует основные конструкции.

title: When a Data Artifact Isn't a Shortcut: Causal Auditing of Synthetic RLVR Corpora
abstract: Several recent pipelines build RLVR training data by masking a span of real corpus text and asking a language model to invent plausible wrong answers around it. The correct option is therefore genuine human prose; every distractor is synthetic. Correctness and provenance become entangled, and a policy could in principle learn the second instead of the first. We audit that possibility in GooseReason-0.7M. First we ask whether the asymmetry is visible at all: a classifier reading only five surface statistics (never the meaning) reaches AUROC 0.562 over 315,499 options, barely above chance. The aggregate hides something, though. Code sits at 0.416, below chance, and manual inspection explains why: code distractors turn out to be single-operator mutations of the gold answer rather than freely written alternatives, so the two classes are nearly identical by construction. Detecting a signal is not the same as showing a model uses it, so we then run an intervention. We build a paraphrase-matched control corpus, hold training-set size identical across arms, and train two policies under one fixed budget. The exploitation gap does not favour the unmodified-data arm: 0.021 against 0.027 for the control. Under our budget, in other words, a detectable artifact went unexploited. We think that dissociation, along with the domain-specific construction finding, is worth knowing for anyone curating corpora of this kind, and we release the audit as a mostly CPU-only protocol.

title: Flow-Based Lattice Surgery Optimization with Runtime T Gate Scheduling
abstract: Lattice surgery on the surface code is a leading route to fault-tolerant quantum computation. Compiling logical circuits into lattice surgery operations is a pivotal step that determines the resource cost of a computation. Prior compilers build on idealized assumptions, and one that works in practical settings remains to be developed. Existing works are either unscalable or route one gate at a time within a layer, so the embedding depends on the order of gates and opportunities to route many gates at once are lost. In addition, they assume magic states are always available and cost-free, even though preparing one costs more than a Clifford operation. We present FlowRouter, the first topological lattice surgery compiler that places Clifford routing and stochastic magic state cultivation inside a single 3D embedding. At compile time, FlowRouter formulates the routing of an entire circuit layer as a maximum-flow problem, embedding many gates simultaneously. At runtime, it allows magic states to be cultivated at every idling patch, works with the realistic cultivation process with multiplexing and multi-stage post-selections, and absorbs the stochasticity by introducing delay mechanisms that add as little spacetime volume as possible. With magic states assumed free, FlowRouter reduces spacetime volume by 2.3x and compiles 10.8x faster than the state-of-the-art static topological lattice surgery compiler. With the cultivation-aware setting that includes both Clifford and magic state cost, FlowRouter reduces spacetime volume by 2.3x on a distance-13 surface code when compared with the state-of-the-art runtime compiler.
