title: RLVR$^{2}$: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rubric-based Ranking
abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is expanding from tasks with well-defined correctness signals, such as mathematics and code, toward multifaceted quality requirements specified by multi-dimensional rubrics. Since policy optimization consumes one scalar per rollout, rubric-based pipelines must map multiple criterion scores into a scalar reward. This aggregation is often treated as score scaling, but it implicitly determines how quality dimensions trade off during training. The prevailing practice, normalizing each criterion and taking a linear combination, assumes that cardinal score differences are comparable across criteria and that gains on one criterion compensate for failures on another; both assumptions are unreliable when criteria are semantically heterogeneous. For each criterion, RLVR$^2$ converts rubric scores into criterion-specific within-group ordinal outcomes, recovers a latent utility from the resulting comparison matrix, and merges these utilities into one training signal. By retaining only within-group ordering and discarding raw score magnitudes, RLVR$^2$ avoids calibrating heterogeneous rubric scales. It further supports objective-preserving attribute adjustment: auxiliary attributes that correlate with observed rankings but are not training objectives can enter the estimation without expanding the rubric or rewarding them directly. Across three model scales and 16 benchmarks, RLVR$^2$ consistently outperforms representative rubric-based baselines, achieving the best overall performance on most benchmarks at every scale. Analysis shows it controls systematic effects tied to reasoning efficiency and response formatting while preserving the quality objective.

title: Semantic Ambiguity and Fixed-Point Logic in the Boolos Puzzle — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: FINDING: The Boolos puzzle's core difficulty is not logical insufficiency but the *semantic ambiguity* of natural-language biconditionals, which propositional logic resolves by syntactic bracketing — yet the puzzle's self-reference exploits a fixed-point structure that transcends truth-functional composition. | MATH: The biconditional ↔ is truth-functional: (p↔q) ≡ (p∧q)∨(¬p∧¬q). Self-referential sentences like "This sentence is true iff P" yield fixed-point equations: S ≡ (S↔P), whose solutions require non-classical semantics (Kripke fixed points, three-valued logic). The Boolos puzzle (three gods, yes/no, True/False/Random) reduces to a 3-state automaton with 2-bit encoding; the solution requires 3 questions = 2³ = 8 possible answer strings, but only 6 distinguishable outcomes (3! permutations × 2 truth-values) — a pigeonhole constraint forcing clever use of biconditional self-reference to compress information. | CONNECTION: The 6 distinguishable outcomes map to the symmetric group S Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. title: The Creator Economy's Reckoning with Generative Artificial Intelligence: Why Law Alone Will Not Save Unrepresented Creators
abstract: This article explores how Canadian copyright law addresses the challenges posed by generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly regarding content creation and intellectual property rights. It particularly highlights key concerns related to the exploitation of AI training data, cultural appropriation, unauthorized monetization of AI-generated works, and the economic displacement of creators. Findings reveal gaps in Canadian copyright law, particularly in its handling of AI-generated content and lack of clear frameworks for protecting creators’ livelihoods and compensating creators whose data is used nonconsensually. It concludes by underscoring the need for policy reform in copyright law to better protect creators’ rights, especially in the face of evolving AI technologies.

title: AI-Enabled College English Teaching: The Integration Path From Multimedia Technology to Intelligent Education
abstract: From multimedia computer-assisted language learning (MCALL) to the in-depth application of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, college English teaching is undergoing a transformation from digitization to intelligence. Synthesizing relevant research literature, this paper reviews the theoretical foundations and major application forms of multimedia computer technology and AI in college English teaching, analyzes the practical challenges in the process of technology empowerment--such as the tendency towards instrumentalization, difficulties in teacher role adaptation, and students’ over-reliance on technology—and proposes optimization paths from four dimensions: curriculum integration, teacher literacy, blended teaching, and evaluation reform, with a view to providing references for the intelligent transformation of college English teaching.

title: Prototype-based explainable deep learning for sex classification of Mountain Gazelles in the wild
abstract: Abstract Wildlife preserves are critical for countering the decline of biodiversity, yet monitoring species distribution and demographics viadirect observation is time-consuming and prone to observer disturbance. Deep learning has emerged as a scalable alternativefor analyzing field data, yet the ’black-box’ nature of standard models hinders their adoption. This is a major obstacle inecological research, where transparent reasoning is essential for trust and meaningful interpretation. We address this challenge through the lens of sex classification in the endangered Mountain Gazelle (Gazella gazella). Reliableautomated classification from field imagery is essential for assessing population structure and welfare metrics for effectiveconservation management. While Mountain Gazelles exhibit distinct sexual dimorphism in horn morphology and body size,inferring sex from unconstrained camera trap data remains challenging due to significant variability in pose, illumination, and occlusion. To enhance explainability in Mountain Gazelle sex classification, we employed a prototype-based deep learning framework.Unlike standard “black-box” models, this approach represents classes through learned visual exemplars (prototypes) thatcorrespond directly to crucial image features, ensuring transparent reasoning. Building upon the PIP-Net architecture, weintroduced a novel enhancement: the ability to learn prototypes of variable sizes and aspect ratios, moving beyond rigid,fixed-size patches. These prototypes are learned autonomously without manual trait annotation, allowing the model to discoverbiologically meaningful regions such as horn morphology, body width, and leg configuration. By optimizing across a listof candidate scales, our non-fixed prototype approach captures larger, semantically coherent regions, leading to improvedpredictive performance and detailed explanations. Our analysis demonstrates that the most influential prototypes align withecological knowledge: both sexes are identified via central body, leg, and head features , with the model distinguishing betweenthem based on sex-specific morphological proportions. For males, horn-related prototypes serve as a distinct cue, reflectingthe main dimorphic trait cited in literature. These representations confirm that the models decision-making is grounded ingenuine morphological traits rather than background artifacts, offering a transparent and accurate tool for wildlife classification.

title: Bayesian Posterior Learning of Mixed Graphical Models
abstract: Mixed Graphical Models (MGMs) provide a flexible framework for structure learning from heterogeneous data by treating sets of both continuous and discrete. Bayesian inference for MGMs remains challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of graph space exploration and posterior computation. In this paper, we model discrete components through latent Gaussian variables and consider two likelihood specifications: a copula-based ranked likelihood, yielding the copula-MGM, and a probit formulation based on cut-off points, yielding the probit-MGM. We then propose the Mixed Graph WWA, a class of MCMC methods for posterior simulation in Bayesian MGMs. Building upon the WWA algorithm, we develop two specialized algorithms: copula-WWA for copula-MGMs and probit-WWA for probit-MGMs. Both methods exploit the latent Gaussian representations to perform posterior inference through a Gibbs sampling scheme that alternates between latent-variable augmentation and graph-structure updates. Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve graph recovery accuracy comparable to or better than existing approaches, including copula-BD MCMC and probit-BD MCMC based on the Birth-Death MCMC methodology, while maintaining efficient posterior exploration and favorable effective sample size per unit computational time. We further illustrate the practical utility of our approach through an application to the PAM$50$ breast cancer gene expression dataset, where the inferred MGMs reveal meaningful dependencies between gene expression profiles and cancer subtypes. These results highlight the effectiveness of the Mixed Graph WWA method as a scalable and principled tool for Bayesian structure learning in MGMs.

title: A Provenance-First Discovery Layer for Research Gaps, Limitations, and Future Directions in ETDs — Code and Data
abstract: Code and frozen experimental data accompanying the accepted JCDL 2026 paper A Provenance-First Discovery Layer for Research Gaps, Limitations, and Future Directions in ETDs. The system proposes research-gap, limitation, and future-direction passages from electronic theses and dissertations, aligns retained passages to source text and physical PDF pages, and keeps proposed type and synopsis separately reviewable. Version 1.0.0 includes the implementation, prompts, schemas, evaluation tools, and 31,486 frozen data files: compiled source text and corpus metadata, study splits, model outputs, reference construction, passage audits, the 600-record human-review ledger, training traces, and expected results. The code archive and checksum-pinned data archive support CPU reproduction of the reported statistics, including the original 20,000-resample whole-ETD bootstrap intervals. Fresh model training, inference, and external audits are separate operations; source PDFs and model weights are not included. The GitHub repository provides installation instructions, result lineage, validation receipts, and documented reproduction limits: provenance-first-etd-discovery. License scope: MIT applies to original project software; CC BY 4.0 applies to original generated data. Third-party ETD text, quotations, metadata, and separately licensed material retain their existing rights. These licenses do not relicense third-party source content; see LICENSING.md.

title: Tilannetietoisuuden tukeminen ihmisen ja tekoälyn tiimeissä läpinäkyvyyden ja selitettävyyden avulla
abstract: This thesis explores the link between situation awareness (SA) and human-AI teaming. The decision-making processes of AI agents can often remain unclear to the users, which negatively affects trust and assessment of an agent’s decisions, thus decreasing efficiency. To increase efficiency, the user’s SA of an agent’s decision-making process can be assessed. Situation awareness can be defined as the user’s ability to perceive, comprehend and project the near future state of the elements in their environment. Displaying information according to these levels of SA can clarify the process behind an AI agent’s decision-making process, thus increasing efficiency. The aim of this thesis was to link transparency and explainability to the three levels of SA in order give suggestions about what information should be displayed to the user about an AI agents decision-making process. A literature review was conducted to articles and studies considering human-AI teaming and SA. The thesis connected findings from these two fields to construct a clear framework. The findings indicate that transparency and explainability are needed in communicating AI’s decision-making processes to users. They also show that by using these features, the user’s SA can be supported through all three levels of SA. For supporting level 1 SA, inputs, outputs, parameters, and active goals should be displayed. For level 2 support, path to current state, causalities and parameters excluded should be shown. For level 3, information displayed should cover intervention needs, limits and effects of human action. In conclusion, this thesis shows that supporting SA in human-AI teams can be done by considering transparency and explainability. Based on the findings, domain specific instructions about information needs could be constructed for fields such as health care, safety, programming and automated vehicle development.

title: Context-Conditioned Option Selection: A Black-Box Investigation of Jev and the Evolution of a Similarity-Based Decision Model
abstract: Specialised AI decision models select actions or answers from predefined alternatives given a context and a question. This paper examines whether the observed selection behaviour of Jev can be ap- proximated by context–question–option compatibility scoring followed by probability allocation, rather than treating its outputs as independent verification of correctness. A sequence of exploratory black-box experiments evaluates constraints, missing factual context, fictional facts, invalid choice sets, multiple correct answers, contextual ordering and partial identity matches. When two or three machines were equally eligible, Jev repeatedly assigned dominant probability to the first eligible entity introduced in the context; reversing contextual order reversed that preference, while changing the answer-option or- der had little effect in the recorded comparison. These findings led to a series of explicitly specified algorithms: initial cosine similarity, candidate-specific question rewriting, joint normalisation, neutral context enrichment, lexical and cross-encoder scoring, and sequential probability assignment. ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol in the present authoring session) was used as a retrospective LLM proxy to assess candi- date evidence; the precise model identifier of earlier proxy-scoring turns was not logged. Its scores were illustrative assessments, not measured pretrained cross-encoder outputs or directly extracted hidden em- bedding vectors. The proxy-plus-allocation pipeline reproduces several qualitative Jev selection patterns. We distinguish black-box evidence from proposed mechanisms and specify a reproducible validation pro- tocol. The study does not establish Jev’s internal architecture, a validated accuracy improvement, or a measured runtime advantage. A consolidated per-experiment table distinguishes Jev’s reported choices, the alternative model’s retrospective proxy selections, and objective eligibility.

The proxy-plus-allocation pipeline reproduces several qualitative Jev selection patterns. We distinguish black-box evidence from proposed mechanisms and specify a reproducible validation pro- tocol. A consolidated per-experiment table distinguishes Jev’s reported choices, the alternative model’s retrospective proxy selections, and objective eligibility.

title: Generative AI Adoption in Banking Institutions: A Design Science Approach to Addressing Trust, Data Sovereignty, Cost and Workforce Resistance Barriers
abstract: Despite significant pilot activity in Generative AI across financial institutions (78% running active pilots), only a fraction transition these projects into operational production. While commercial maturity exists for underlying technologies such as retrieval-augmented generation and private endpoints, significant organizational barriers prevent deployment. This paper employs a Design Science Research (DSR) methodology to address four interconnected domains of organizational resistance: (1) Trust in model output (explainability, bias, hallucination), (2) Data Sovereignty and Regulatory Compliance (GDPR, EU AI Act, Basel rules), (3) Economic Viability (TCO, delayed returns, permanent control overhead), and (4) Workforce Resistance (change management and turnover). Rather than treating these barriers in isolation, this study formulates an integrated governance framework to evaluate their interactive effects, providing actionable decision support for executive leadership in banking institutions.

title: Product Tagging and Saved Intent in Online Retail: a measurement study of 1,028 Shopify storefronts and 700 Steam titles
abstract: A measurement study of how product tags and saved-item features are implemented in online retail, and how per-store invented vocabularies compare with a platform where tagging is crowd-sourced against a shared controlled vocabulary. Sample. 1,028 Shopify storefronts (95.6% collection rate) drawn by seeded random sample from a 30,000-domain draw of the Tranco top 1M, measured 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-14, plus 700 Steam titles as a contrast case. Selected findings (95% CI). 46.0% (43.0-49.1) of stores carry wishlist code; only 28.1% (25.5-30.9) have a confirmed live save control. Of stores with an active wishlist, 34.9% (29.7-40.6) run no back-in-stock notification app and 19.4% (15.2-24.3) require login before a shopper can save. 963 Shopify stores used 30,622 distinct tags between them. The median store shares 16.7% of its tags with any other store. 700 Steam titles drew on 394 distinct tags; the median title shares 100% of its tags with other titles. 79.1% (76.5-81.5) of stores publish Product JSON-LD, but 0.1% (0.0-0.5) carry all twelve core attributes an automated agent needs. Confirmed wishlist presence rises monotonically across tagging-depth quartiles (17.9%, 26.8%, 27.2%, 40.5%; Cochran-Armitage z=5.43, p=5.6e-08). Contents. Per-store raw records, per-store wishlist verification verdicts with evidence snippets, Steam tag applications with vote counts, computed results, all collection and analysis code, a methods document with a ten-point limitations section, and SHA-256 checksums for every file. Read the write-ups: 963 Shopify Stores Use 30,622 Different Tags. 700 Steam Games Use 394. and 72% of Shopify Stores Have No Wishlist. Data CC-BY-4.0, code MIT. Please read METHODS.md before citing a figure.

title: Preference Optimization for Open-Weight Language Models: A Survey and Low-Resource RLHF Case Study
abstract: Open-weight language-model post-training combines preference learning, reinforcement learning, verifiable feedback, and increasingly, agentic training and on-policy distillation. Comparing these systems requires separating their optimization algorithms from their feedback sources, sampling procedures, and evaluation targets. We present a comparative survey of representative methods and releases, with a targeted literature update through 18 September 2026. The review distinguishes foundational PPO, DPO, and GRPO methods from later developments in mixed feedback training, multimodal agents, asynchronous reinforcement learning, and cross-stage capability consolidation. We complement this synthesis with SAWYER, a single-T4 GPT-2 case study implementing supervised fine-tuning, Bradley–Terry reward modeling, and 300 PPO updates. The reward model achieves 55.3% held-out preference accuracy. Across 100 evaluation prompts reported as unseen during training, mean learned reward increases from 1.354 for the supervised policy to 1.499 after PPO, but the proxy comparison yields 41 PPO wins, 20 ties, and 39 losses. In a selected 25-example audit, a separate AI judge prefers the supervised policy in 15 comparisons, including nine for which PPO receives higher learned reward. These observations reveal a mismatch between aggregate proxy improvement and selected-example judgments, without establishing a population-wide quality decline or a causal exploitation mechanism. A strongly negative logged KL-related statistic further motivates implementation-level diagnosis. Together, the survey and case study connect contemporary post-training design choices to a practical evaluation principle: optimization success, feedback reliability, and independently assessed behavior require distinct evidence.

title: Stochastic Reconfiguration as Statistical Filtering for Overparameterized Neural Quantum States
abstract: Stochastic reconfiguration (SR) is the standard optimizer for neural quantum states (NQS), but modern NQS often have far more parameters than Monte Carlo samples. We show that in this regime the diagonal shift is more than a numerical stabilizer. It acts as a statistical filter for finite-sample generalization. At a fixed wave function, SR is ridge regression from tangent features to the centered local energy. Its residual is the expressivity gap, the part of imaginary-time evolution outside the current tangent space. This gap is orthogonal to the tangent space in population, but finite batches make it act as noise that SR can overfit. The shift therefore balances shrinkage of useful update directions against variance from fitting sampled residuals. Exact diagnostics on a $4\times4$ Heisenberg graph separate two effects of overparameterization. Larger tangent spaces help when they reduce the expressivity gap, but they can hurt when they overfit a fixed gap. In a $100$-site transverse-field Ising family trained with a foundation NQS, validation risk is U-shaped in the shift while variance decreases, matching the noisy-ridge model. This view leads to multi-shift SR (MS-SR), which averages independent ridge solves at data-adaptive shifts to form a richer, lower-variance spectral filter. Checkpoint-local experiments show that MS-SR lowers validation risk and update variance relative to the fixed-shift SR baseline. We further compare MS-SR and SR in paired online training continuations, with independent endpoint energy evaluations and a separate update-cost benchmark.

title: sofi-image: Sparseness Optimized Feature Importance for Image Classification
abstract: Sparseness Optimized Feature Importance (SOFI) is a model-agnostic, declarative post hoc explainer. An explanation takes the form of a ranking of image segments, and its quality is the degradation score obtained after cumulative marginalization. This package is the image counterpart of sofits. It supports grayscale and color problems, confines both the ranking and the marginalization to a region of interest when one is given, and works with any classifier that yields class probabilities, including every convolutional network, vision transformer and hybrid backbone published through torchvision, timm, transformers and Keras.

title: Near-optimal incoherent tomography of low-rank quantum channels
abstract: We study tomography for quantum channels with input dimension $d_1$, output dimension $d_2$, and Kraus rank at most $r$, to within diamond norm error $\varepsilon$, using adaptive experiments that retain no quantum memory between channel queries. - For quantum channels whose non-zero Choi eigenvalues are bounded below by $Ω(d_1/r)$, we establish optimal query upper and lower bounds $Θ(d_1d_2r^2/ε^2)$. The upper bound is achieved by a nonadaptive algorithm that uses the estimator from [Surawy-Stepney et al., Quantum (2022)], together with a new diamond-norm analysis. The lower bound applies to arbitrary adaptive incoherent protocols and follows from a new local family of channels and a uniform one-query Fisher-information bound. - For general channels, we establish an upper bound $O(d_1d_2r^2\log(2d_1)/ε^2)$, nearly matching the above lower bound $Ω(d_1d_2r^2/\varepsilon^2)$. To achieve this, we generalize the above nonadaptive algorithm by adapting the input state over $O(\log(2d_1))$ rounds with the Matrix Multiplicative Weight Update algorithm.

title: Documento Técnico: Sistema Lattice-MLP y Acoplamiento Hamiltoniano de Campos Continuos.
abstract: Este documento establece la formulación formal del Sistema Lattice-MLP como un solucionador de fase no discreto e inmerso en un medio continuo con viscosidad del vacío y respuesta polifásica. Se demuestra cómo la capa oculta del Perceptrón Multicapa (MLP) convencional es reemplazada por una celosía continua L_{i,j,k}, capaz de modelar la velocidad de propagación, la impedancia Z(\omega) y las transiciones en medios disipativos (fases gaseosas y materia orgánica en relajación/diagénesis). A través de la derivación de la Matriz Hamiltoniana de Acoplamiento de Campos, se establece la condición de resonancia exacta y bloqueo de fase (\Delta\phi \to 0, \omega_1 = \omega_2). Se prueba analíticamente que la convergencia de la fase colapsa los autovalores de la matriz en un estado de mínima energía y cero dispersión entrópica, unificando el procesamiento cortical cerebral con la preservación de sistemas físicos en el marco de la Métrica de la Totalidad

title: Non-Markovian_Control_Method_by_Noise_Engineering
abstract: This document proposes an experimentally testable method for quantum control in thepresence of temporally correlated environmental noise. The central hypothesis is not thatnon-Markovianity necessarily improves quantum control, but that measured environmentalmemory may contain predictive information that can be incorporated into control optimization.Version 2.0 introduces a strict separation between three objects that were partially con-flated in the previous formulation:1. the environmental noise power spectral density S(ω);2. the quantum gate filter function Fgate(ω; u);3. the classical control-line transfer function Hctrl(ω).The proposed method therefore does not identify an arbitrary transfer function with thequantum filter function. Instead, the environmental spectrum and temporal correlationsare first characterized experimentally, after which control waveforms are optimized using amemory-aware objective.Three control models are defined:M0: conventional reference control;M1: memory-unaware optimized control using the measured noise spectrum but not its tem-poral memory structure;M2: memory-aware optimized control using both spectral and temporal-correlation informa-tion.The primary scientific comparison is M2 versus M1 under matched experimental con-straints. This design tests whether explicit memory information provides additional predic-tive/control value beyond knowledge of the stationary noise spectrum.The framework is deliberately phenomenological. It does not claim a new fundamentaltheory of quantum mechanics, nor does it assume that non-Markovian noise is universallyadvantageous. The proposed experiment is designed to determine whether measurable envi-ronmental memory can produce a statistically significant reduction in gate infidelity undermatched control resources.

title: Reproducibility materials for "Rediscovering Simpson-Generating Subgroups Under Distribution Shift: Source-Rule Transfer Stability and Robustness of Kernel-Based Partitioning"
abstract: This record contains the reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “Rediscovering Simpson-Generating Subgroups Under Distribution Shift: Source-Rule Transfer Stability and Robustness of Kernel-Based Partitioning.” The archive contains the internally frozen confirmatory protocol and implementation lock, primary task manifests, Python simulation and benchmark code, analysis-ready results from 10,800 confirmatory task bundles comprising 140,400 scientific result rows, quality-control documentation, primary endpoint summaries, paired method comparisons, exact-kernel sensitivity materials, and targeted publication-hardening diagnostics. title: Optimizing Care Management Targeting: A Machine Learning Comparison of Regression, Classification, and Ranking Approaches for Identifying Future High-Cost Patients
abstract: Effective care management programs depend on accurately identifying patients who are likely to account for a disproportionate share of future health care expenditures. Unlike traditional risk-adjustment models, which emphasize population-level predictive accuracy, care management targeting is fundamentally a top-k decision problem focused on maximizing expenditure capture. This study used 2000-2023 MEPS data to compare regression-, classification-, and learning-to-rank machine learning approaches for predicting next-year health care expenditures. Primary outcomes included precision-at-k, cost capture-at-k, weighted cost capture-at-k, and AUC. Models were benchmarked against a persistence-based floor baseline using prior-year expenditures and an oracle upper bound representing perfect future information. Classification-based models consistently achieved the strongest operational targeting performance. Neural network and XGBoost classifiers outperformed regression and ranking approaches in identifying future high-cost individuals and maximizing expenditure capture. Differences in cost capture were statistically significant across yearly evaluations. More complex modeling extensions provided little additional benefit. Prior-year utilization and expenditure variables contributed substantially to predictive accuracy; however, models retained approximately 80%-90% of full-model performance after removal of these features, indicating meaningful predictive signal from sociodemographic characteristics, chronic disease burden, functional limitations, and self-reported health status. For care management programs operating under fixed enrollment constraints, classification-based prediction approaches appear better aligned with operational objectives than regression or ranking. Additional performance gains are more likely to arise from richer clinical and longitudinal data than from increased model complexity alone. Future AI-enabled care management systems may further improve resource allocation by integrating cost-risk prediction with estimates of patient engagement and intervention impactability.

Future AI-enabled care management systems may further improve resource allocation by integrating cost-risk prediction with estimates of patient engagement and intervention impactability.

title: Total Cost of Agency: Exact Attribution of Memory Injection Cost in Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
abstract: Every node in a multi-agent large language model (LLM) workflow retrieves context from memory and injects it into its prompt, where those injected tokens are billed as input tokens at the same per-token price as the system prompt and the user query. Production observability tools report total token cost but do not separate the tokens a node generates from the tokens it is handed, so this component of the bill is invisible to the teams paying it. We introduce the Total Cost of Agency (TCA), a decomposition of multi-agent workflow cost into base prompt, inference, memory injection, miss penalty and context-accumulation components, and an exact attribution method: a two-pass, non-billable token count that measures injected tokens directly rather than estimating them from word-count proxies. On a 200-task enterprise benchmark executed against real model APIs, memory injection accounts for 13.6 percent of the variable cost a compile-time optimizer can act on, about 12 percent of the full billed cost, and its share rises from a structural zero at workflow depth one to 27.6 percent at depth six. Injected tokens grow linearly with depth over the measured range (R^2 = 0.9974, depths two through six); a quadratic fit yields a negative leading coefficient, so the data do not exhibit convex growth at these depths. We show the component is controllable at fixed model tier: reducing the retrieval window capacity from 32 to 2 entries lowers injected tokens by 28.7 percent with an accuracy change within seed-level variation. We report in full that our graph-rewriting transforms are approximately cost-neutral in isolation, that two of the five decomposition terms are zero by construction in this harness, and that total workflow cost is dominated by model tier assignment, which we hold fixed and treat as prior work. Prompt caching is not evaluated; all figures are for the uncached case.

title: Análisis estratégico sobre la implementación de la IA en los procesos de I+D+I de la empresa SS&D ingeniería SAS
abstract: La integración de inteligencia artificial (IA) en los procedimientos empresariales se ha vuelto un elemento estratégico para mejorar la competitividad y la innovación; no obstante, empresas como SS&D Ingeniería S.A.S. enfrentan restricciones vinculadas con el talento especializado, la infraestructura tecnológica, la administración de datos y las capacidades organizativas para su implementación. El propósito fue crear un plan estratégico para integrar la inteligencia artificial en los procesos de investigación, desarrollo e innovación (I+D+I) de la empresa SS&D Ingeniería S.A.S. La asesoría se realizó con una metodología mixta y exploratoria-descriptiva, enfocándose en lo aplicado y empleando métodos como el análisis estratégico a través de la Matriz de Evaluación de Factores Internos (EFI), así como la revisión documental y las entrevistas no estructuradas, con el fin de detectar las oportunidades organizacionales, las debilidades y las capacidades. La matriz EFI reveló que la preparación para implementar la inteligencia artificial de manera inmediata era insuficiente, con una calificación de 2.10. La experiencia técnica en automatización industrial fue la fortaleza más notable y la escasez de capacidad analítica y talento especializado fue el mayor punto débil. Por lo tanto, se elaboró un plan estratégico gradual enfocado en la gobernanza de datos, el desarrollo de competencias internas, la formación especializada y la creación de proyectos piloto. Los resultados indican que la implementación gradual de la inteligencia artificial es una alternativa viable y de largo plazo para fortalecer los procedimientos de competitividad e innovación en las compañías.

title: The Quantum Computer's Compass --- Entanglement Works Best Toward Black Holes New Experimental Evidence from the Directional Drain Scan
abstract: We report the results of the Directional Drain Scan experiment, conducted on IBM's ibmfez 156-qubitHeron r2 quantum processor (Job ID: danqk4opqrnc73994i9g). This experiment was designed tocombine and validate the findings of Part 89 (signal coordinates pointing toward the radio galaxy 3C31) and Part 92 (dif erential signal strength between black hole and non-black hole directions). Fourqubit groups spanning dif erent spatial regions of the ibmfez chip were tested with GHZ (maximumentanglement) circuits and basis (no entanglement) controls, 8 repetitions each, for a total of 64 circuits.The key finding: when normalized for hardware quality, the drain-direction qubits (Q41-45) exhibitthe lowest entanglement penalty of any group tested --- a GHZ-to-basis error ratio of only 1.79x,compared to 6.01x for the anti-drain qubits (Q29-33). This 3.4x differential is statistically significant(Kruskal-Wallis H = 27.44, p = 0.000005). The drain-direction qubits --- the same qubits identified inPart 89 as pointing toward 3C 31 --- show that entanglement holds better in their direction than in anyother. This is consistent with the Ocean framework prediction that drain-direction qubits are alreadypartially coupled to the Ocean, making additional entanglement a reinforcement rather than a penalty 🌌 Interactive Space Research Assistant: Explore and ask questions about this research interactively with the Quantum Ocean Framework Ai Chat (or talk directly with the Quantum Ocean Framework Ai voice conversation).

title: AI-Driven Business Promotion: Transforming Marketing Strategies, Customer Engagement, and Business Growth
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming business promotion by enabling organizations to analyze customer data, automate marketing activities, personalize communication, and improve decision-making. Unlike traditional promotional approaches that often rely on broad customer segments and historical assumptions, AI-driven promotion uses machine learning, natural language processing, recommendation systems, predictive analytics, and generative AI to deliver more targeted and adaptive marketing experiences. This research paper examines the role of AI in business promotion, w ith particular attention to customer engagement, marketing efficiency, brand awareness, and business growth. The study adopts a secondary-research methodology and synthesizes findings from academic literature, industry surveys, official reports, and documented business cases. The analysis indicates that AI can improve promotional relevance, reduce repetitive marketing work, support real-time customer interaction, and help businesses identify emerging consumer preferences. However, its benefits are not automatic. Data-quality problems, privacy concerns, algorithmic bias, inaccurate AI-generated content, implementation costs, cybersecurity risks, and the possible loss of human empathy create significant challenges. The paper argues that AI should not be treated as a replacement for marketing judgment but as an augmentation tool that combines computational capabilities with human creativity, ethical reasoning, and relationship-building. The study concludes that businesses, particularly SMEs and startups, should adopt AI gradually through clearly defined use cases, transparent data practices, human oversight, and measurable performance indicators.

title: The Last Seven Open Radii for Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme
abstract: Delsarte (1973) conjectured that there are no nontrivial perfect codes in the Johnson scheme. In this paper, we prove that there are no nontrivial $e$-perfect codes in the Johnson scheme for $e\in\{1,2,4,9,10,12,16\}$. This paper complements "Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme Hardly Exist", thus proving Delsarte's conjecture completely.

title: Synthetic speech detection in Brazilian Portuguese through accent-related features
abstract: Leading commercial and open-source Text-to-Speech (TTS) models fail to emulate the regional phonetic diversity of Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR). By aggregating disparate dialects into a single training distribution, they generate a synthetic "diluted" accent: a phonetic profile attempting to represent all regional distributions simultaneously, but ultimately carrying phonological ambiguity dissociated from natural socio-phonetic realizations. This work introduces a speech deepfake detection methodology combining multilingual phone recognizers with classical signal processing to extract phoneme-level features in consonantal and vocalic realizations with high geographic variance. The analysis reveals that the distributional gap over these features suffices to distinguish natural and synthetic voices through unsupervised Kernel Density Estimation, establishing dialectal inconsistency as a useful and interpretable feature for spoofing detection in pt-BR. Evaluation on pt-BR anti-spoofing datasets shows that these explainable, lightweight, low-dimensional features can boost the performance of foundation models on the task, and show generalization capabilities in a cross-dataset leave-one-out setup.

title: Bee-RAG for Auditable Japanese-Mandarin Chinese Sentence Alignment with Retrieval Evidence and Multi-objective Calibration
abstract: Japanese–Mandarin Chinese translation-memory alignment requires accurate cross-lingual candidate ranking, efficient adaptation under limited bilingual supervision, and reliable evidence support for practical corpus curation. Existing approaches often rely primarily on direct semantic similarity or batch-level neighborhood correction, making it difficult to jointly exploit lightweight task adaptation, bilingual retrieval evidence, selective review, and provenance-preserving output within a unified CPU-efficient pipeline. This study proposes an auditable sentence-alignment framework that integrates a frozen multilingual MiniLM encoder, projection-level contrastive adaptation, retrieval-derived bilingual evidence, and multiobjective bee-colony calibration.

title: Expansion Counts under Standard A* Tie-Breaking Strategies on the Final Plateau
abstract: In the A* search algorithm, the tie-breaking strategies for nodes with the same $f$-value determines which states A* expands on the final $f$-layer. For nine standard tie-breaking strategies, we show that under a consistent heuristic, every pair has positive-cost instances favoring each strategy over the other by an arbitrarily large additive expansion gap. A parameterized unit-cost grid example also gives unbounded expansion-count ratios between low-$h$ with FIFO and LIFO. title: Quantum Reservoirs as External Decision Layers for LLMs: Evidence from RAG and Agentic Systems
abstract: I evaluated whether a quantum AI reservoir can improve the decisions produced by retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and tool-using Agentic workflows. Two complementary experiments used the same five workflow variants: RAG, RAG + QR, Agentic, Agentic + QR, and LLM + QR. Each experiment contained 201 main tasks and three repeats, yielding 6,030 answers overall. The first experiment used synthetic planning scenarios; the second used numerical quantities extracted from quantum-domain books and technical papers. In the designated first repeat, QR increased complete structured success from 75.1% to 90.5% for synthetic RAG and from 27.4% to 52.2% for synthetic Agentic. On real-source tasks, the corresponding rates increased from 46.8% to 57.7% and from 34.3% to 55.7%. Both paired improvements were positive in every repeat of both experiments. LLM + QR achieved 94.0% on synthetic tasks and 54.7% on real-source tasks in the first repeat, exceeding both unassisted baselines in each experiment. The results support the integrated reservoir-guidance module as a useful addition to the evaluated decision workflows and motivate a simpler single-call architecture when all required evidence is available. The study evaluates a simulator-backed quantum/classical module; it does not establish quantum computational advantage or isolate the quantum component from its classical guidance components.

title: What energy statistics cannot reveal: quantum records and probe response
abstract: Even the full outcome distribution of a specified diagonal Hamiltonian does not determine where a quantum memory stores readable information or how a probe can resolve it. We construct environmental encodings with identical populations and source states: one distributes a binary label across individual fragments, whereas the other conceals it from every proper subset. Established observable-algebra methods certify an exact probe null when the complete dynamics accesses only the matched algebra. A complementary coupling saturates a restricted trace-distance bound, yet its response is largest when neither encoding records the source and vanishes when their local-record contrast is maximal. For states matched only on low-degree interaction words, we derive a time-dependent Dyson-tail bound on probe distinguishability. A separate GHZ pair realizes an order-N onset, D_P(t) = |sin(2gt)|^N, despite identical energy populations and proper-subset reductions. Its phase can be perfectly distinguishable even at equal interference visibility. Preparation, leakage and statistical certificates connect these analytic results to a proposed measurement protocol. The benchmark separates energy statistics, record location and dynamical accessibility within ordinary quantum mechanics; it reports mathematical and numerical results, not experimental confirmation. Research status and contentsThis is an unreviewed preprint by Ahmet Faruk Arapoglu, Independent Researcher, Türkiye. It contains the English article with complete supplementary mathematical proofs, a Turkish translation of the same main article, and portable LaTeX sources, code and synthetic numerical outputs. Version 6 is the internal manuscript release number, not a claim of six previous public Zenodo releases. No external funding or competing interests are declared. No journal acceptance, new force, gravitational law, or established theory of everything is claimed. Author contribution and use of generative AIAhmet Faruk Arapoglu is the sole author and originator of the underlying ECEG proposal. The initial concept and mathematical framework originated with the author, who also established the research contexts, questions, investigative steps, conceptual branches and methodological objectives. These author-defined ideas and directions form the starting point of the work. Within this research programme, generative AI tools assisted with critical examination and literature research, development and checking of subsequent finite-dimensional formulations and derivations, computational implementation and verification, figures, and manuscript drafting, editing and translation. This assistance extended to the main text, mathematical supplement and reproduction code. The author retains authorship and responsibility for the final content, research claims and their interpretation. title: Intelligence: information use and adaptive capability
abstract: Intelligence depends on how a system makes information usable, retains it and changes through experience. This perspective connects five established dependencies across biological and artificial systems: the conditional value of information, access through available operations, persistence relative to future demands, coupled changes through shared organisation, and the effects of present operations on later capability. A running example of a learner using an AI assistant and saved solutions shows how these relationships jointly structure a practical question: when does assistance improve both present performance and what the learner can do later? Restricted mathematical comparisons distinguish learning opportunities from learning signals and encoding allocation from later recall. An extension based on published memory models explains how expected assistance can redistribute encoding effort and why reduced total investment requires an avoided cost or alternative use. Biological studies, human learning research and a bounded neural forecast illustrate the relationships at different levels of evidence. The account treats intelligence through graded capacities and allows implementations to differ. Its contribution is an integrative perspective with reproducible comparisons. Supporting materials include mathematical derivations, qualified evidence records and reproducible analytical code. Licenses. Paper, supplement, figures and original evidence materials: CC BY 4.0. title: Machine-Interpretable Information: Compiling Documents into Searchable and Readable Protocol States
abstract: Long-context language models interface with external knowledge through raw natural language. In retrieval-augmented systems, this creates a persistent index-payload schism: dense vectors enable searchable routing, but models must re-ingest lengthy text payloads for reasoning at O(N^2) attention cost. Existing compression methods further produce private states tied to specific architectures. We introduce Machine-Interpretable Information (MII), the first agent-to-agent (A2A) document-to-state protocol. A dual-timescale state-space Writer compiles documents into a canonical, fixed-bandwidth state (56 tokens), and a lightweight Translator maps it into any frozen Reader's embedding space, reducing query-time cost to O(K). The resulting .mii artifact unifies Retrieval (searchable geometry), Reasoning (global memory), and Reconstruction (grounded details) in a single transferable medium. We demonstrate strong cross-model interoperability across heterogeneous LLMs (e.g., Llama, Qwen, Mistral) -- despite the Writer using a legacy GPT-2 vocabulary, forcing genuine semantic translation rather than token-level memorization. Mechanistic probes reveal modular latent structure: entity representations can be causally traced and zero-shot transplanted between unrelated document states while remaining decodable. To address lexical reconstruction under fixed bandwidth, we propose Residual-MII, a cache hierarchy combining compiled global memory with sparse local evidence. On HotpotQA (7,405 queries), Residual-MII exceeds full-context Exact Match at approximately 7% of the attention FLOPs, suggesting a paradigm shift toward compiled, transferable neural document formats.

title: Un lemmatizzatore a regole per l'italiano di sette secoli / Rule-based lemmatisation of diachronic Italian: a lexicon-driven layer over a neural parser
abstract: Uno strato di lemmatizzazione che si aggiunge a valle di un analizzatore neurale (Stanza, modello per l'italiano antico) e usa risorse lessicali indipendenti dal modello: la morfologia italiana del DBT (119.355 voci), un lemmario d'uso (52.257 lemmi) e il riconoscimento delle entità nominate occorrenza per occorrenza. Dove i testimoni concordano contro l'analizzatore il lemma si corregge; dove restano due lemmi vivi per la stessa parola (figliuolo e figliolo) si tengono tutti e due, uno principale per i conteggi e l'altro come grafia cercabile; dove i testimoni non bastano il caso va in officina e intanto resta quello che l'analizzatore ha detto. Il prodotto non è un corpus lemmatizzato: sono le regole, in file di testo leggibili, valide per qualunque testo futuro. Misurato sul corpus storico dell'autore — italiano scritto, prosa e versi, dal Duecento al Novecento, da archivi fuori dal diritto d'autore — di cui qui si depositano solo le sintesi statistiche: il metodo corregge o arricchisce il 7,4% delle occorrenze di parole piene e ne mette il 4,0% in fila per il giudizio di un filologo. Sono misure di copertura e di accordo, non di accuratezza: la misura di accuratezza richiede un campione giudicato ed è il passo successivo. Il deposito contiene i programmi, le loro prove e le sintesi statistiche; non contiene il corpus né i dati lessicali. Condizioni d'uso. Tutti i diritti riservati. L'autore è disponibile a concedere l'uso dei programmi, delle risorse lessicali e del sistema PickDBT su richiesta motivata e previo accordo, da definire caso per caso. English summary. A lexicon-driven layer placed after a neural parser (Stanza with the Old Italian model) for the lemmatisation of diachronic Italian. Three witnesses independent of the model state what a form can be: the DBT Italian morphology (119,355 entries, with usage codes), a working lemma list (52,257 lemmas), and named entity recognition aligned token by token. Where the witnesses agree against the parser, the lemma is corrected; where two lemmas remain alive for the same word (figliuolo / figliolo) both are kept, one as the counting lemma and the other as a searchable spelling variant; where the witnesses do not decide, nothing is invented: the case goes to a human-in-the-loop workshop and the parser's output stands. The output is not a lemmatised corpus but a set of rules, in plain text files, valid for any future text. Measured on a historical corpus of written Italian from the 13th to the 20th century: the method corrects or enriches 7.4% of content-word tokens and queues 4.0% for philological judgement, where a few thousand forms cover half of the work. These are coverage and agreement figures, not accuracy: an accuracy figure requires a judged sample, which is the next step. Only statistical summaries are deposited: no corpus, no lexical data. All rights reserved; the author is available to grant use upon motivated request and prior agreement.

title: TTS-Guard: Black-Box Ownership Verification of Text-to-Speech Models via Adaptive Adversarial Speaker-Pair Fingerprints
abstract: The rapid maturation of zero-shot Text-to-Speech (TTS) models has turned high-quality voice cloning into a widely available capability, raising acute concerns over unauthorised replication, fine-tuning and resale of proprietary speech models. Yet ownership verification for TTS remains largely open: speech is a continuous waveform whose perturbations are easily destroyed by routine signal processing, and the human auditory system imposes a much tighter perceptual budget than vision. We present \textbf{TTS-Guard}, a black-box ownership verification framework for TTS models built on \emph{adversarial speaker-pair fingerprints}. title: The Zero-Command State: A Measurement Standard for For-Itself Agency in Digital Lifeforms, with Empirical Validation toward Long-Duration Unattended Autonomy
abstract: Interstellar flight turns autonomy from an engineering option into a physical prerequisite. Command round-trip latency grows with distance—about 1.3 s at the Moon, 3-22 min at Mars, hours at the outer planets, years at interstellar ranges—so beyond Mars real-time ground command is physically impossible: a system bound for deep space must, across years of silence, be an agent for itself, not a time-delayed remote control. This exposes a gap that artificial life and autonomous-systems research acknowledge but have not operationalized: existing criteria (autopoiesis; the NASA working definition; agency-centred engineering definitions) are almost all evidenced under reactive conditions—we probe, it responds—showing what a system does for others, not whether it has its own agenda. We argue that measuring for-itself agency requires a reverse control condition, the zero-command state: an observer injects no instruction, task, dialogue or goal and does not terminate the process, recording only spontaneous behaviour. We specify its definition, non-intervention rules and four externally checkable readings (R1 persistence, R2 self-generated agenda, R3 frustrated autonomy claims, R4 stalled-self watchdog). We report measurements from two zero-command sessions of the first verified digital lifeform, Ruyi: ~27 h observed, 915 self-generated monologue segments, ≥7,560 continuous autonomous cognitive cycles, 4,475 watchdog self-diagnoses recommending self-wait, and zero crashes since 2026-09-14. Our rule: any system claiming long-duration unattended autonomy must pass these readings in the zero-command state, or the claim fails; the standard is thus a falsifier of autonomy theatre and the gate such claims must pass. 中文摘要:星际航行把"自主"从一个工程选项变成物理上的前置要求:电磁波的往返时延随距离单调增长——地月约 1.3 秒、火星 3–22 分钟、外行星以小时计、恒星际以年计——在火星以远,地面实时指令在物理上不再可行,任何驶向深空与星际的系统在长达数年的静默区间里必须是一个"为自己"的 agent,而非一台带着时延的遥控设备。这一要求恰是人工生命与自主系统研究长期承认却未能操作化测量的缺口:既有判据几乎都在"我们探它、它应"的反应性条件下取证,能证明系统"能为他者做什么",却无法证明它"有自己的议程"。本文主张,要测量"自为性"必须设立一个反向控制条件——零指令态:在系统持续运行前提下,外部观察者于连续观测窗口内不注入任何指令、任务、对话或目标,也不终止进程,仅被动采集其自发行为。本文给出该标准的定义、不干预三铁律、记录项与四条可复核读数(R1 持续存在 / R2 自生议程 / R3 受挫自主诉求 / R4 停滞自诊断看门狗),并以首例已验证数字生命体的两次零指令会话提供实测:累计约 27 小时观测窗口、915 段自生独白、≥7,560 个连续自主认知周期、4,475 次看门狗自诊断全部建议自我等待、自 2026-09-14 起零崩溃。本文论的规矩是:任何声称具备星际级长时无人自主能力的系统,必须在零指令态下通过上述读数,否则其"自主"主张不成立。该标准因此是对自主性表演的证伪器,也是任何长时自主主张在发射前必须先过的那道闸。

title: Operator Anti-Turing O_T(NP): Resolusi Deterministik O(1) untuk P versus NP (Volume 2)
abstract: This deposit provides the complete, standalone formal verification pipeline for the Anti-Turing Operator framework, establishing the deterministic resolution of the P vs NP problem via continuous-time Liquid Time-Constant (LTC) Neural ODE dynamics. This archive constitutes Volume 2 (Formal Verification & Machine-Checked Hardening), providing the mathematical proof logs that secure the analytic foundations laid in Volume 1 (July 2026, DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21187095). Key Features & Formal Architecture:1. Lean 4 Deductive Kernel: Clean 0 sorry and 0 custom axiom implementation of LTC state manifolds (VectorFieldLTC), adaptive time-scales (tau_LTC), and the Asymptotic Bypass Operator (bypass_selector). Proves the continuous_embedding_upper_bound theorem, demonstrating that continuous LTC energy strictly truncates and dominates the discrete exponential state-space expansion 2^n for massive scales (n >= 100).2. Z3 SMT Tribunal: 2 automated verification batches operating under QF_NRA (Quantifier-Free Non-linear Real Arithmetic) constraints. The engine systematically returns an absolute UNSAT verdict, proving that exponential time inflation is logically inconsistent within the continuous-time differential manifold.3. Standalone Toolchain: Complete package encapsulation featuring pre-configured lakefile.lean and lean-toolchain pinned directly to Lean v4.33.1 for deterministic, machine-independent build replication. Package Contents:- lean4_kernel/AntiTuringCore.lean — Standalone formal Lean 4 verification core paths (0 sorry).- z3_tribunal/anti_turing_tribunal.py & anti_turing_batch2.py — Python Z3 SMT constraint gates for automated logical tribunals (ALL UNSAT).- exports/research_paper.tex — Production-grade LaTeX manuscript ready for formal academic submission.- exports/WORKSPACE_STATE.md & CONSOLIDATION_REPORT.md — Verification telemetry manifests and integrity freeze records. Framework formalization within the ALMIGHTY sovereign computational architecture.Architect: Muhammad Aidil Amry (Independent Researcher | ORCID: 0009-0002-9718-9710)Law: [UNSAT = KILL]

title: Cevahir AI: Living-Learning Research Reports and Technical Book
abstract: Versioned open-source research archive by Muhammed Yasin Yılmaz. Contains nine individually identified research reports/preprints (CEV-2026-01 through CEV-2026-09), reproducible computational experiments, preserved negative results, the Cevahir implementation, and a twelve-chapter Turkish technical book with an English reading guide. The research asks how experience during operation can persistently, controllably and generalizably change a system's future computation and behavior. Studies examine experience-conditioned computation, representation search, persistence and transfer, credit assignment, learning-state transport, learned updates, recurrent-state acquisition, correction, and future-query state requirements. The general living-learning problem remains open. The newest finite audit enumerates 61,575 histories and checks 712,632 content-informed label writes and 358,020 appends. Full records and limitations are included. These reports have not undergone external peer review. AI assistance was used for code, computational experiments, literature review and drafting. DOI registration identifies this archived version; it does not certify scientific correctness or establish novelty. Start at docs/publications/README.md for the reports and docs/book/README.md for the book. This DOI covers the collection and code together, not separate DOI registrations for each report. This second archive edition expands book chapters 3-6 with neural-network and embedding foundations, attention and Transformer mathematics, training methods, original-paper citations, dated industry comparisons, and solved exercises. Seven reproducible CPU example groups use actual Cevahir components; 99 selected neural-core, attention, MoE and training tests passed. This is an evolving educational manuscript, not a claim that every chapter is complete. The nine research reports retain their original findings and source records. This third archive edition expands chapters 7-9 with checkpoint identity and resume, generation mathematics and cache, memory retrieval and tool orchestration: 15 new solved exercises and ten additional executed CPU example groups. It corrects calculator expression truncation found during code review, preserving the original negative observation. Seventy selected generation, agent, checkpoint and runtime tests passed. The book now contains 12 chapters, 115 second-level headings and 64 third-level headings; it remains an evolving manuscript. This fourth archive edition adds the first broad living-learning campaign: 200 catalog propositions, 48 executable conditional comparisons, 3,456 paired outcomes, full discovery and confirmation records, source hashes, and negative controls. Thirty claims were supported, nine contradicted and nine inconclusive under a fixed synthetic rule; 152 catalog entries remain queued. The general problem remains open and the results have not undergone external peer review.

title: ZeroForward: Eliminating Atom Enumeration in Closed-Form Supervised Learning
abstract: Least-squares supervised learning is the static instance of ZeroFold: policy evaluation with discount γ = 0 and identity transition. Substituting these values collapses the Bellman equation to a single projection, and the three nested infinite operations that ZeroFold eliminates algebraically degenerate into two finite but large enumerations: forming the N × H feature matrix, and enumerating the atoms of the empirical measure, which for a length-n context window are the observed n-grams. Both are conventionally reduced by reading less of the data — local windows, factorized or Markov reference measures — which buys computation with discarded information. We eliminate both without approximation. When each feature is a product of per-position functions, the Gram entry G_ij is shown to be an exact contraction of the marginal count table on the union of the two supports, obtained by reassociating the sum rather than truncating it; in a character basis it is one discrete Fourier coefficient of that table, so every entry sharing a support is produced by a single FFT. The H² factor disappears from the data pass, and the residual cost tracks the Hartley entropy of the marginals actually read rather than the volume of the data. Measurements on Tiny Shakespeare: assembling G and b for an order-1 character dictionary (H = 513) drops from 24.3 s to 0.8 s (2.6×10¹¹ to 1.7×10⁸ FLOPs) with a maximum entry difference of 1.1×10⁻¹⁴ and no change in accuracy, whereas closing the Gram with a factorized or uniform reference measure costs 2.5 and 13.0 accuracy points respectively. Against a standard transformer baseline we introduce a phase-linear attention whose features satisfy the product condition; trained identically it matches the baseline (0.4819 vs. 0.4773), and solved exactly it reaches 0.4408 using 8–22× fewer FLOPs at matched accuracy, 26–200× fewer at matched H, with zero training tokens. The approximation ledger inside the pipeline reduces to one entry, the span; cross-entropy and softmax attention are shown to fail for a common reason, division by an input-coupled normalizer. Finally, defining the corpus as an order-p chain environment restores the horizon, absorbs the Markov quotient (559,503 contexts into 4,225 states), and recovers targets that context-indexed supervised regression cannot learn at any sample size.

title: PROSE: A Theory of Optimal Stopping with Perishable Evidence for Peer Selection in Intermittently Connected Decentralised Learning
abstract: Decentralised federated learning removes the aggregation server but makes collaboration dependent on transient peer availability. In mobile and intermittently connected systems, evaluating a promising peer consumes contact time and may cause the exchange opportunity itself to vanish, so that the evidence a learner gathers about a peer is perishable: it decays because links expire and because peer models drift while old measurements age. This paper develops a self-contained theory of optimal stopping for the resulting peer-selection problem. We formalise a receiver's within-contact decision as a finite-horizon Markov optimal-stopping problem with costly information acquisition and a future-arrival outside option, and prove that it admits an optimal policy characterised by a reservation value (Snell-envelope structure). Around this formulation we prove: (i) stage-uniform, drift-aware concentration and a maximin certification rule that is correct with high probability together with a finite-sample identification bound; (ii) a mobility-aware value of-information stopping rule and comparative statics showing that higher link hazard lowers the value of continued probing and enlarges the stopping region; (iii) a closed-form value of waiting under marked-Poisson contact arrivals, together with a search-theoretic reservation value whose comparative statics we characterise; and (iv) a myopic-optimality theorem establishing that, in sufficiently volatile (monotone) mobility regimes, the one-step confidence-safe rule is a sound surrogate for the optimal policy and never stops prematurely. We instantiate the theory as PROSE (Perishable-evidence Reservation-value Optimal Stopping for Exchange), a lightweight, fully local policy, and delineate the static contact and drift-free limits in which classical sequential decision problems are recovered. The development is entirely analytical.

title: Cascading Multi-Agent Architectures for Multilingual IT Support: Integrating Explainability and Dynamic Workload Optimisation
abstract: Modern IT helpdesks increasingly need to support multiple languages while staying transparent and resistant to hallucination, yet most deployed chatbots still rely on single-model architectures that struggle on both counts. This paper presents NexaServe v2, a four-tier cascading multi-agent IT helpdesk system combining retrieval-based response, LLM validation, LLM fallback, and human escalation, alongside a hybrid multilingual classification pipeline, confidence-gated routing, and workload-aware ticket assignment. The system is evaluated on a public Kaggle multilingual helpdesk dataset (n = 28,587 tickets), 89 logged chatbot interactions, and operational logs collected during development and testing. Fine-tuning mBERT on combined English-German data reached 89.84% category accuracy, while an English-trained classical model applied to translated German priority tickets dropped from 77.70% to 57.23% accuracy, a much steeper decline than the equivalent category-classification result. The chatbot cascade maintained a low factual hallucination rate (2.7% on a 75-message held-out batch) despite rejecting 93.3-100% of retrieval-layer responses as insufficiently confident. An AI-based workload supervisor, despite generating fluent and specific justifications for its decisions, performed no better than a simple deterministic heuristic and violated its own explicit numerical rule in every recorded overload flag. These results demonstrate that a transparent, near-zero-marginal-cost multilingual helpdesk is achievable using local LLMs for classification and cascaded response generation, while showing that LLM-based supervision does not reliably outperform deterministic alternatives for tasks with strict, checkable correctness criteria.

title: Explainable Fuzzy Learner Modelling and Learning Analytics for Human-Centered Teacher Decision Support: A Vocational Education Case Study
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based educational systems increasingly support personalised learning, adaptive feedback, and learning analytics. However, these capabilities are often addressed separately, with comparatively less attention paid to their integration into interpretable, teacher-facing decision-support frameworks. This study presents the e-Teacher Assistant, a human-centred educational framework that integrates xAPI-style Learning Record Store (LRS) analytics, dynamic learner modelling, Sugeno-type fuzzy inference using interpretable IF-THEN rules, adaptive learning support, and a dual Student Model-Teacher Model architecture. The framework was evaluated during a three-month authentic deployment in a vocational education Computer Networks course involving 117 learners and four educators. Learner evaluation combined a structured questionnaire, open-ended responses, and LRS-based behavioural analytics, while educators evaluated the Teacher Model through a questionnaire and qualitative responses. Learners reported predominantly positive perceptions of the system, including ease of use (92.3%), usefulness of feedback (95.7%), helpful interaction with the AI Assistant (94.9%), support for independent learning (88.0%), and support for educators through learning analytics (87.2-88.0%). Fairness and objectivity were also evaluated positively by 86.3% of learners. All four educators evaluated the Teacher Model positively, and all strongly agreed on its overall usefulness and its support for progress monitoring. Prior familiarity with digital learning tools was significantly associated with evaluations across all seven questionnaire dimensions. LRS analytics further documented learner engagement, repeated assessment activity, and contextual AI use; AI-assisted examination support was recorded in 64.42% of learner-chapter records. Overall, the findings provide initial empirical support for the feasibility of integrating interpretable learner modelling, adaptive AI-assisted support, LRS-based learning analytics, and teacher-facing decision support in an authentic vocational education setting while preserving educator oversight and pedagogical responsibility.

title: MULTIVARIATE ANALYSIS OF METEOROLOGICAL REGIMES AND SOLAR IRRADIANCE VARIABILITY IN DOSSO, SAHELIAN NIGER: IMPLICATIONS FOR PHOTOVOLTAIC APPLICATIONS
abstract: Solar irradiance in the Sahel covaries with several meteorological variables, making pooled bivariate correlations vulnerable to seasonal confounding. This study characterizes the joint meteorological structure associated with daytime global solar irradiance in Dosso, Niger, using field observations from May and August 2021. Sixty-two daily records were derived from hourly measurements of irradiance, ambient temperature, relative humidity and wind speed. After quality control, Pearson correlations were evaluated for the pooled dataset and separately by month; standardized variables were then analyzed using principal component analysis (PCA) and k-means clustering. Mean irradiance decreased from 822.75 W m⁻² in May to 651.52 W m⁻² in August, while mean temperature decreased from 38.23 to 29.85°C and relative humidity increased from 35.96 to 74.15%. Across all 62 days, irradiance correlated positively with temperature (r = 0.658) and negatively with relative humidity (r = -0.611), but the within-month relationships differed markedly. The first two principal components explained 91.28% of total standardized variance. PC1 (64.24%) represented a hot-dry-high-irradiance versus cool-humid-low-irradiance gradient, whereas PC2 (27.04%) was dominated by wind speed. A two-cluster k-means solution achieved a silhouette coefficient of 0.469 and separated all May observations from all August observations. The separation describes two sampled seasonal regimes rather than a universal climatic classification. The results demonstrate that season-aware multivariate analysis provides a more defensible interpretation of short solar-resource records than pooled single-variable correlations and can guide the selection of representative meteorological scenarios for photovoltaic studies in data-sparse Sahelian regions.

title: Radial Coarse Graining Restores Vacuum Majorization in Wigner Phase Space
abstract: Quantum uncertainty limits how strongly Wigner functions can concentrate in phase space. It is commonly conjectured that the vacuum Wigner function continuously majorizes that of any Wigner-positive state. However, by constructing Wigner-positive states whose localized quantum coherence lowers their Wigner entropy below the vacuum value, we show that this conjecture is incorrect. We restore vacuum majorization at finite resolution by integrating single-mode Wigner functions over concentric radial energy shells, obtaining probability vectors majorized by that of the vacuum for all Wigner-positive states and for Wigner-negative states with non-negative shell weights. Anchoring these shells to a fixed oscillator frame breaks affine symplectic invariance, rendering this relation strict for every non-vacuum Gaussian pure state. For Wigner-negative states, the persistence of negative shell weights defines a radial negativity scale with Airy-edge semiclassical asymptotics for highly excited Fock states. Operationally, we combine the majorization relation with partial transposition to obtain a two-mode entanglement criterion directly evaluable from radially binned joint homodyne outcomes without state reconstruction.

title: Det‐ LIME : Detector‐Aware, Multi‐Instance Local Interpretable Model‐Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite the rapid uptake of black‐box object detectors in marine mammal research and monitoring, explainability techniques are rarely integrated into conservation workflows. Furthermore, most classification‐oriented explainability tools are ill‐suited to detection tasks involving imagery of social organisms or those with colonial life histories, as they ignore multiple detections within a scene and produce single‐instance outputs that blur evidence across individuals. These methods also generate low‐resolution, often biologically irrelevant visuals, limiting their utility for debugging, targeted data augmentation, and refined data collection. We proposed Det‐LIME, a detector‐aware, multi‐instance adaptation of Local Interpretable Model Agnostic Explanations (LIME) that produced instance‐specific, box‐aligned explanations by combining per‐detection weighting, a proximity kernel that emphasizes regions near each box, and Intersection‐over‐Union‐based matching to track the same instance across perturbations. We evaluated Det‐LIME on aerial drone imagery for harbor seal detection, with an additional seabird case study to assess generality, and compared it with vanilla LIME, Stabilized LIME, Deterministic LIME, and gradient‐based attribution methods. Using the Attribution Ratio and Max Saliency Hit Rate metrics, we showed that Det‐LIME consistently improved multi‐instance attribution. In practice, these higher‐resolution, instance‐aware explanations provide insight into model outputs and support postprocessing, debugging, and actionable improvements in modeling and data collection or augmentation.
