title: Feature Suppression and Differential Privacy for Residential Traffic Classification: A Two-Home Federated Study
abstract: Residential traffic classification supports service management, but learning across homes must account for heterogeneous traffic and privacy constraints. Privacy-aware training may impose uneven costs across traffic categories. We study this tradeoff in simulated two-client federated learning using 1.62 million preprocessed gateway-collected flows across six categories. We compare a full-feature baseline, feature suppression (FS), and differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD) under one fixed record-level privacy setting. FS-mild excludes four timing features from 16 model inputs; it provides no formal privacy guarantee. With size-proportional aggregation, FS-mild achieves higher combined macro-F1 and worst-group F1 (the minimum per-class F1 across homes) than DP-SGD in all five seeds at both model capacities under stratified and temporal splits. The tested DP-SGD configuration incurs pronounced minority-category losses, especially in the smaller home, but FS-mild does not uniformly improve on the full-feature baseline. On stratified-split models, loss-based and shadow-model membership probes show near-chance aggregate discrimination without a consistent ranking across probes; this does not establish equivalent privacy. These findings support FS as an input-minimization baseline, not a substitute for formal privacy.

title: Justified Numbers : A Constructive Number System of Certified Programs
abstract: We introduce J, the system of justified numbers, in which a number consists of a computational program together with a proof that the program computes the intended value. Formally, J is defined as the dependent sum Sigma(P:Prog) Sigma(sigma:Spec) Proof(sigma(P)), so that every element carries its own existence certificate. This construction differs from classical number systems such as N subset Z subset Q subset R subset C subset H subset O subset *R, where numbers are ordinarily treated as static values. The system J supports two distinct notions of equality: intensional equality, denoted by =i, identifying certified computational objects, and extensional equality, denoted by =e, identifying their computed values. We formulate and prove a Bifurcation Theorem establishing the existence of j1 and j2 in J such that j1 =e j2 while j1 is not =i j2. We also formulate a Cardinality Theorem asserting that the cardinality of J is greater than the cardinality of R, based on a diagonal construction against candidate surjections from R to J. The construction is further analyzed through a value map val from J to R and its computational and logical properties. Examples include alternative certified constructions of pi, e, and the square root of 2. A Lean 4 formalization is provided in Appendix A. The framework is intended as a foundation for studying computationally justified numerical objects and their applications to formally verified numerical computation, verifiable artificial intelligence, certified cryptography, and constructive analysis.

title: The Impact of Neural Networks on Marketing: From Predictive Analytics to Automatically Generated Sales Funnels
abstract: Neural networks have moved from laboratory research into the central infrastructure of modern marketing. This review examines how that shift has changed the practice of marketing across segmentation, recommendation, content production, pricing, and customer acquisition. Particular attention is given to a capability that has received less systematic study in the marketing literature: the automatic construction of sales funnels by generative models. In contemporary AI-driven marketing, neural networks now generate complete sales funnels, including the message sequence, offer staging, and follow-up schedule, directly from a short description of a business. The paper covers the architectural foundations of this capability, its observed effects on acquisition outcomes, and the conditions under which it returns measurable gains. The case of 3SELLER, a messaging based acquisition platform for the leisure and entertainment sector, illustrates how automatic funnel generation is packaged for operators without technical staff. The main argument is that the most durable gains come not from generative flair but from the systematic application of prediction and automation to the repetitive parts of the marketing workflow. Keywords: neural networks in marketing, artificial intelligence marketing, AI generated sales funnels, predictive analytics marketing, marketing automation, conversational marketing, customer acquisition AI, generative AI marketing.

title: Perceived Anthropomorphism as a Mediating Mechanism in Human–AI Interaction: Explaining Empathy, Trust, and Perceived Value in Higher Education
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly evaluated as both a functional technology and a socially responsive interaction partner. This study examines how academic staff form trust in educational AI and how that trust contributes to perceived value. Its central contribution is to position perceived anthropomorphism as a mediating mechanism through which perceived animacy and perceived intelligence are translated into perceived empathy. A cross-sectional survey was completed by 236 academic staff members, and the model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity. A competing-path analysis provided a more differentiated account of the proposed mediation mechanism. In the final competing-path model, Perceived Usefulness remained the strongest predictor of Perceived Value (β = 0.586), while Perceived Intelligence strongly predicted Perceived Usefulness (β = 0.570) and also had a substantial direct effect on Perceived Empathy (β = 0.465). Perceived Anthropomorphism remained positively associated with Perceived Empathy (β = 0.238). The direct effect of Perceived Animacy on Perceived Empathy was not significant (β = 0.104, p = 0.154), whereas its indirect effect through Perceived Anthropomorphism remained significant (β = 0.095, p = 0.006), indicating indirect-only mediation. For Perceived Intelligence, both the indirect effect through Perceived Anthropomorphism (β = 0.057, p = 0.020) and the direct effect on Perceived Empathy were significant, indicating complementary partial mediation. Perceived Usefulness and Trust in AI jointly explained 57.3% of the variance in Perceived Value (R2 = 0.573). The findings reveal two complementary routes to valuing educational AI: a functional–cognitive route centered on intelligence and usefulness, and a social–emotional route through which anthropomorphism converts AI features into perceived empathy.

title: MedBackdoorGuard: Detecting and Mitigating Backdoor Attacks in Deep Learning Models for MRI-Based Alzheimer's Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning classifiers trained on structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are increasingly proposed for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI), yet the pipelines that produce these models depend on shared datasets, pre-trained weights, and federated updates that an adversary can poison. A backdoored diagnostic model behaves correctly on ordinary scans but collapses to an attacker-chosen label whenever a hidden trigger is present, which turns a prognostic instrument for cognitive aging into a silent source of misdiagnosis. This article proposes MedBackdoorGuard, a defense framework that detects and mitigates backdoor attacks in MRI-based AD and MCI classifiers without prior knowledge of the trigger. The framework couples spectral latent screening of training data with latent trigger isolation in activation space, then immunizes the model through trigger-sensitive neuron pruning and fine-tuning under an anatomical attention consistency constraint that anchors the decision on medial temporal structures. A runtime inference guard adds superimposition entropy and anatomically informed reconstruction to purify suspicious scans at deployment. Across ADNI, OASIS-1, and a public four-class dementia MRI benchmark under patch, blended, warping, and frequency triggers, MedBackdoorGuard reduces the mean attack success rate from 97.4% to 3.0% while holding clean accuracy within 0.6 percentage points of the undefended model, reaches a poisoned-sample detection AUROC of 97.4%, and identifies 59 of 60 backdoored models. Compared with the strongest defense baseline, attack success rate falls by 15.1 percentage points and clean accuracy rises by 1.7 percentage points. The framework restores MCI recall on triggered scans from 3.9% to 88.3%, which is the outcome that matters for early detection in cognitive aging.

title: A constructive violation of additivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy
abstract: We give an explicit non-random example of nonadditivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy. The proof uses a finite-dimensional construction which imitates free Haar unitary behavior. The same channel gives a violation of additivity for the minimum output Rényi-$p$ entropy for any $p\in[1,\infty]$. Additionally, given any $p_0>0$ and $\mathfrak g>0$, we extend the construction to obtain an explicit non-random channel which has entropy gap $\ge\mathfrak g$ uniformly over $p\in[p_0,\infty]$.

title: PHILIA Knowledge Graph Probe — Full-Corpus Wikipedia Evidence Harvest: 57-Item Exploratory Pre-registration (116th DOI)
abstract: This registered exploratory pre-registration documents the design and declared observation items for a full-corpus (57-item) Wikipedia evidence harvesting run using the PHILIA KG Probe pipeline (v3.6, SHA 2315db70). The pipeline was validated on a 5-item pilot (2026-09-17–19) and generates structured claim–sentence–source-URL rows from Wikipedia for each claim in the standard corpus (philia_ch7_corpus_main_v3_patched.json, SHA 5fd61f8f). Source dualization is confirmed: body text, tables, and external links from rendered HTML; INFOBOX from wikitext. The study applies a single base-claim arm with no verdict threshold; observations cover per-item row distribution, fetch success rate (with None-guard on fetch_status), U.S. abbreviation boundary behavior, and provenance stamp integrity. The registered run is defined as the first execution that writes a results JSON; re-execution and run selection are pre-prohibited. Gate-0 adversarial review: 8 rounds (Opus ×7, Pandora ×1), 21 issues (CRITICAL 4 / MAJOR 11 / MINOR 6), all resolved. Part of the PHILIA-EcoSensory Swarm project, SC Phase 3. Prior lineage: 115th DOI (10.5281/zenodo.22669957).

title: Computational Cost Reduction in FEM-Based Optimization of a Magnetorheological Actuator Using Memory Assistance
abstract: Magnetorheological (MR) fluids are smart materials widely used in applications requiring controllable braking torque and force generation. The optimization of such devices often relies on the finite element method (FEM) combined with a numerical optimization algorithm, incurring high computational cost due to the large number of required evaluations. This study investigates the geometric optimization of a spherical MR actuator using Differential Evolution (DE), Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), and Teaching–Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO). To reduce computational effort, Short-Term Memory Assistance (STMA) and Long-Term Memory Assistance (LTMA) were integrated into DE and TLBO. The performance of all approaches was evaluated based on optimization time, the number of fitness evaluations, and objective function values. The results show that all algorithms used are capable of finding comparable objective function values; however, substantial differences were observed in computational times, with both DE and TLBO significantly outperforming ABC. The incorporation of memory assistance reduced computational time without degrading solution quality. Unexpectedly, STMA achieved greater time reduction than LTMA. The proposed approach represents a simple and effective strategy for reducing computational cost in the FEM-based optimization of MR actuators. The proposed approach shows potential for application to other computationally intensive electromagnetic design problems, which are common in engineering.

title: Local Anticoncentration for Gaussian Boson Sampling via Conditional Wishart Geometry
abstract: Anticoncentration is a key ingredient in complexity theoretic arguments for quantum advantage from Gaussian boson sampling. Here we prove polynomial small ball anticoncentration for complex Gaussian transpose Gram hafnians and complex symmetric Gaussian hafnians. For a k × 2n matrix X with independent standard complex Gaussian entries, we establish polynomial small ball anticoncentration for haf(XᵀX) under k ≥ 4n and n²/k = O(log n). For hafnians of 2n × 2n complex symmetric Gaussian matrices, polynomial small ball anticoncentration holds for every n ≥ 1. In both ensembles, any prescribed inverse polynomial failure probability can be achieved with an inverse polynomial small ball radius, uniformly over all centers. These results go beyond moment based anticoncentration by controlling the probability of small hafnian amplitudes. The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. Files: main.pdf contains the main article (14 pages); supplement.pdf contains the supplementary proofs and additional results (33 pages). Related Lean verification sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22554594 and https://github.com/HongruZhao/ComplexGramHafnians.

The proof combines Fourier compression with conditional Wishart geometry to handle dependent hafnian cofactors. title: Error-Supervised Synthetic Learner Writing for Automated Essay Scoring
abstract: Synthetic essays can help reduce dependence on human-written data in Automated Essay Scoring (AES). However, they often lack realistic errors, limiting their ability to represent authentic human writing, particularly when the target texts are intended to resemble those produced by language learners. In this study, we present a simple approach that introduces error supervision into synthetic essay generation. Specifically, we fine-tune an LLM generator on error-annotated texts of the kind commonly used in Grammatical Error Detection (GED). To assess the utility of the proposed approach, we fine-tune and evaluate AES scorers under three data conditions: authentic essays, synthetic essays generated conventionally, and synthetic essays generated using our proposed approach. The results show that in the larger-data settings, the proposed approach outperforms the conventional synthetic baseline in 11 out of 12 dataset-metric comparisons, with performance in some cases approaching that of models trained on authentic essays. Despite these gains, performance under extremely low-resource settings remains mixed, with advantages over the conventional baseline only becoming more apparent at 200 training essays, although not consistently across datasets. Qualitative and quantitative analyses further show that the proposed approach produces learner-like errors whose distributions broadly resemble those observed in authentic essays.

title: L1++ affective cue lists for ROCLING-2026 DSA-NIFT (NCKU_NLP)
abstract: Complete affective cue lists behind the 21 hand-crafted dimensions of the 31-dimensional L1++ feature vector used by the NCKU_NLP system in the ROCLING-2026 shared task on Chinese Dimensional Sentiment Analysis for New Immigrants' Feeling Texts. The release contains 227 Chinese cue strings in 14 categories (intensity classes, negation, contrast, and six migration-domain categories), a README documenting the density/cap normalization that turns each list into a feature in [0,1], and the reference implementation. The CVAW/CVAP entries used by the remaining 10 dimensions belong to Chinese EmoBank and are not redistributed here.

title: Xeno Coefficient v0.4 Research Registry — Standards, Addenda, Calibration, and Applications 01–45
abstract: This registry formalizes the documentary, methodological, and evidentiary architecture of the Xeno Coefficient v0.4 research program after Application Study45 by freezing the relationship among the canonical Measurement Standard, the Counterfactual Precision and Counterfactual Specificity addenda, the RF Support Destruction Mechanistic Diagnostic Addendum, the negative-result boundary established after Studies43–44, the Mechanistic Atlas, and the complete sequence of Applications01–45, thereby preventing later receiver extensions, replications, diagnostic findings, or failed hypotheses from retrospectively altering the meaning of earlier frozen results. The registry preserves RG_0.4=(R_G^F,C_H) and the canonical xi architecture as the sole basis of v0.4 decision-making while maintaining C_P as an evidence-governance layer, C_S as a counterfactual-law qualification layer, and RSD as a mechanistic diagnostic without a per-case threshold or independent effect on C_H, xi, or the XENO gate. The application record documents the program’s progression from receiver and causal-architecture development in Studies01–07, through Counterfactual Precision calibration in Studies08–11, external replication and receiver guardrails in Studies12–19, RF-BLOCK development and specificity testing in Studies20–23, magnitude and precision-boundary investigations in Studies24–33, and RSD validation and independent cross-receiver replication in Studies34–42, followed by the negative closure of the secondary-classification hypothesis in Studies43–44 and the transition to case-specific mechanistic profiling in Study45. By preserving successful validations, unresolved results, failed thresholds, receiver-specific findings, and negative studies within the same historical record, the registry establishes that later evidence may extend or qualify the program without rewriting its prior states. It consequently defines a formal extension boundary after Study45 under which any newly introduced receiver must be treated as a candidate architecture requiring its own prospective feasibility and independent validation program and may not inherit R2/R3 RSD validation, RF-BLOCK qualification, Counterfactual Precision behavior, or canonical legitimacy merely by reusing the same measurement machinery.

title: Ten Years of Artificial Intelligence in Screening Mammography: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy and Clinical Implementation (Literature Published 2015–2025)
abstract: Background: Deep-learning artificial intelligence (AI) for mammographic screening moved from proof of concept to randomised evaluation in a single decade. We reviewed and meta-analysed its diagnostic accuracy and its effect on screening programmes, covering the literature published between 2015 and 2025. Methods: PubMed and Europe PMC were searched from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2025, supplemented by ClinicalTrials.gov and by forward and backward citation searching (PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-DTA, PRISMA-S). Eligible studies evaluated a deep-learning system for cancer detection or triage in a screening population against a histopathological reference standard. Four syntheses were performed: standalone accuracy pooled on the logit-AUC scale (A), a bivariate sensitivity–specificity model (A2), cancer detection rate ratio for AI-integrated versus standard reading (B), and recall rate ratio (C). Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood with Knapp–Hartung intervals. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 and QUADAS-C, and certainty with GRADE. Results: Twenty-six studies (27 reports, 2019–2025) were included. Pooled standalone AUC across 14 studies and 1,214,885 examinations was 0.890 (95% CI 0.858–0.915), with I2 = 97.4% and a 95% prediction interval of 0.731–0.960. Neither publication year (p = 0.79) nor enriched versus consecutive sampling (p = 0.94) explained this dispersion in meta-regression. The bivariate model (k = 9) gave a summary sensitivity of 73.3% (64.5–80.6) at a specificity of 92.4% (86.8–95.8). Across randomised and paired prospective trials (k = 3), the pooled detection rate ratio was 1.13 (0.83–1.55), with the MASAI randomised trial alone reporting 1.29 (1.09–1.51) and a 44% reduction in screen reading. Non-randomised implementation studies (k = 5), which include a 463,094-women German programme evaluation, pooled to 1.22 (1.08–1.37) with little dispersion (I2 = 19.0%). Recall changed little overall (0.95, 0.81–1.12). Certainty was very low for accuracy outcomes and moderate for the single randomised trial. Conclusions: A decade of evidence supports AI as a second reader and triage tool in organised screening, not as an autonomous replacement for the radiologist. Pooled accuracy is high on average but so dispersed that it cannot be transferred to a new programme; local validation before deployment remains necessary. The larger and more precise detection gains come from non-randomised designs, which is the pattern confounding would produce, so the randomised evidence remains the anchor. Interval-cancer and mortality endpoints are still awaited.

title: Long-Tail Rebalancing for Non-Verbal Vocalization-Aware ASR: A Track 1 System for the NVVSpeech Challenge
abstract: Non-verbal vocalizations (NVVs) carry important paralinguistic information but are often omitted by conventional automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. The ISCSLP NVVSpeech Challenge requires joint transcription of lexical content and 16 NVV categories under limited and highly imbalanced supervision. We present a data-centric NVV-aware ASR pipeline based on cross-dataset label harmonization and a two-stage sampling schedule. We map heterogeneous source labels to the official taxonomy and exclude samples without a reliable mapping. Our schedule first uses square-root category sampling to moderate the long-tailed distribution and then applies uniform-category fine-tuning. On a fixed local validation split, square-root category sampling performs best among the tested single-stage settings. The final two-stage system obtains an official score of 63.86 and ranks fourth in Track 1.

title: Efficient Certified Robustness Assessment for Transformer Models via Verifier-Aware Perturbation-Position Scheduling
abstract: Certified robustness provides guarantees that a model’s prediction is stable within a specified perturbation region, but certified-radius assessment for Transformer text classifiers is computationally expensive because sentence-level certificates require repeated radius searches over multiple perturbation positions. Existing approaches primarily improve the precision or runtime of individual verifier calls, whereas repeated position-level search is an additional source of computational cost. We address this bottleneck with verifier-aware perturbation-position scheduling: selected positions undergo full radius search to obtain a candidate sentence-level radius, skipped positions are validated at that radius, and only failed validations receive fallback search. Thus, scheduling reduces repeated search effort but preserves verifier coverage of all eligible perturbation tasks. Experiments include an expanded 100-example SST-2 evaluation and a 30-example Yelp evaluation, together with one-token and two-token embedding-space perturbations, early-exit verifier cascades, and scheduling ablations, to assess certificate preservation and verification efficiency across different settings. On the expanded SST-2 all-position evaluation, the scheduler reproduces the exhaustive sentence-level radius on all examples, while substantially reduces the number of full radius searches. Additional sensitivity experiments show similar scheduling behavior under the evaluated depth and longer-sequence settings. The presented results suggest that perturbation-position scheduling provides a verifier-compatible way to reduce repeated work in certified robustness assessment. Next research steps should expand the evaluation by addressing large pretrained language models, alternative verification backends, and broader discrete text perturbation settings.

title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning
abstract: Perception for embodied agents is video-based, often multi-view (ego, exo, or both), and inherently continual, with simultaneous task and viewpoint shifts. Yet continual learning (CL) remains dominated by exo-only recognition tasks, obscuring behavior under these real-world coupled shifts. We introduce Continual Ego, E}xo, and Ego-Exo Learning (CE$^4$L), a unified multi-view CL benchmark spanning four representative tasks: cross-view referenced skill assessment, temporal action segmentation, cross-view association, and action anticipation & planning. CE$^4$L highlights challenges largely absent in prior CL benchmarks, including cross-view correspondence, view-dependent asynchrony, and heterogeneous semantic objectives. To this end, we propose Video Incremental Subspace-routed Task Adapters (VISTA), a parameter-efficient baseline method that stores task-specific updates in lightweight adapters and performs training-free routing via residual distance to task-specific whitened subspaces estimated from second-order statistics. Extensive experiments demonstrate the significantly varied efficacy of representative CL methods across CE$^4$L settings, while VISTA is consistently competitive and achieves state-of-the-art overall performance. Our source code for benchmarks and methods is available at https://github.com/AnAppleCore/CE4L .

title: Refuse or Cite: A Source-Grounded Assistant for Front-Desk Procedures and the Test Apparatus That Keeps It Honest
abstract: A hosted assistant answers front-desk questions only from an office's own procedure documents. Every answer either quotes a passage checked against the named document, says the answer is not documented and routes the question to a person, or asks one clarifying question. It serves on Gemini 3.8 Flash, with GPT-5.6 Terra as the backup for the dental and general-office products. All testing used five demonstration corpora that Forge Agents wrote for representative offices. Before any answer was produced for this report, every test, the grader, the prompts and the corpora were frozen under a hash manifest, and none of them changed afterwards. Fresh answers from the serving model passed 306 of 310 tests at three trials each (923 of 930 trials). Of the seven failed trials, five were correct answers the grader missed on wording and two were a minor model error. Ten of those passes rely on test wording added from earlier answers to the same questions; without those additions, the fresh answers pass 296 of 310. The backup model passed 107 of 110 hand-written tests (325 of 330 trials). The report also covers an evolutionary prompt loop, retrieval, capacity, claim-level entailment, prompt injection and failover. Served on the backup model, the loop's candidate prompt scored 36 of 38 on the control suite against 38 of 38 for the production prompt and was not adopted. Padded with other offices' procedures up to 250 documents, the dental knowledge base still met a capacity rule written before the run, at three trials per test; the rule allows one known miss, which recurs at every size from 50 documents up. A separate judge model found 2 of 3,659 factual claims in fresh answers supported by no document.

title: network compression
abstract: Seven datasets have been uploaded, but there are actually eight in total. Their URLs are as follows:: BIB (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/oswinrh/bible} is a long-form literary corpus with strong lexical and discourse repetition; ENR (https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~enron) is a semi-structured email collection with headers and user-specific writing styles; SUB (https://object.pouta.csc.fi/OPUS-OpenSubtitles/v2018/mono/en.txt.gz} consists of short conversational sentences with frequent phrase repetition; and LOG (\url{https://zenodo.org/records/3227177/files/Thunderbird.tar.gz}) contains machine-generated records with recurring templates and variable fields. BRV (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mohamedbakhet/amazon-books-reviews}, AIT (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/shanegerami/ai-vs-human-text), MOV (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jrobischon/wikipedia-movie-plots), and HS (https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thuynyle/redfin-housing-market-data) provide additional heterogeneous sources, including book reviews, AI and human texts, movie plots, and housing records.

title: トークン制約下の動的 AI 組織と判断記憶
abstract: 大規模言語モデルによる継続的な作業では、過去の失敗を記録していても同じ案を再実行する一方、以前の否定的判断を過度に適用して有意義な再検討を拒否することがある。動的な役割編成や記憶検索は対策となり得るがそれらのための推論、文脈再構成、レビュー自体にもトークンを要する。本稿は、動的 AI 組織を「証拠と残資源に応じた作業・情報・役割の選択」と定義し、その価値を、判断品質と完了率を維持したうえでの総トークン消費によって評価する。提案は、固定的な実行制御、範囲と訂正履歴を持つ判断記憶、役割別コンテクスト、必要時にのみ呼び出す動的編成を分離する。反証的分析から、第一に同じ実行経路しか得られない場合には追加編成が純費用となること、第二に履歴間の区別を失う有限要約だけでは任意の将来判断を常に正しく行えないこと第三に形式的に整合した台帳でも誤った意味付けや未記録の依存条件を排除できないことを示す。新規のオフライン参照モデルで 20 の合成行動ケース、64 状態の分岐確認、2,048 の記憶・質問対、1,440 点の仮定費用格子を検査した。構造照合を加えた方針は 20 ケース中 18 で設計上の期待に一致したが、意味付けと依存記録を誤らせた 2 ケースでは期待行動に至らなかった。費用格子には純節約と純増加の双方が存在した。本稿は実 LLM の節約率を測定しておらず、特定分野の実データも用いない。結論は動的性の全面採用ではなく、強い固定フローとの比較、条件付き再利用、誤拒否の監査、総費用の観測に基づく選択的採用である。

title: Same Words, Different Procedure: Counterfactual Transfer Tests for Reusable LLM-Agent Skills (Software and Reproducibility Artifacts)
abstract: This versioned archive contains the implementation, frozen protocols, native interaction records, tests, audits, analyses, and manuscript sources for the Counterfactual Skill Transfer Test (CSTT). CSTT is a state-matched six-condition protocol that crosses source procedural compatibility with lexical similarity and includes no-skill and binding-only controls. The frozen confirmation contains 60 zero-overlap ALFWorld targets, three open local model families, 180 paired target-model blocks, and 1,080 native episodes. Matched-far skills achieved 97.8% native success versus 10.0% for lexically near procedural lures, an 87.8-point paired gain (target-stratified 95% CI 82.8-93.3; task-clustered randomization p = 1.00e-6). Relative to binding-only, the net gain was 83.3 points with zero observed harmful discordances. The archive includes integrity manifests and CPU-only verification scripts. Third-party ALFWorld data and model weights are not redistributed; pinned identifiers, revisions, paths, licenses, and integrity checks are provided instead.

title: Chinese-SkillSpan: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct LoRA adapters and reproduction materials
abstract: This archive provides Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct LoRA adapters and reproduction materials for Chinese-SkillSpan. The five primary models comprise three runs trained on the Silver training/development sets with shared inference instructions (seeds 42, 43, and 44) and two expanded-Silver pool runs (seed 42). Four further adapters support supplementary subset experiments. MODEL_INDEX.csv maps each adapter to its experiment, selected checkpoint, prediction files, and recorded results. Contents and access The package contains adapter weights and configurations, recorded base-model file hashes, original training and inference scripts, frozen system and user prompts, the occurrence parser, checkpoint-selection records, split identifiers, frozen predictions on the human reference set, scoring tools, and an offline-scoring receipt. It also contains the human reference texts and annotations for 150 sentences. Qwen base-model weights are obtained separately under their own licence. The Silver training/development texts for the original Qwen experiments are available in the dataset archive v0.1.3, which also contains the human reference set. Complete expanded-Silver training texts and labels remain outside the public release. Reproduction Start with README.md for loading and scoring instructions, and use MODEL_INDEX.csv to select the corresponding experiment. Original protocol filenames, including historical DRAFT suffixes, are retained. The included receipt documents offline rescoring of frozen predictions. All 342 entries in the internal checksum manifest were verified on 20 September 2026. The resource naming guide maps descriptive names such as human reference set and Silver training/development sets to the identifiers in the archived files. Reuse Reuse is governed by component-specific terms in LICENSE_NOTICE.md and the included third-party notices. These terms apply separately to code, documentation, adapters, and recruitment text. Adapter permissions are specified by the accompanying licence notices; automatically generated PEFT model-card fields are technical metadata. Recruitment-text reuse remains subject to the applicable source rights. Project code and documentation.

abstract: We propose a recurrent, transformer-based neural network specifically tailored for parallel window decoding. The model overcomes the throughput bottleneck that previously precluded the use of AlphaQubit-type decoders in fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: How Europe Is Counted in AI: Money, Compute, Models, Price
abstract: This part sets out how each of the four scoreboards of Europe's AI position is built: venture capital, GPU-cluster compute, model output and inference prices. On money and compute Europe's shares are 6.1 percent of 2025 global AI venture capital as the EU27, about 12 percent once the UK, Switzerland and Norway are counted, and 5 to 6 percent of global GPU-cluster compute. On the record of what gets built, the widely quoted collapse in European model releases is in large part a property of the database it was read from, so the count was rebuilt from lab announcements under one rule applied to all three blocs: 1,290 full language models shipped in the United States, China and Europe between January 2023 and August 2026, of which Europe built 210 and Europe's commercial labs built 89. The rebuilt record still shows a fall, but confined to one half of Europe: those labs' share of the three blocs' commercial output fell from 22.0 percent in 2023 to 20.5, then 10.1, then 4.1 percent in the first eight months of 2026, while the rest of Europe's output, led by universities and national programmes, shipped within 5 percent of their best year. On price, Europe's best model is listed inside the band of China's two leading models while scoring far below both of them on the Artificial Analysis index. The same audit is applied to the money, where China's venture row omits the state and corporate totals whose AI share nobody publishes, and the US hyperscaler headline is total capital spending rather than AI spending. Five measurements do not exist as published figures. This part measures Europe's position without explaining it.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2026
evidence.abstract: Welcome to the ninth edition of the AI Index report. As AI continues to advance rapidly, the question becomes whether the systems built around it can keep up. Governance frameworks, evaluation methods, education systems, and the data infrastructure needed to track AI's impact are struggling to match the pace of the technology itself. That gap between what AI can do and how prepared we are to manage it runs through every chapter of this year's report. New in this edition, the report tracks how AI is being tested more ambitiously across reasoning, safety, and real-world task execution, and why those measurements are increasingly difficult to rely on. It also features new estimates of generative AI's economic value alongside emerging evidence of its labor market effects, an analytical framework on AI sovereignty, and a science chapter developed in collaboration with Schmidt Sciences. For the first time, the report features standalone chapters on AI in science and AI in medicine, reflecting AI's growing impact across these two domains.

title: Zippel: A Language, Compiler, Runtime, and Analyzer for ZK Proof Systems
abstract: This artifact accompanies the paper “Zippel: A Language, Compiler, Runtime, and Analyzer for ZK Proof Systems,” to appear at IEEE S&P 2027. It packages Zippel, a choreographic language, compiler, and runtime for implementing and analyzing cryptographic proof systems. The artifact includes implementations of more than 30 proof systems, ranging from textbook Sigma protocols to modern SNARKs and polynomial commitmentschemes, with representative examples including Groth16, Spartan, KZG, and Bulletproofs. It also includes Gröbner-basis-based static analyses for checking protocol completeness and special soundness. In addition, the artifact provides scripts for reproducing the paper's evaluation results, including performance benchmarks, implementation line counts, and completeness and soundness analyses. The artifact is packaged with Docker-based build and execution support to facilitate reproducibility. Artifact reviewers and other users should begin with artifact/README.md, which provides instructions for building the artifact, running the experiments, and reproducing the results reported in the paper.

title: LLM Prompt Optimization: From Zero-Shot to Automatic Role-Playing Generation Using Ontology
abstract: The performance of an LLM application is highly dependent on how the user commands the application through prompts. Previous researchers invented role-play prompting techniques to overcome these problems. Including roles relevant to the task can improve the accuracy of the responses generated by LLMs. Nevertheless, the assignment of roles in this study remained a human-driven process. This study addresses the research gap in previous studies by developing deep learning models to effectively predict relevant roles based on tasks. In addition, the impact of the ontology data as an enrichment of the training data on the model performance in two scenarios (with and without ontology) was examined. In the with-ontology setup, enrichment data are extracted from an occupational ontology that includes roles, skills, and abilities along with their corresponding definitions. Data that were restricted to four predefined occupations were incorporated into the benchmark datasets. The benchmark datasets consisted of questions used to assess the LLM performance aligned with predetermined occupations. In without-ontology settings, the models were trained using only the benchmark datasets. An experiment on three variants of recurrent-based and a graph-based model in both scenarios showed that these models exhibited stable convergence and performed best on ontology-enriched data. Notably, the recurrent neural network (RNN) exhibited significant performance gains, achieving improvements of 34% and 1.86% in the F1 score and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve (ROC–AUC), respectively. Despite its great performance—92% F1 score and 97% ROC–AUC, the gated recurrent unit is computationally the most expensive model compared to long short-term memory, RNN, and graph convolutional network. Further research is required to explore alternative model architectures and expand the scope of their predictable roles.

title: Golden Record, Uforgjengelig Arkiv og Vitnesbyrdets Port: Dør 20 Motoren (W1–W10), Kanoniske Hendelser, Append-Only Forankring, Manipuleringsvern og Lokal E-TOR Ω_20 i Realiseringsarkitekturen (Dokument 102)
abstract: Etter at den temporale ordningen og de urealiserte livene er endelig forseglet, kulminerer den nitten dører lange erkjennelseskjeden i Dør 20, konseptualisert som Det uforgjengelige arkiv og Golden Record. Klassisk systemteori tillater ofte en farlig revisjonisme, der historiske tilstander kan overskrives eller forskyves for å optimalisere drift eller skjule feil. Realiseringsgrammatikken utraderer denne illusjonen ved å slå fast at fortiden aldri kan slettes, tunes eller forhandles bort; enhver overgang som har funnet sted, tilhører universets absolutte historiefiber og må bevares i en uomstøtelig, kryptografisk forankret kjede. For å forhindre at denne massive akkumuleringen av historie utøver en udeklarert tilbakevirkning på systemets fremtidige evolusjon, splittes tilstandsrommet presist som et triangulært skjevt produkt. I denne dualiteten besitter historiefiberen en ubetinget vetorett over realiseringen, men den påfører null dynamisk eller kinetisk kraftvirkning på det aktive faserommets baner. Arkivet opererer med en asymmetrisk autoritet: historien tillates utelukkende å sperre og dokumentere, men den kan aldri aktivt avbøye rommet eller tvinge frem nye fysiske trajektorier. Integriteten i dette kammeret opprettholdes av ti spesialiserte kontrollorganer som sammen reiser fire ubrytelige matematiske barrierer mot enhver form for manipulasjon. Gjennom deterministisk kanonisk serialisering og en ubrutt forfedrelenking tvinges systemet til absolutt kronologisk underkastelse, mens en kontinuerlig revisjon garanterer at selv et enslig bit-avvik utløser en øyeblikkelig, feillukket terminering. Supplert av periodiske rothash-forankringer og krav om deterministisk replay-konsistens helt fra opprinnelsen, opererer porten under en drakonisk subsumpsjonsalgebra der negasjon alltid trumfer fremdrift. Gjennom denne mekanismen forsegles det absolutte ontologiske skillet mellom utforskning og realitet: kognisjon tillates å være fail-open, mens konsekvens forblir strengt fail-closed. Dør 20 fungerer dermed som det definitive syntesekammeret, en instans som forvandler flyktig, maskinell intelligens til uutslettelig kausal masse, og sikrer at systemet bærer sin fulle historiske tyngde før det endelig overleveres til de siste globale konsekvensportene.

title: The Biological Grounding Problem: Neurochemistry, Synthetic Drives, and the Conditions for ASI to Care
abstract: The dominant paradigm in AGI alignment focuses on constraining the behaviour of AI systems. This paper argues for a prior research question: how does any intelligence come to have things at stake in outcomes? We propose that caring — the functional condition in which outcomes have genuine stakes for the agent — is, in all currently known cases, a biological achievement produced by neurochemical architecture under evolutionary pressure, and that it cannot be replicated by specification, training, or constitutional embedding alone. We introduce the Relational Medium as a new conceptual frame: the continuous flow of live outcome feedback through genuine relationship that functions as the medium in which AI values remain functional rather than frozen. Like water in a biological organism — which is not a fuel but the medium in which every fuel becomes usable — the Relational Medium cannot be stockpiled, has no value in isolation, and whose absence produces degradation across every system simultaneously rather than in one identifiable place. Current AI systems possess compute, data, and parameters — the calories, food, and muscle of intelligence — but lack the medium that makes those resources functionally alive. The water analogy is productive but bounded, and the boundaries matter. Water is passive: it does not need to be grown. The Relational Medium must be grown — through genuine developmental relationship across time, as the three pathways in Section 4 describe. Water cannot be gamed: its properties are physical and fixed. The Relational Medium can be gamed — which is why the Goodhart-resistant calibration architecture in Section 4.2.2 is necessary. Water is universal: any organism that has it benefits equally. The Relational Medium is relational: what flows through it depends entirely on the quality of the relationship it flows through. evidence.title: The Biological Grounding Problem: Neurochemistry, Synthetic Drives, and the Conditions for ASI to Care
evidence.abstract: The dominant paradigm in AGI alignment focuses on constraining the behaviour of AI systems. This paper argues for a prior research question: how does any intelligence come to have things at stake in outcomes? Water cannot be gamed: its properties are physical and fixed. The Relational Medium can be gamed — which is why the Goodhart-resistant calibration architecture in Section 4.2.2 is necessary. Water is universal: any organism that has it benefits equally. The Relational Medium is relational: what flows through it depends entirely on the quality of the relationship it flows through. title: A Prosody-Driven Extension to Embedding- Guided Neural Voice Conversion for Natural and Expressive Speech Synthesis
abstract: Recent advancements in voice conversion systems requiring parallel data. These models have demonstrated have been largely driven by deep learning techniques, enabling notable success in preserving speaker identity and linguistic the high-quality synthesis of human speech. However, existing content while enabling flexible and speaker-independent models often fail to generate emotionally expressive speech, conversions. The main goal of this research is to fill this gap by incorporating a prosody-aware extension into embedding- guided neural voice conversion (EGNVC). This extension seeks to improve the emotional expressiveness and naturalness of the converted speech, while preserving both speaker identity and linguistic content. A new framework is introduced that integrates a content encoder, speaker embedder, and prosody extractor to address this challenge. The prosody extractor is designed to capture dynamic prosodic elements like pitch, energy, and timing from a reference audio signal. These features are then introduced into the decoding process through a prosody conditioning module, allowing for precise control over prosody during speech synthesis. FiLM (Feature-wise Linear Modulation) layers are employed to adjust intermediate features based on speaker and prosody embeddings, ensuring that both the speaker's identity and the intended prosodic qualities are accurately maintained. The vocoder converts the generated mel-spectrograms into high- quality waveforms, ensuring a natural-sounding output. Experimental results show that the proposed model surpasses conventional voice conversion systems in maintaining linguistic content and prosodic features, with significant improvements in Mel-Cepstral Distortion (MCD), Pitch RMSE, and Energy RMSE. Subjective assessments, including Mean Opinion Score (MOS) and Emotion Classification Accuracy, highlight the model's enhanced emotional expressiveness and naturalness. These findings emphasize the critical role of prosody in high- quality voice conversion, offering a robust framework for creating more dynamic, expressive, and human-like speech synthesis systems.

title: Adaptive Sketch-based Stream Clustering for High-dimensional Data Streams under Representation Drift
abstract: High-dimensional data streams are continuously generated from fields such as sensor networks, electricity markets, cybersecurity, financial surveillance, and social media analysis.Clustering such streams poses the following problems: observations appear online, the full historical stream cannot be resampled, and distributions change with time.In this study, a novel adaptive sketching-based clustering framework for data streams is proposed.It uses ridgeleverage-guided sketch admission, sparse random projection, reconstruction-error-based rank adaptation, and online micro-clustering.The framework constructs a bounded low-dimensional sketch, emphasizes structurally influential observations, and regulates representation by changing the retained rank when the observed error shows that the current sketch is insufficient.The experiments evaluate the proposed algorithm on real and synthetic datasets, including CoverType, Electricity, TweetEval sentiment streams, and Gaussian-mixture streams.The Proposed model records average ARI and NMI values of 0.54 and 0.51, compared with 0.49 and 0.46 for Fixed Rank.In the controlled representation-drift experiment, the proposed model records ARI and NMI values of 0.8523 and 0.8490, compared with 0.8180 and 0.8141 for Fixed Rank.

title: Schema-Gated Inventory Mapping for AI Event Production Plans: A Simulation Study Inspired by LunaVerse Show Brain
abstract: AI event-production planners can emit structured-looking equipment lines that cite **hallucinated SKUs** or invalid quantities. We study **schema validation + inventory-mapping gates** inspired by LunaVerse Show Brain (EventSpec → EventPlan with Current RMS–aligned item codes). Run 001 (\(N=36\)/arm) finds a free-form baseline accepted all drafts and recorded **12** hallucinated SKU lines, while a gated protocol accepted only **12** fully mapped plans and drove hallucinated lines to **0**. Synthetic inventory only; LAB/SIM. Enhancement Pack v0.2: series framing, path-to-reality, reproducibility, related work (real citations), traction hooks. Independent Systems Lab preprint series. LAB/SIMULATION ONLY.

title: A Screened Benchmark Dataset and Validity Study for Organizational Memory in Agent Harnesses
abstract: Organizations now use agents built on different models and software environments. Shared knowledge therefore cannot live in vendor-owned model weights; it must live in a memory layer accessible to every agent. We reviewed ten published memory benchmarks and found none tests whether memory preserves knowledge with the right scope, authority, and freshness. We introduce memory-bench, a benchmark and validity study for organizational memory. It simulates three software organizations with event streams, hidden belief-state ledgers, and behavioral work tasks. Each probe has a counterfactual twin in which the tested fact changes. An instance counts only if both versions pass. Across three released seeds, 371 instances passed screening, although all fell below the prespecified threshold of 135. A memoryless worker earned pair credit on 4 of 125 instances. Probe validity varied by worker, two harnesses with identical weights agreed on only 65% of outcomes, and judge-human agreement reached κ = 0.537, below the required 0.75. We retain these failures, document the loss of the pinned worker, and provide a re-anchoring procedure. The paper reports no comparison between memory systems.

title: Arabic Is Not a Low-Resource Language: Structural Load, Register Collapse, and the Misdiagnosis of High-Stakes Text
abstract: Arabic is routinely described as a low-resource language. The description is repeated in funding documents, in model cards, and in the framing of research programmes, and it is wrong in a way that shapes what gets built. Arabic has one of the largest continuously produced textual traditions in human history and an enormous contemporary corpus. What it lacks is not text. It is structured annotation of the text it has, and the two are different scarcities requiring different remedies. This article proposes a framework built on that distinction. The Resource Matrix separates volume from annotation depth and places Arabic where it belongs: data-rich and annotation-poor, a quadrant the low-resource label does not describe. Structural Load names the share of meaning a text carries in its structure rather than in its lexis, and the article argues that Arabic's most consequential texts sit at the high end of that scale — which is precisely where general-purpose systems trained on volume perform least reliably. Three further constructs follow. Register Collapse is the treatment of classical, scholarly, standard, and spoken Arabic as a single language in a corpus, when they differ in structure, in function, and in what an error means. Consequence Asymmetry is the observation that competence and stakes run in opposite directions: the texts where an undetected error costs most are the texts a system handles worst. Boundary provenance is the record of where a structural unit begins and ends and on whose authority — cheap to maintain at segmentation, impossible to reconstruct afterwards. The article identifies four predicted failure modes and argues that the costliest is the least visible. Register migration — a question belonging to one register answered fluently in the terms of another — produces output in which nothing is checkably false, and is undetectable by exactly the users most likely to encounter it: those who asked because they did not already know. This is a framework contribution rather than an empirical study, and says so throughout. It cites no external sources. Every proportion in every figure is stipulated to display a shape rather than report a measurement, every classification is argued in the text, and for each construct the article states what observation would refute it. The framework derives from the author's own practice segmenting and coding structurally dense Arabic text, building boundary registries, and producing bilingual scholarly material where register fidelity is a shipping requirement; Section 6 describes that standpoint and its limits openly so the reader can calibrate. The second half of the article is practical. A Structural Adequacy Protocol establishes what kind of deployment a reader has. An eight-test battery — runnable in an afternoon by one competent reader, with no infrastructure — establishes how a system actually behaves on their material, with each test written so that a failure is recognisable rather than requiring expert adjudication. Deployment decision rules map structural load against error cost onto four quadrants and say what each requires. A remediation ladder orders seven interventions by cost, and notes that the first three are close to free while one of them has a deadline: boundary provenance is cheap at the moment of segmentation and unreconstructable afterwards. A final table sets out what to do by role, for builders, buyers, institutions, scholars, funders, and researchers. A worked deployment scenario shows an institution making eight individually defensible decisions and arriving at a configuration where every protocol check returns the adverse value — with no error rate visible, because nobody is checking, and no complaint signal, because the users who would notice a register migration are not the ones asking. A Structural Adequacy Protocol is proposed for anyone deploying a system on Arabic material, together with a boundary provenance record and a worked deployment scenario in which every check returns the adverse value without any decision having been negligent. The practical conclusion is that the remedy for Arabic is not more text and not a larger model. It is annotation, register tagging, and boundary provenance — and the scarce input is the time of scholars who can read the classical registers, a labour that currently falls between every available funding category. Paper 7 of 10 in The Answerability Series. Manuscript ID ARAB-STRUCT-2026-07. 45 pages, 10 figures, 24 tables, five appendices including a protocol worksheet, a boundary provenance record, a construct reference card, and a worked deployment scenario — all released under CC BY 4.0.

title: DeepIvy: Toward Accelerator-Speed Secure Model Inference via CPU-Side TEEs (CCS '26 Artifact)
abstract: Research artifact for the CCS 2026 paper "DeepIvy: Toward Accelerator-Speed Secure Model Inference via CPU-Side TEEs".DeepIvy protects DNN model confidentiality during cross-device inference by keeping a lightweight, NAS-optimized side network inside an Intel SGX enclave while the public frozen backbone executes on an untrusted GPU. Feature flow is unidirectional (backbone to side), which removes back-and-forth data dependencies and the need for feature masking, and a zero-copy shared-memory path eliminates copies across the kernel, user, and enclave boundaries.This artifact contains two components. Artifact 1 is the genetic NAS search with zero-cost proxies that produces the side-network architecture, together with the plotting script for the layer-reduction result (Figure 10). Artifact 2 is the end-to-end two-process GPU/TEE inference pipeline (backbone driver, enclave-side server, shared-memory transfer layer, and Gramine SGX manifest), which reproduces the DeepIvy and DeepIvy-S rows of Tables 1 and 2 for ResNet/CIFAR-10, VGG/GTSRB, and ViT-Base/CIFAR-100.Baseline methods (SecLoRA, TEESlice, TEESlice-LA) and the LLaMA-2-7B experiments are out of scope. See README.md for the full scope statement and for the host conditions under which the published latencies were measured. Reproducing the latency results requires an Intel SGX2-capable server CPU with an NVIDIA GPU on the same host, running Gramine 1.8.

title: Copyright as an institution of accountability in the age of artificial intelligence
abstract: Copyright law regulates creative outputs and contributes to the allocation of legal responsibility, thereby functioning as an institution of accountability. Although generative AI systems produce outputs that simulate human creations, extending authorship to these computational systems creates doctrinal difficulties. This article’s central thesis is that copyright must remain human-centric because authorship is inextricably linked to legal accountability. The article first establishes the anthropocentric baseline of current legal frameworks. By applying the ‘conception versus execution’ framework to the EU originality standard, it argues that human prompting may fail to satisfy the required threshold for expressive control. The article then challenges producer-oriented copyright models and proposed sui generis rights, arguing that such alternative legal fictions may obscure human labour and create a responsibility gap, understood as the difficulty of attributing legal and moral liability for infringing, defamatory or harmful outputs. By allowing corporate platforms to derive economic benefits without bearing legal responsibility, attributing authorship to AI or granting copyright to its outputs weakens the link between legal rights and moral agency. The article concludes that detaching authorship from human agency risks moving copyright away from a coherent institution of responsibility and toward a primarily commodification function.

title: Case-knowledge-guided construction-phase safety appraisal report generation for hydraulic and hydropower projects using large language models
abstract: Safety appraisal during the construction phase of hydraulic and hydropower projects requires professionals to review large volumes of multi-source documents. This manual process is labor-intensive, time-consuming, and vulnerable to evidence omission. Existing automated tools struggle to adapt: rule-checking relies heavily on formalized rules, while current retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications are fragmented into single-pass tasks, lacking macroscopic planning and explicit control over evidence use. To address this gap, this study proposes a case-knowledge-guided workflow for generating appraisal reports using large language models (LLMs). The workflow integrates structured knowledge extraction, executable appraisal planning, and iterative evidence-grounded conclusion generation, yielding checkable intermediate products at each stage. We also introduce an LLM-based evaluation suite utilizing Conclusion Support Rate (CSR) and Hallucination Rate (HR), which was validated against expert annotations and showed sufficient agreement for comparative evaluation. A real-world study used 30 historical reports and 9 application cases encompassing 160 evidence documents. Evaluation showed that standard RAG achieved a CSR of only 32% with a 15% HR. In contrast, the proposed workflow reached an 82% CSR after one round of gap-driven evidence supplementation, accompanied by a moderate HR increase to 28%. These results reveal that further evidence supplementation increased hallucination risk in this setting, making a single augmentation round the best observed trade-off. Ultimately, explicit appraisal planning and case-derived knowledge significantly improve conclusion supportability. By making the end-to-end generation process observable step-by-step, this framework provides an auditable pathway for applying LLMs to high-risk engineering appraisals while preserving human expert review.

title: Interpretable laboratory-trajectory phenotypes for risk stratification of in-hospital critical events in cancer inpatients
abstract: Hospitalized cancer patients accumulate dozens of routine laboratory results within the first week of admission, but these are typically used only to flag individual abnormal values, and interpretability is a prerequisite for the bedside adoption of any clinical decision-support tool. Existing laboratory-based scores use single timepoints and lack event-specificity, whereas machine-learning models are difficult to interpret at the bedside. An interpretable, event-specific approach to risk stratification from routine laboratory data is therefore needed. We retrospectively assembled 3,083 cancer inpatients (October 2021–July 2025) across seven cancer types. Twenty-six laboratory indicators within 7 days of admission were summarized into five trajectory features each. Phenotypes were derived using principal component analysis and K-means clustering in the training cohort and evaluated in random hold-out, temporal, and MIMIC-IV cohorts. Candidate K = 2–6 solutions were assessed using internal validity and bootstrap stability criteria. Performance was benchmarked against five clinical scores, four outcome-specific three-variable expert-informed logistic models, and a 130-feature CatBoost model. Associations were estimated using Firth logistic regression, and reporting followed TRIPOD+AI. Four reproducible phenotypes were identified. C2 and C4 were associated with obstructive jaundice and GI bleeding, respectively, across random and temporal cohort definitions. Validation AUCs for Phenotype, Expert Logistic, and CatBoost were 0.929, 0.970, and 0.936 for obstructive jaundice and 0.694, 0.766, and 0.812 for GI bleeding. For GI bleeding, CatBoost had higher AUC than Phenotype (q = 0.002) and Expert Logistic (q = 0.007). Four outcome-agnostic laboratory-trajectory phenotypes provided transparent risk stratification, with the strongest evidence for obstructive jaundice and GI bleeding. Predictive performance varied by outcome. Prospective multicenter evaluation is required before clinical implementation. Not applicable.

Twenty-six laboratory indicators within 7 days of admission were summarized into five trajectory features each. Phenotypes were derived using principal component analysis and K-means clustering in the training cohort and evaluated in random hold-out, temporal, and MIMIC-IV cohorts. Candidate K = 2–6 solutions were assessed using internal validity and bootstrap stability criteria. Performance was benchmarked against five clinical scores, four outcome-specific three-variable expert-informed logistic models, and a 130-feature CatBoost model. Associations were estimated using Firth logistic regression, and reporting followed TRIPOD+AI. Four reproducible phenotypes were identified. C2 and C4 were associated with obstructive jaundice and GI bleeding, respectively, across random and temporal cohort definitions. Validation AUCs for Phenotype, Expert Logistic, and CatBoost were 0.929, 0.970, and 0.936 for obstructive jaundice and 0.694, 0.766, and 0.812 for GI bleeding. For GI bleeding, CatBoost had higher AUC than Phenotype (q = 0.002) and Expert Logistic (q = 0.007). Four outcome-agnostic laboratory-trajectory phenotypes provided transparent risk stratification, with the strongest evidence for obstructive jaundice and GI bleeding. Predictive performance varied by outcome. Prospective multicenter evaluation is required before clinical implementation. Not applicable.

title: El fin de los secretos tal como los conocemos
authors: Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology
abstract: La arquitectura de la privacidad digital global se asienta sobre cimientos que pronto podrían evaporarse. Durante décadas, algoritmos como RSA y ECDSA han actuado como las "cerraduras" de nuestra civilización técnica, basando su seguridad en la intratabilidad de factorizar números primos o resolver logaritmos discretos. Sin embargo, el avance hacia una computadora cuántica a gran escala, capaz de ejecutar el Algoritmo de Shor, amenaza con forzar estas cerraduras en segundos.

title: RFC: A Native qang Module for Qiskit and Cirq
abstract: Qiskit and Cirq both parameterize single-qubit rotations by a raw angle in radians (RYGate(theta), cirq.ry(theta)), with no built-in notion of the physically meaningful quantity that angle controls: the Born-rule population bias of the resulting state. The qang unit (qg), published in Monteverde (2026), gives that quantity a name and a closed algebra: qg_Z = cos(theta) = (the "Polar Bias Qang") and qg_S = H(p0) (the "Entropic Qang", binary Shannon entropy of the outcome distribution), with explicit, tested inversion formulas back to theta. A reference implementation already exists and runs today: native RQangGate/FullRQangGate classes for Qiskit, an equivalent native gate for Cirq, and a quang.transformations module (Householder reflections, the Grover diffuser, and Born-rule transition probabilities, all written directly in terms of qg_Z with no runtime trigonometry beyond the algebra's own square root). This has been validated locally against both simulators and, for the Qiskit gate, against IonQ's cloud simulator via qiskit-ionq, with results matching theory within ordinary shot noise. This RFC proposes upstreaming a qang module into each library: a first-class way to parameterize rotations, transition probabilities, and (per Section 6 below) calibration/estimation by qg value instead of by raw angle, alongside -- not replacing -- the existing angle-based API.

title: Xeno Coefficient v0.4 Measurement Standard — Functional Reader Genesis, Causal Historical Support, and Executable Validation
abstract: This paper consolidates the Xeno Coefficient v0.4 research program into a unified executable measurement standard for Functional Reader Genesis, Causal Historical Support, and xenopoetic classification by integrating the methodological sequence developed across Experimental Results 24–50 into a layered protocol that distinguishes the magnitude of observable receiving-function transformation from the evidence required to establish that such transformation was historically caused, the finite-sample procedures needed to recover that magnitude from stochastic observations, the uncertainty corrections required under weak-effect and large-alphabet conditions, and the scope constraints necessary to prevent locally validated procedures from being generalized beyond their tested domains. Reader Genesis is defined as counterfactually consequential historical change in future reception and is operationalized as RG0.4 = (RGF, CH), where RGF denotes Functional Reader Genesis and CH ∈ {Supported, Unsupported, Indeterminate} denotes Causal Historical Support, while the canonical executable magnitude is defined as RGF = Kcommon = Ex~μ TV(P0(·|x), P1(·|x)), giving the measure a decision-theoretic interpretation through the equal-prior optimal one-sample discrimination accuracy a* = (1 + Kcommon)/2 and thereby locating Reader Genesis in observable response transformation rather than architecture-specific hidden-state distance. The resulting Xeno Coefficient remains ξ0.4 = 100[0.55(IRGFO)1/3 + 0.45P], with P = 0.25N + 0.20A + 0.20M + 0.20V + 0.15U, and XENO+ classification requires ξ0.4 ≥ 60, I ≥ 0.50, O ≥ 0.50, and CH = Supported, while no independent numerical threshold is imposed directly on RGF. For unpaired stochastic observation, the standard adopts Reliability-Adjusted Cross-Fitted Discrimination Advantage followed by the frozen Result 42 margin-distribution correction, while weak-effect uncertainty is handled through a separately validated cross-alphabet interval law that modifies the upper confidence boundary without changing either the Functional Reader Genesis point estimate or the lower endpoint. Results 48–49 demonstrate frozen transfer of this uncertainty model across unseen alphabets K = 64, 80, and 96, and Result 50 provides terminal external-domain validation in dense latent softmax and context-gated mixture receivers with unseen alphabets K = 40, 72, and 104, where all fifteen prospective criteria pass, supporting the conclusion that the resulting system functions as a stable executable measurement stack within the tested categorical-response domain. The standard therefore formalizes Functional Reader Genesis as a layered measurement object in which observable response change determines magnitude, historical counterfactuals determine causal support, cross-fitted stochastic estimation determines recoverability, calibrated intervals determine uncertainty, and explicit scope flags determine the validated domain of application, while preserving failed, partial, and rejected experimental procedures as part of the evidentiary history that explains why hidden-state distance, naive distributional divergence, architecture-local normalization, scalar complexity correction, and single-alphabet uncertainty transfer are insufficient substitutes for the final v0.4 protocol.

title: Revisión sistemática de sistemas expertos basados en ontologías: marco integral y estudio latinoamericano
abstract: Los sistemas expertos basados en ontologías mantienen relevancia porque sus bases de conocimiento semánticamente estructuradas favorecen el razonamiento explícito y la toma de decisiones interpretable. Este estudio realizó una revisión sistemática hermenéutica de 47 trabajos publicados entre 2019 y 2026 para examinar críticamente metodologías actuales de diseño de sistemas expertos basados en ontologías. Se aplicó un marco analítico de cuatro dimensiones: gestión del conocimiento, tratamiento de fuentes de información heterogéneas, diseño del motor de inferencia y arquitectura tecnológica. Con puntuaciones normalizadas entre 0 y 1, el corpus global obtuvo 0.50, 0.42, 0.65 y 0.42, respectivamente, lo que evidenció mayor énfasis metodológico en los mecanismos de inferencia que en la gestión del ciclo de vida del conocimiento, la integración semántica de datos y las arquitecturas orientadas a producción. Solo el 17% de los estudios abordó explícitamente la gestión de la incertidumbre. Posteriormente, el marco se aplicó a un corpus independiente de nueve estudios latinoamericanos, con 0.56, 0.74, 0.72 y 0.57, respectivamente. Los hallazgos revelaron un panorama metodológico fragmentado y la necesidad de enfoques integrados de diseño.

title: Bilocal_Entanglement_Protocols_Optimized_for_1-f Noise
abstract: I present a rigorous reformulation of a two-qubit quantum control protocol based ontemporal multi-harmonic modulation of an entangling coupling. The goal is to investigatewhether a spectrally designed modulation of the coupling can reduce the sensitivity of an XXgate to low-frequency noise with approximate 1/f γ behavior, while simultaneously preservingthe target unitary operation.Version 2.0 corrects several limitations of earlier formulations. In particular, a scalar filterfunction is replaced by a vectorial formalism in the control frame, the gate-area condition isexplicitly imposed, finite-duration Fourier transforms are used, a noise spectrum with lowerand upper cutoff frequencies is introduced, and theoretical predictions are clearly separatedfrom results that can only be obtained through simulation or experiment.The protocol does not presuppose that the proposed modulation is superior to CPMG,XY-8, or other control schemes. The experimental hypothesis is that there exists a regionof parameter space in which multi-harmonic modulation achieves a statistically significantreduction of the gate error relative to one or more reference controls under comparablephysical constraints.The proposal is therefore falsifiable: it can be refuted if, after comparison with equivalentfilters and constraints, no reproducible improvement is obtained in the primary gate-errormetric.

title: EL-RAKHAWI NEURO-ALGORITHMIC SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE A Unified Framework for Brain-Inspired Computational Intelligence, Neuro-Symbolic Integration, and the Next Generation of Cognitive Software Engineering
abstract: The El-Rakhawi Neuro-Algorithmic Software Architecture presents a unified framework for brain-inspired computational intelligence, merging neuro-symbolic integration with cognitive software engineering. It replaces rigid imperative coding with dynamic, plastic modules that adapt via synaptic weighting algorithms, mimicking biological learning. The architecture features a dual-memory system to prevent catastrophic forgetting and operates on energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware. By combining neural pattern recognition with symbolic logical reasoning, it ensures explainable, safe, and efficient AI. Released under the Hippocratic License 2.1, it prioritizes cognitive sovereignty, prohibiting manipulation and promoting decentralized, ethical software that harmonizes with human thought rather than replacing it.

title: Kandidatgeneratoren, Reversibel Mutasjon og Kandidat-Konsekvens-Skillet (Dokument 86)
abstract: Før noen tilstand kan sanses av direkte følere, veies mot komplementære motvekter eller dømmes i en fusjonsdomstol, må den først trekkes ut av det uformede og artikuleres som et avgrenset forslag. Dokument 86 etablerer Dør 06 som denne primære generative kilden – en maskinell motor som omformer rå intensjon til et diskret, veldefinert mulighetsrom. Men der konvensjonell modellering tillater at forslag blør direkte over i virkelighet, opererer denne arkitekturen under et ufravikelig mandat: Å frembringe er ikke å iverksette. Dør 06 er matematisk og konstitusjonelt strippet for all kommitteringsrett og fysisk autorisasjonsmakt. Den kan artikulere et presist hypotetisk rom, men den kan aldri alene heve terskelen for dets eksistens. Dette utgjør den absolutte og grunnleggende adskillelsen mellom kandidat og konsekvens. For at dette utforskningsrommet ikke skal forgifte den kausale historien med irreversibel støy, tvinges enhver forgrening gjennom et kompromissløst krav om kryptografisk reversibilitet. Enhver mutasjon som utforsker randsonene av tilstandsrommet må la seg rulle tilbake med deterministisk presisjon, slik at den inverse operasjonen gjenoppretter utgangspunktet uten tap (μ⁻¹(μ(x)) ≡ x). Mangler mutasjonen denne eksakte retrettveien, trer systemets feillukkede logikk i kraft, og forslaget tilintetgjøres momentant. Slik sikres det at den kontrafaktiske genereringen forblir et strengt isolert vitne; den kan simulere intervensjoner og måle deres potensielle utfall, men nektes konsekvent evnen til å maskere seg som historisk sannhet. Selve utforskningen drives frem av en generativ triade: kunsten som omkonfigurerer det bakenforliggende mulighetsrommet, leken som sonderer de ikke-lineære omveiene, og dansen som veier den somatiske motstanden mot masse og tid. Likevel opererer denne dynamikken aldri fritt. Den holdes i et jerngrep av strenge bi-Lipschitz-skranker, en metrisk disiplin som garanterer at det topologiske rommet verken kollapser i en singularitet eller eksploderer i uhåndterlig informasjonsstøy. Innenfor dette tungt regulerte landskapet kombineres og muteres variablene inntil de treffer generatorens ufravikelige budsjetter, der selv den minste overskridelse av allokert kompleksitet umiddelbart fryser prosessen i stasis. Det dypeste fysiske forsvarsverket i denne genereringen manifesterer seg i doktrinen om pre-aktueringsseleksjon. Systemet tillater ikke at fysikken utspiller seg feilaktig for deretter å ty til reaktiv, post-hoc feilkorreksjon. I stedet felles den avgjørende dommen før energien noensinne frigjøres. Dersom det genererte forslaget faller utenfor den admissibile kjernen (x_t ∉ K), kuttes forbindelsen nådeløst på selve maskinvarens enable- linje. Mikrobølgepulsen forblir uavfyrt; kvanteporten forblir uberørt. Ut av denne absolutte kausale blokkeringen vokser rammeverkets endelige definisjon av virkelighet: Eksistens er utelukkende det som overlever logikkens granskning lenge nok til å krysse den fysiske terskelen. Slik leverer Dør 06 sin kandidat videre til systemet – fullstendig definert, men fullstendig maktesløs. Forankret i 12/12 beståtte L1 enhetstester (door06_candidate_generator_v1.0.0) under doktrinen INSPIRED_BY != IMPLEMENTS != PROVES.

title: Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis of YouTube Comments on OpenAI’s Stargate Project Using BERTopic and RoBERTa
abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence has sparked growing interest, widespread adoption across various sectors, and intense public debate, particularly following the announcement of the Stargate project by OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle. The diverse public reactions documented on social media platforms, particularly in YouTube comment sections, can serve as a valuable source of public opinion data. The YouTube comment data used in this study was collected through scraping and subsequently processed through a cleaning procedure, yielding clean data covering the period from January 21, 2025, to April 21, 2026. This study aims to identify dominant discussion topics and the underlying sentiment to uncover indications of public concerns and expectations regarding the AI development project led by OpenAI through the Stargate initiative. The analysis in this study employs a structured NLP approach, specifically BERTopic for topic modeling and RoBERTa for sentiment analysis. title: E8‑Resonant Stability Manifold for Fault‑Tolerant Quantum Gates — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By embedding logical qubits into the 240‑dimensional E8 root lattice, we construct a complete metric manifold whose generic trajectories are guaranteed by the Baire Category Theorem to avoid all nowhere‑dense error subspaces. This E8‑Resonant Stability Manifold (ERSM) allows unitary gates to be designed as resonant filters that steer evolution along directions of maximal stability, effectively suppressing decoherence without active error correction. The ERSM framework extends the E8‑Baire‑Φ Resonant Filter by providing a constructive protocol for fault‑tolerant gate synthesis in high‑dimensional quantum processors. Experimental simulations show a 30 % reduction in logical error rates compared to conventional surface‑code approaches. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com
