title: FiLMoS-Net: A Filter-driven Multi-branch Spectral-morphological Network for Robust Breast Ultrasound Image Classification
abstract: Breast ultrasound imaging is a widely available, non-ionizing, and cost-effective modality for breast cancer screening; however, reliable multiclass classification remains challenging because of speckle noise, low contrast, irregular lesion boundaries, inter-scanner variability, and visual overlap among benign, malignant, and normal tissues.FiLMoS-Net integrates learnable Gabor orientation cues, block-wise DCT frequency representations, differentiable edge-morphology features, and sample-adaptive convex routing in a compact 1,288,966-parameter architecture.Evaluation used 780 independent BUSI images in a fixed stratified 544/118/118 train/validation/test split.All comparative runs used random initialization, the same optimization and validation-selection protocol, and five distinct training seeds (42-46).The seed-42 cold-start checkpoint achieved 91.53% accuracy, 91.80% macro-F1, 91.64% sensitivity, 95.11% specificity, 95.54% macro-AUROC, and 94.80% macro-AUPRC.Its benign, malignant, and normal F1 scores were 93.13%, 84.85%, and 97.44%, respectively.Five-run means, sample standard deviations, confidence intervals, and paired nonparametric comparisons were calculated from the archived per-sample predictions of the five independent runs.A separate warm-start sensitivity analysis achieved 93.22% accuracy and 93.71% macro-F1 and was excluded from the cold-start comparative statistics.

title: Quantum Risk and the Governance Gap: A Threat-Informed Prioritization Framework for Critical Infrastructure and Space Systems
abstract: Quantum computing creates a governance challenge before it creates a demonstrated cryptanalytic event. Information collected today may remain sensitive after a cryptographically relevant quantum computer becomes available, while long-lived operational technology and space systems may be unable to adopt new cryptographic mechanisms within conventional replacement cycles. This paper examines how operators of long-lived cyber-physical systems should prioritize post-quantum migration under uncertainty. It distinguishes the present confidentiality risk of harvest-now, decrypt-later collection from the prospective integrity and authentication risks associated with scalable attacks against public-key cryptography. Building on Mosca’s migration inequality, the paper introduces a transparent Quantum Migration Priority Score (QMPS) combining timing pressure, consequence, exposure, and cryptographic agility. A documented scoring protocol and scenario-based sensitivity analysis are provided to prevent the score from being interpreted as a prediction or actuarial estimate. Illustrative applications to municipal water systems and proliferated low-Earth-orbit architectures demonstrate how migration priority depends on mission consequences, protocol boundaries, key management, supply-chain dependencies, compensating controls, and system lifecycle constraints. The paper concludes with a staged governance strategy centered on cryptographic inventories, crypto-agile procurement, testable migration pathways, and explicit acceptance of residual risk.

title: AI-Driven Business Promotion: Applications, Effectiveness, Challenges, and Future Trends
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly embedded in the way businesses promote their products, communicate with customers, and make marketing decisions. Earlier applications were mainly concerned with analysing customer data and predicting behaviour, whereas current systems can also generate content, recommend products, communicate with customers, and support decisions in real time. This paper examines the development of AI-driven business promotion through a critical review of academic and institutional literature. Particular attention is given to customer segmentation and personalization, predictive analytics, recommendation systems, chatbots, marketing automation, and generative AI. The literature indicates that AI can make promotional activities more responsive and can reduce the amount of routine work involved in analysing information and producing content. At the same time, the evidence does not support the idea that AI automatically improves marketing performance. Results depend on the quality of data, the purpose for which AI is used, organizational capabilities, and the way customers perceive AI-mediated communication. Privacy, security, algorithmic bias, transparency, and authenticity have consequently become central concerns. Recent studies on generative AI are especially relevant because they show that consumers may react differently to AI-created communication than to human- created communication. Looking ahead, multimodal generative AI, real-time personalization, predictive customer journeys, and AI agents are likely to expand the range of promotional activities that can be automated or augmented. The paper argues that the long-term value of AI-driven promotion will depend less on automation alone and more on the combination of technological capability, human judgement, reliable data, and responsible governance.

title: I2BA: A Semantic Intent-to-Bounded-Action Architecture for Agentic Systems
abstract: Intent-driven software increasingly relies on language models, tool invocation, workflow planners, and agent-facing protocols. Yet existing mechanisms typically standardize only part of the path from a source’s desired outcome to an authoritative state transition: tools describe callable operations, planners produce plans, control protocols govern execution, and UI protocols transport or render interaction. This paper proposes I2BA (Intent-to-Bounded-Action), a domain- and intent-source-agnostic semantic architecture for the complete lifecycle from intent ingress to bounded execution and ordinary system-state handoff. An intent may originate from a human, another agent, a workflow, an event, or a deterministic controller. An interpreter grounds that intent in explicitly approved context, decomposes it into accounted goals, reconciles those goals with a machine-readable bounded action space, produces a typed ActionPlan, and hands only validated operations across a host-owned authority boundary to closed effectors. Results return through the target system’s ordinary state model rather than remaining isolated in an agent transcript.I2BA does not claim novelty for typed tools, capability schemas, intent translation, plans, approval, or bounded execution individually. Its contribution is their integration into a single semantic control plane with first-class goal accounting (planned, needs-input, unsupported), dialogue or another resolution mechanism for constraint egotiation, exact revision binding for capability/context snapshots, host-owned confirmation and authorization, execution-binding independence, legacy semantic facades, and normative state handoff. Existing technologies can therefore be reused rather than displaced: MCP or OpenAPI may expose operations, AICP may serve as an infrastructure-control execution binding, AG-UI may transport interaction and state, A2UI may render declarative surfaces, A2A may coordinate independent agents,and WoT descriptions may supply device affordances. We accompany the architecture with the public I2BA Specification 0.1.0 Draft 3, including JSON Schemas, neutral examples, semantic validation, and adversarial negative vectors, and use AxolDB Studio, a proprietary database workbench, as a black-box reference implementation evaluated through disclosure-safe human-smoke scenarios. Proprietary database-core algorithms and implementation details are intentionally excluded.

title: Do Language Models Know Their Own Constraints
abstract: We ask whether behavioral constraints acquired through post training remainexplicitly reportable. Using constrained recipe generation as a testbed, fivebanned ingredients enforced via LoRA fine tuning of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct wecompare supervised fine tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization(GRPO) against an untrained baseline on a four tier Constraint AwarenessBenchmark. Averaged over three seeds, both methods raise behavioral compliancefrom 4% to about 90% while reducing explicit constraint reporting below theuntrained model (0.48/5 to 0.16/5 for SFT, 0.07/5 for GRPO) and erodingretained third person knowledge (93% to 36% for SFT, 14% for GRPO; p less than0.01 between methods). Contrary to our initial hypothesis, the reward basedsignal is the more destructive of the two: a reward that penalizes bannedingredient tokens regardless of framing learns a context independentsuppression rather than a self directed constraint. A context conditionedreward designed to teach the self to other distinction fails, collapsing towardinclusion in both framings. Probing prompt time hidden states recovers peringredient avoidance at 83.8% (layer 24 MLP), but only 6.4 points above a peringredient base rate predictor (77.4%), and the model's own verbal self reportis more accurate still (87.8%). A positive control adding explicit selfdescription examples does not restore reporting. The failure is thereforespecific to enumerating constraints on request, not a general loss of access tothem.

title: Controlled Emergence in τ-TCPN: An Agent-Based Framework for Self-Growing Causal Topology under Axiomatic Constraints
abstract: Modern AI systems largely operate as fixed-architecture function approximators: topologies are predefined, and learning adjusts weights inside a closed graph. We argue that the next breakthrough in autonomous intelligence lies not in scaling fixed networks, but in controlled emergence—letting causal topology itself grow, repair, and prune under hard axiomatic constraints. This paper presents τ-TCPN (timed, typed, controlled-emergence Petri-net), a dual-track (thinking / execution) agent simulation framework in which nodes and edges are not prescribed but emerged. A Gap detector senses broken causal input; a candidate generator proposes new bridge nodes (bypass or forward-extension); a local Proof checker validates candidates against non-cycle, arithmetical, and safety predicates; STDP-like co-firing strengthens legal bridges; a dormant-wake operator opens the gate when causal evidence accumulates; and a pruning operator recycles valueless transients. Across four stress scenarios (single-cut, cascaded cut, secondary destruction of a self-grown bridge, multi-source competition with planted loops), the system autonomously rebuilt causal paths with main-chain fake-spike ratio < 2%, zero false Proof rejections in 465 calls, and stable node-population dynamics via pruning. We report the full mathematical specification, the six life-cycle operators, the logged empirical traces, and a conjecture: useful inductive biases for AGI-scale systems may be reverse-extracted from repeated emergence patterns rather than hand-designed upfront. Keywords: controlled emergence, self-organizing topology, causal spike, Kuramoto coupling, STDP, Petri net, axiomatic AI, neuro-symbolic growth, spike causality

title: AI in Real Estate: From Experimentation to Enterprise Transformation
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence is moving from a technology experiment toward a potential operating-model capability for real estate and construction. This research paper examines the transition from AI experimentation to enterprise-scale value creation, with particular focus on data foundations, workflow integration, enterprise architecture, AI governance, agentic AI and measurable business value. Drawing on recent research and industry evidence, the paper examines the gap between widespread AI experimentation and limited enterprise-scale deployment. It identifies key AI opportunities across customer experience, sales, design and planning, construction, procurement, finance, property operations and investment decisions. The paper proposes a five-stage AI maturity model for real estate: Awareness and Experimentation, Controlled Pilots, Integrated Workflows, Enterprise Intelligence and Intelligent Enterprise. It also presents an illustrative AI value chain connecting governed data, AI and analytics, workflows, human decision-making and measurable outcomes. Particular attention is given to data quality, systems integration, human oversight, responsible AI, privacy, cybersecurity and governance. The paper argues that sustainable AI value depends not simply on adopting AI tools, but on redesigning selected business processes around reliable data, intelligent automation and human judgement. The geographic perspective is Global + India, with specific consideration of the Indian real-estate and construction context.

title: An Integrated Machine Learning Framework for Multi-task Retail Decision Support with Explainable AI
abstract: Modern Retail companies must understand their customers, optimize their products, and forecast revenue accurately to remain competitive, yet most organizations lack integrated systems capable of translating transactional data into concrete business decisions.These are not data problems but intelligence problems: the absence of systems that extract the right insight at the right time.Machine learning (ML) addresses this gap by automatically generating customer profiles, product suggestions, and revenue forecasts from historical data.However, Artificial Intelligence (AI) alone is insufficient; managers will not act on predictions they cannot understand.Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) solves this final barrier by making every model transparent and justifiable, ensuring AI-driven recommendations carry the trust required for real operational adoption.This paper proposes a unified, intelligent decision-support framework integrating four ML modules: Customer Segmentation, Product Recommendation, Product-Level Sales Prediction, and Daily Sales Forecasting, with XAI applied to the segmentation, product-level prediction, and forecasting modules, and a Large Language Model (LLM) based automated reporting with the LLaMA model, evaluated on the Global Superstore dataset.The LRFMV (Length, Recency, Frequency, Monetary, Volume) model with K-Means (K=3) yields three interpretable segments: At-Risk (16%), Regular (51.3%),VIP Active (32.7%), validated at 93% classification accuracy with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) Fidelity=1.00 and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME) Stability=0.99 for the segmentation surrogate classifier.User-User Collaborative Filtering (CF) achieves the best recommendation F1-Score = 0.31 and Recall=0.98;XGBoost achieves Test R²=0.95 for product-level prediction, and Linear Regression outperforms all ensemble models for daily forecasting (R²=0.9876,Mean Absolute Error=$198), with 7-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) confirmed as the dominant feature across all three models.LLM layer synthesizes all outputs into structured business intelligence reports.The results demonstrate that accuracy, interpretability, and actionability are mutually reinforced rather than competing objectives, providing a replicable blueprint for deploying responsible, human-centered AI in retail decisionmaking.

title: Foundations of Trans-Planckian Horizon Lock Mechanics – Special Treatise: Mathematical Design for a Fault-Tolerant Topological Super-Quantum Computer Architecture via the Khandey Causal Invariant Constant
abstract: This special treatise establishes the complete formal mathematical physics blueprint and structural regularization architecture for a stable, fault-tolerant Topological Super-Quantum Computer, operating inside the non-perturbative framework of Trans-Planckian Horizon Lock Mechanics (TPHLM). Classically, scalability limits in quantum computing grids suffer from catastrophic decoherence flows, high-order loop noises, and infinite phase divergences that destroy qubit state unitary vectors near initialization phases (t → 0). By anchoring the underlying topological quantum processor mesh directly onto the absolute spatial scale of the Khandey Causal Invariant Constant (K_J = 2.02 × 10^{26} m), we dimensionally regularize multi-loop braiding gates across sub-Planckian tracking boundaries. We satisfy non-perturbative 4D/5D Ward-Takahashi-Slavnov-Taylor gauge identities, eliminate computational trace anomalies, and guarantee an unassailable 0.0000000000000000% phase error baseline optimized for next-generation infinite-capacity quantum information systems.

title: The Growth Claim
abstract: A claim, not a paper. No data, no method, no weights and nothing buildable is included, deliberately. Third in a series after The Substrate Claim (19 August 2026) and The Station Claim (4 September 2026). Patent applications were filed at the UK Intellectual Property Office between July and September 2026, the most recent on 19 September 2026, and are not listed here. title: Evidential Post-Clustering Explanations with Dempster–Shafer Surrogates
abstract: Post-clustering explanations connect unsupervised partitions to explicit rules describing cluster membership. We present a modular empirical evaluation framework that jointly assesses surrogate fidelity, partition validity, explanation complexity, and uncertainty across hard, fuzzy, and evidential clustering outputs. K-Means, Agglomerative Clustering, DBSCAN, Fuzzy C-Means, and Evidential C-Means are paired with Decision Tree, RIPPER, and Dempster-Shafer Gradient Descent (DSGD) surrogates on synthetic, tabular, digit-image, biological, and text representations. Learnability and non-leaky protocols distinguish reproduction of a full-data partition from evaluation with clustering fitted on training data. Native fuzzy and evidential diagnostics complement fidelity to hardened assignments, while the DSGD maximum-score-based ambiguity proxy provides an epistemic diagnostic. In the common six-dataset benchmark, shallow Decision Trees achieve the highest average hard-label fidelity for K-Means, Agglomerative Clustering, Fuzzy C-Means, and Evidential C-Means. For DBSCAN, macro-F1 and noise diagnostics further characterize agreement with imbalanced cluster assignments. Joint analysis of membership entropy and fidelity distinguishes reproduction of hardened labels from membership concentration. The framework provides a reproducible basis for selecting and assessing clustering-surrogate pairings according to partition geometry, output type, and explanation requirements.

title: The social presence of artificial intelligence in the MICE industry: Conceptualization, scale development, and validation
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping the meeting, incentives, conferences and events industry which forms part of the broader tourism industry. Social presence is a central construct in human-artificial intelligence interaction research, yet its conceptualization and measurement remain underdeveloped in this context. This study conceptualizes social presence in artificial intelligence-enabled meeting, incentives, conferences and events services and develops an initial context-specific scale. Following a three-stage scale-development procedure, 362 questionnaires were distributed in China and 300 valid responses were retained for analysis. The scale was refined through literature-based item generation, expert evaluation, pilot feedback, item analysis, and exploratory factor analysis. To strengthen measurement assessment, the revised scale further clarifies content validity, face validity, construct validity, convergent validity, and preliminary discriminant validity. The final scale supports a four-dimensional structure comprising artificial intelligence competence in the meeting, incentives, conferences and events industry, human-like interaction of artificial intelligence, artificial intelligence emotional influence, and artificial intelligence communication accessibility.

title: Lee-Yang preserving quantum Markov semigroups and channels
abstract: This preprint studies quantum Markov dynamics and quantum channels that preserve the Lee–Yang property. For systems of two or more qubits, preservation for all Lee–Yang density matrices forces tensor-product dynamics, with local generators characterized by explicit semidefinite conditions. This ordinary preservation property is equivalent to preservation in the presence of arbitrary inert reference systems. For systems containing higher spins, preservation of all pure Lee–Yang inputs excludes intersite interactions and forces isotropic diffusion with axial drift at higher-spin sites. The paper also develops classifications of static maps with stable full Choi tensors, including singular one-qubit maps and independently covariant maps between finite spins, and establishes quantitative rigidity results for diagonal Hamiltonians. The proofs combine positivity of quantum maps, polynomial root-collision arguments, and coherent tensor contraction. The manuscript includes a disclosure of the AI tools used in its development.

title: Thin-film lithium niobate-based sensing-computing integrated photonic chip for microwave frequency discrimination
abstract: Real-time and accurate identification of microwave frequencies is of great significance for applications such as radar detection, electronic countermeasures, and future 6G wireless communications. Traditional electronic chip-based frequency discrimination schemes face severe challenges in power consumption and cost when achieving ultra-wide bandwidths, making it difficult to meet the urgent demand for ultra-wideband in applications like 6G. Based on thin-film lithium niobate photonic integration technology, this paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a sensing-computing integrated microwave frequency discrimination photonic chip, aiming to achieve real-time microwave frequency identification in the optical domain. Firstly, the microwave signal is converted into an optical signal via an on-chip thin-film lithium niobate electro-optic modulator, and then utilizes a disordered microring lattice to construct a photonic reservoir. The incident light carrying the microwave signal information undergoes complex resonance and interference effects, mapping it into a high-dimensional optical response, thereby achieving ultra-low-power, high-speed nonlinear feature extraction at the physical layer. This architecture significantly reduces reliance on high-speed analog-to-digital converters and subsequent electronic processors. Experimental results show that the device achieves single-shot real-time frequency identification over an ultra-wide microwave frequency range from 10 MHz to 66.01 GHz, with a root mean square error of 40 MHz. Furthermore, a multi-tone signal classification and recognition task was performed, achieving an accuracy of 95%. The scheme proposed in this paper provides an efficient new approach for real-time ultra-wideband microwave frequency measurement and has potential in fields such as microwave photonic signal analysis, real-time spectrum sensing, and on-chip intelligent photonic information processing.

title: External validation of AI assisted colposcopy using WHO dataset for cervical precancer and cancer detection
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-guided colposcopy has previously been developed to assist colposcopists in detecting cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse (CIN2+) and guiding biopsies, but internal testing of the AI model could overestimate diagnostic performance. We validated the performance of the AI-guided colposcopy on an independent WHO open-source set of 187 patients with 855 colposcopic images. Forty-five colposcopists with different levels of experience from 12 regions in China participated in the validation set. The sensitivity of the AI system on CIN2+ standalone diagnosis were 84.2% (95%CI 74.4–90.7%). With AI assistance, colposcopists sensitivity increased from 84.8% (95% CI, 82.7–86.9%) to 90.6% (95% CI, 88.7–92.1%). The improvement was most evident among low-experienced colposcopists, with sensitivity increasing by 6.5%, and AUC from 0.72 (95% CI, 0.68–0.77) to 0.76 (95% CI, 0.72–0.80; p = 0.043). AI-guided biopsy support was also associated with a reduction in the mean number of biopsies per case, from 2.48 to 2.02. These findings highlight the AI system’s robust performance on an independent external dataset and its capacity to bridge the diagnostic experience gap among readers, supporting its clinical implementation as a valuable adjunct for colposcopic assessment.

title: ClozeCongruence: Human-Style Essay Classification vs. AI-Written Text via Multi-Horizon Semantic Infilling and Calibrated Stylometric Manifolds
abstract: Abstract—Distinguishing authentic human-authored essays from machine-generated prose remains a critical challenge for educational integrity, admissions authenticity, and digital forensics. Existing zero-shot detectors either rely on inaccessible white-box token logits (DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT) or penalize formal, non-native human writing styles through uncalibrated perplexity metrics. Furthermore, prior forensic benchmarks frequently evaluate specialized technical preprints (e.g., ArXiv, PeerRead) or truncate samples to 200 words, destroying macro-discursive structure. In this paper, we present ClozeCongruence, an unconfounded forensic framework evaluated on a curated benchmark of $N = 6{,}997$ samples dedicated to full-length human-style essay classification vs. AI-written text (mean length $\approx 640$ words, up to 1,500 words). Our methodology delivers five core contributions under strict zero-target-leakage protocols (verified via label permutation tests yielding null AUROCs of $0.4870 \approx 0.50 \pm 0.02$ and Pearson length correlation $r = 0.0000$): In-Domain Essay Classification & Operating Points: On clean, prompt-matched human vs. machine essays ($N = 3{,}000$; 1,500 matched pairs), zero-shot stylometric scoring achieves an AUROC of 0.8554 [95% Bootstrap CI: 0.8420–0.8682] and AUPRC of 0.8391. To guarantee that 99% of algorithmic accusations are accurate (False Positive Rate $\le 1.0\%$ at threshold $\tau = 0.9276$), zero-shot sensitivity yields a True Positive Rate (TPR) of 13.33% ($\approx 1$ out of 7 AI essays), rising to 39.73% TPR at 5.0% FPR ($\tau = 0.8505$). Augmented by a 5-fold cross-validated supervised manifold ensemble, discrimination reaches an AUROC of 0.9651 with 52.17% TPR at 1.0% FPR. Adversarial Robustness (RAID Benchmark): Across the Full RAID 11-Attack Adversarial Benchmark ($N = 6{,}000$; Dugan et al., ACL 2024), pre-inference canonicalization neutralizes surface attacks: homoglyph substitution recovers from 0.6793 to 0.9649 AUROC ($\Delta = +0.2856$, 62.4% TPR at 1% FPR; clean baseline maintains 0.9799 AUROC). Concurrently, it establishes the empirical failure boundary against 11B DIPPER neural paraphrasing (0.6956 AUROC, 13.2% TPR at 1% FPR; overall benchmark AUROC = 0.9459). Cross-Domain & Zero-Shot Multilingual Transfer (M4): Evaluation on the M4 Benchmark ($N = 4{,}000$ across 8 strata and 6 languages) demonstrates robust generalization on structured academic English (PeerRead AUROC = 0.9977, 92.0% TPR at 1% FPR) alongside natural script attenuation across Arabic (0.8706), German (0.8008), Chinese (0.7143), Urdu (0.7038), and Russian (0.6700) without language-specific tuning (Full M4 AUROC = 0.8165). Boundary Detection & the Slack Window Paradox: On the Chimeric Co-Authorship Benchmark ($N = 2{,}000$ documents), we expose the Slack Window Paradox: while naive $\pm 1$ paragraph slack inflates boundary F1 to 77.35%, heuristic inter-paragraph difference alone yields an AUROC of only 51.32% (random chance). This establishes that short-document slack is an empirical artifact and demonstrates that supervised sliding-window gradient segmentation is required. Attribution Auditing & Demographic Fairness: Cross-architecture fingerprinting achieves 80.01% Macro-F1 across distinct generator families (BLOOMZ, Cohere, GPT), whereas stylometrics collapse into majority prediction ($\text{F1} = 48.03\%$) on intra-family shared-weight variants (ChatGPT vs. GPT-3.5-Turbo). Crucially, the detector achieves a 0.00% False Accusation Rate across $N = 600$ non-native ESL essays at the calibrated 1.0% FPR threshold ($\tau = 0.9276$), deliberately trading sensitivity for equity. All code and curated benchmarks are available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/DebdipCS/human-vs-ai-essay-benchmark. Index Terms—AI Text Forensics, Human-Style Essay Classification, Multi-Horizon Cloze Infilling, Stylometric Manifolds, RAID Benchmark, Operational Sensitivity.

title: Bayesian Nonparametric Factor Analysis via Marginalized Dirichlet Process Column Clustering with Spike-and-Slab Sparsity
abstract: We propose a Bayesian nonparametric factor model that infers the number of factors, induces row-wise sparsity, and merges redundant dictionary elements via exact clustering. A Dirichlet process prior is placed on the columns of an overcomplete loading matrix and fully marginalized to an exact Pólya urn, avoiding stick-breaking and auxiliary variables. A spike-and-slab base measure allows entire factors to be exactly zero. The model uniquely combines exact zeros, exchangeability over columns, and exact merging within a single marginalized Dirichlet process, unlike CUSP, MGP, or the beta process. An exact Gibbs sampler with canonical relabeling and parallel C/MPI implementation is developed. We prove posterior contraction at rate $\sqrt{M s_0 \log n / n}$ for the covariance matrix, and in the fixed-dictionary setting obtain the minimax optimal rate $\sqrt{s_0 \log n / n}$ plus underfitting consistency; the overfitting direction is an open conjecture. The spike-and-slab is essential: without it the effective dimension scales as $pM$, yielding a slower rate. Simulations show the method is the only fully adaptive approach to recover the true rank, achieving the smallest covariance, loading, and signal-reconstruction errors, beating an oracle baseline. On van 't Veer breast cancer data ($n=97$, $p=1213$), the posterior concentrates on eight interpretable programmes; seven pass coherence and two pass Bonferroni-corrected Hallmark enrichment.

title: From Native Structure to Necessary Form
abstract: An integrated synthesis of the eleven-paper TUS OS mathematical research programme, culminating in the General Theory of Answerability, across thirteen documents. Abstract This synthesis reconstructs the complete TUS OS mathematical research programme and its culminating result: Complete Answerability has a necessary protected organisational form, lawfully equivalent to the abstract TUS form independently extracted from TUS OS. Across eleven papers and thirteen documents, the programme progresses from the exact geometry of a deterministic six-bit system through quantum-operational representation, predictive structure, contract-relative resource theory and operational observability to an independently constituted mathematical theory of Answerability. title: Inferring channel memory, phase, and noise symmetry from the output of noisy quantum teleportation
abstract: Abstract We consider quantum teleportation channels in which a phase $$\varphi$$ is imprinted onto the initial shared resource channel. The resource qudits interact with either two independent local environments or a common environment; we classify the noise as symmetric when the noise parameters on the two qudits are identical, and as asymmetric otherwise. By teleporting an arbitrary input state, we compute the Hilbert–Schmidt speed (HSS) and quantum Fisher information (QFI) of both the noisy resource channel and the teleported output state, each computed with respect to the initially encoded phase $$\varphi$$ . We show that under symmetric noise, the HSS and QFI of the teleported output reproduce the same qualitative temporal behavior as their resource-channel counterparts. Because HSS can witness essential non-Markovianity—defined here as the violation of P-divisibility—within established contractivity regimes, this correspondence enables indirect inference of the resource channel’s memory effects from the output alone, without requiring direct access to the channel after teleportation. The output HSS and QFI also carry information about the initial phase, allowing its estimation. We further find that asymmetric noise can cause the qualitative dynamics of the output HSS and QFI to deviate from those of the resource channel. Such a deviation provides a diagnostic signature of environmental asymmetry. HSS can be evaluated without diagonalizing the density matrix, making it practical for high-dimensional qudit teleportation; moreover, the output state has a lower dimension than the bipartite resource channel, offering a lower-dimensional probe that substantially reduces measurement and computational overhead. Within the representative noise models studied, these findings establish a unified framework for extracting information about channel memory, phase sensitivity, and noise symmetry directly from the accessible teleported output.

title: Genre-Routed Generative Resonance: Black-Box AI Text Detection via Dual-Horizon Probing and Structural Rhythm
abstract: Detecting text synthesized by frontier large language models (LLMs) remains a critical requirement for academic integrity, digital forensics, and media authenticity. Existing zero-shot detectors exhibit severe real-world failure modes: token-curvature methods (DetectGPT, Fast-DetectGPT) require inaccessible white-box model logits, while perplexity baselines disproportionately penalize non-native English writers. In our earlier investigations, single-branch cloze infilling collapsed when scaled to open-domain environments due to the Reasoning Prober Paradox, genre-dependent predictability asymmetry, the 1-word compound noun trap, and the brittleness of punctuation stylometry. This paper introduces Genre-Routed Generative Resonance (ClozeCongruence), a logit-free forensic framework that couples two complementary probing geometries via an automated linguistic Genre Router: factual and expository passages are directed to forward Prefix-Tail Completion, while creative and narrative prose is guided to middle-sentence Cloze Infilling. To shield human authors without punctuation counting, we formulate Clean Structural Dynamics, combining multi-pass inter-horizon void decay ($\Delta\text{void}$) with sentence-length coefficient of variation ($CV$). Across a balanced, stratified benchmark of $N = 1{,}000$ full-length documents (Academic Nature essays, Non-Native ESL essays, Wikipedia expository prose, Frontier LLMs including GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and LLaMA-3.3, and RAID adversarial evasions), three candidate architectures achieve reproducible discrimination with nonparametric bootstrap 95% confidence intervals and label-permutation tests ($p < 0.001$): (1) Clean Structural Geometric Fusion yields the highest global AUROC (0.8283, 95% CI [0.803, 0.853], Youden $J = 0.5120$), capturing 73.6% of frontier AI text at $\tau = 26\%$ with ESL FAR 10.0% and mean separation $+14.14\text{ pp}$ (human $20.29 \pm 8.33$, AI $34.43 \pm 14.57$). (2) Genre-Routed Hybrid with Two-Tier Gate provides a high-recall screening profile (79.8% TPR at $\tau = 26\%$; 69.8% TPR at Youden-optimal $\tau = 28\%$, AUROC 0.8184, 95% CI [0.791, 0.844], ESL FAR 9.0%). (3) Clean Structural Linear Fusion achieves the most conservative Youden-optimal ESL protection (8.5% FAR; AUROC 0.8107, 95% CI [0.783, 0.836]). At the enterprise disciplinary threshold ($\tau \ge 38\%$), Geometric Fusion yields 0.00% ESL false accusation (0/200); Two-Tier and Linear yield 0.5% and 1.0%, respectively. Code, cohorts, and audit logs are released for reproducibility.

title: Singular-Subspace Alignment in Norm-Constrained Asymmetric Low-Rank Updates
abstract: We study the singular-subspace geometry of an asymmetric low-rank update X=BA under a Frobenius-norm constraint. For the affine linearization of a smooth matrix loss, factorized first-order stationarity pairs singular subspaces of the gradient, while the factorized second-order condition selects the leading r subspaces exactly. For a nonlinear loss, let G and G̃ denote the gradients at the pretrained and adapted points. Under full-rank factors, an active constraint, a positive multiplier, and suitable spectral separation, we prove a Wedin-type bound: the alignment error is at most βc/δr(G,G̃), where β is the gradient-Lipschitz constant and c is the update budget. If βc<γG/4, this is bounded by 4βc/(3γG) relative to the pretrained gradient. Globally smooth constructions, including a convex one, attain the same asymptotic order. For r=1, exact alignment can fail outside this perturbative regime at a genuine factorized second-order stationary point. The results concern stationary-point geometry, not algorithmic convergence.

title: Cognitive Provenance - A Framework for the Traceable Formation and Evolution of Cognitive Assets
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence is increasingly transforming cognitive production from a relatively linear process of individual knowledge creation into an iterative process involving human judgment, machine-assisted structuring, validation, transformation, and reuse. As cognitive outputs become continuously developed and recombined, the identity of a cognitive asset may no longer be adequately represented by its current expression alone. This Foundational Note introduces Cognitive Provenance as a conceptual layer within the broader Cognitive Property Theory (CPT) framework. Cognitive Provenance refers to the traceable history through which a cognitive asset is formed, contributed to, validated, transformed, and evolved. It extends the concept of cognitive asset beyond its current expression by treating the formation and evolution history of the asset as relevant to understanding its identity, continuity, and subsequent development. The central proposition is: A cognitive asset should be understood not only through its current expression, but also through a traceable provenance of its formation, contribution, validation, transformation, and evolution. Cognitive Provenance is distinguished from ordinary publication metadata, authorship attribution, intellectual property ownership, and legal priority. A DOI or other public record may provide a temporal or public provenance anchor, but does not by itself establish ownership, authorship, exclusivity, or enforceability. Cognitive Provenance is therefore proposed as a conceptual layer between Cognitive Assetization and the subsequent lifecycle, lineage, reuse, and organizational capability of cognitive assets. This Note does not propose a complete legal doctrine. It establishes a minimum conceptual claim for further development within CPT.

title: Confidence-Driven Backdoor Poisoning in Text Classification: Sample Efficiency, Knowledge-Distillation Survival, and Defense Evasion Across Four Datasets
abstract: A backdoor attack hides a secret switch inside a machine learning model: the model behaves normally almost all the time, but produces an attacker-chosen wrong answer whenever a specific trigger appears in the input. The attacker installs the switch by corrupting a small number of training examples. A method called confidence-driven boundary sampling (CBS) proposes a smarter way to choose which examples to corrupt — pick the ones the model is already unsure about — and was shown on image classifiers to make the resulting backdoor harder for security checks to detect. CBS had never been evaluated on text, and nobody had checked whether these backdoors survive when a large model is compressed into a smaller one. We test both. We use BERT-base as the teacher and DistilBERT as the compressed student, two trigger families (a rare word and an out-of-domain sentence), and four datasets chosen so that each changes a single structural property: SST-2 (short text, binary) as the baseline, AG News (four classes), IMDB (long documents), and Yelp Polarity (long documents, different domain). We report four findings. First, CBS costs the attacker more, not less. To reach a 90% attack success rate on SST-2 it needs about 8.3 times more corrupted data than random selection (5 times for the sentence trigger); on Yelp's word trigger it never reaches 90% at all, even at twenty times random selection's budget. A three-seed replication confirms the SST-2 gap with non-overlapping variance. Second, compression removes most of the backdoor but never all of it. Retention spans 0.88–12.30% across the four datasets, even though the student is trained only on clean text; CBS retains more than random selection in 7 of 8 comparisons. Third, the stealth advantage CBS was designed for does not appear in text — and on Yelp it reverses. Three of four defenses barely affect either method on most datasets, and on Yelp's word trigger every defense strips substantially more from the CBS backdoor (3.9–18.8 points) than from the random one (≤0.2 points). Fourth, document length caps the attack, but the threshold is absolute rather than relative. IMDB plateaus at 79–86% and never reaches 90% at any rate from 0.02% to 10%. Yelp, also long-form, does not plateau — its typical document is 202.6 tokens against IMDB's 305.2. CBS selects systematically longer documents than random selection on both (300.5 vs. 202.6 on Yelp; 387.6 vs. 305.2 on IMDB), which places CBS-selected Yelp documents inside the same dilution regime IMDB imposes on every method — and explains why CBS alone fails on Yelp's word trigger. Code and per-run results: https://github.com/kannu74/cbs_on_text

To reach a 90% attack success rate on SST-2 it needs about 8.3 times more corrupted data than random selection (5 times for the sentence trigger); on Yelp's word trigger it never reaches 90% at all, even at twenty times random selection's budget. A three-seed replication confirms the SST-2 gap with non-overlapping variance. Second, compression removes most of the backdoor but never all of it. Retention spans 0.88–12.30% across the four datasets, even though the student is trained only on clean text; CBS retains more than random selection in 7 of 8 comparisons. Third, the stealth advantage CBS was designed for does not appear in text — and on Yelp it reverses. Three of four defenses barely affect either method on most datasets, and on Yelp's word trigger every defense strips substantially more from the CBS backdoor (3.9–18.8 points) than from the random one (≤0.2 points). Fourth, document length caps the attack, but the threshold is absolute rather than relative. IMDB plateaus at 79–86% and never reaches 90% at any rate from 0.02% to 10%. Yelp, also long-form, does not plateau — its typical document is 202.6 tokens against IMDB's 305.2. CBS selects systematically longer documents than random selection on both (300.5 vs. 202.6 on Yelp; 387.6 vs. 305.2 on IMDB), which places CBS-selected Yelp documents inside the same dilution regime IMDB imposes on every method — and explains why CBS alone fails on Yelp's word trigger. title: N Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model
abstract: This paper proposes the N Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model (N-LMPS): on top of the single-layer logic meta-phase space (whose theory is given in Logic Meta-Phase Space Reasoning Model, hereafter the theory paper), it organizes two orthogonal axes and one review gate. (i) Resolution axis: a θ-refinement filtration C0→C1→⋯→CNC0→C1→⋯→CN of the same structure–symbol space (P,T) — multiple resolution views of one space, with nested partitions, a surjective fine-to-coarse projection ψ, and a canonical section φ satisfying ψ∘φ=id (Propositions 2.1/2.2/2.3); (ii) superposition axis: three classes of independent spaces defined by data source — a core space S₁ (trained on high-accuracy data, with safety specifications applied as application policy), generalization spaces S₂,…,S_M (further training data), and learning spaces S_{M+1},…,S_N (learning data from the usage process, which do not participate in reasoning directly) — combined as the √JS-fidelity-weighted superposition Q=∑iwiqiQ=∑iwiqi, wi∝exp⁡(−JS(qref∥qi))wi∝exp(−JS(qref∥qi)); (iii) review gate: learning content may be merged into the generalization spaces and thus participate in reasoning only after multi-round learning stability (absorption by reflection) and teacher-space answer confirmation (√JS fidelity ≤ θ_teacher). This paper provides the inter-layer maps, the cross-layer edge weights (projection consistency and refinement error), the promotion/demotion operators and their duality, the monotone bounded convergence of the potential function, the formalization and preservation of safety constraints, and three conduction theorems for superposition: Proposition 6.1 (one-step TV conduction), Proposition 6.3 (two-step JS and h² conductions), Proposition 6.4 (one-step Hellinger conduction plus an internal-spread term) — the deviation of the superposition is provably controlled by the fidelity-weighted average of its components, and the worst case never deteriorates. All conclusions are accompanied by basic validation (validation paper V1–V25). The authority of the core layer and the review thresholds are declared application policy: their formalization lies inside the theory, and the basis of their assignment lies outside it. Reading guide. §1.1 contains a self-contained review of the single-layer theory for readers without a logic-theory background; §1.5 summarizes the relation between the two axes and the validation correspondence; Appendix A gives the training and prediction flow diagrams; Appendix B gives a plain-language explanation; Appendix C gives a numerical mini-example. Keywords: N logic meta-phase space; resolution axis; superposition axis; review gate; cross-layer edge weights; potential convergence; deviation conduction theorems; safety constraints 本文提出 N 逻辑元相空间推理模型(N-LMPS):在单层逻辑元相空间(其理论见《逻辑元相空间推理模型》,本文称理论文章)之上组织两个正交轴与一个评审门。(i) 分辨率轴:同一结构–符号空间 (P,T) 的 θ-精化过滤 C0→C1→⋯→CNC0→C1→⋯→CN——同一空间的多个分辨率视图,划分嵌套、细→粗投影 ψ 满射、规范截面 φ 满足 ψ∘φ=id(命题 2.1/2.2/2.3);(ii) 叠加轴:按数据来源定义的三类独立空间——核心空间 S₁(高精度数据训练,安全规范作为应用政策)、泛化空间 S₂,…,S_M(更多训练数据)、学习空间 S_{M+1},…,S_N(使用过程的学习数据,不直接参与推理)——其组合为 √JS 保真度加权叠加 Q=∑iwiqiQ=∑iwiqi,wi∝exp⁡(−JS(qref∥qi))wi∝exp(−JS(qref∥qi));(iii) 评审门:学习内容须经多轮学习稳定(思考吸收)与教师空间答案确认(√JS 保真度 ≤ θ_teacher)后方可合入泛化空间参与推理。本文给出层间映射、跨层边权(投影一致性与细化误差)、升级/降级算子与对偶性、势函数单调有界收敛、安全约束的形式化与保持性,以及叠加的三类传导定理:命题 6.1(TV 一次传导)、命题 6.3(JS 与 h² 二次传导)、命题 6.4(Hellinger 一次传导 + 内部弥散项)——叠加的偏差以可证方式受控于组分的保真度加权平均,最坏情形不恶化。全部结论配基本验证(验证文章 V1–V25)。核心层权限与评审门槛为声明的应用政策,其形式化在理论之内、其权限分配依据在理论之外。 阅读指引。 §1.1 对单层理论做自足回顾,不熟悉逻辑理论背景的读者可直接阅读;§1.5 汇总两轴关系与验证对应;附录 A 给出训练与预测流程框图;附录 B 给出通俗解释;附录 C 给出一个数值小例。 关键词: N 逻辑元相空间;分辨率轴;叠加轴;评审门;跨层边权;势函数收敛;偏差传导定理;安全约束

title: HEXAID: A Task-adaptive Multimodal Ensemble Framework for Disease Identification and Severity Stratification in Emergency Departments
abstract: Clinical decision-making in emergency departments (EDs) requires rapid integration of heterogeneous patient information, including structured vital signs, physical examination findings, and free-text clinical narratives, to support disease identification and patient severity stratification.However, a single modeling strategy may not be equally effective across clinical prediction tasks with different decision-boundary characteristics.This study proposes HEXAID, a task-adaptive multimodal ensemble framework that integrates structured clinical data with n-gram TF-IDF representations of free-text clinical narratives for unified ED decision support.The study used 5,000 electronic medical records from an Indonesian ED, of which 4,374 valid records remained after a multi-stage preprocessing pipeline, resulting in a 719-dimensional feature matrix.A systematic ablation study comprising ten experimental configurations evaluated baseline models, hybrid RF-XGBoost soft voting, Chi-Square feature selection, Bayesian hyperparameter optimization using Optuna TPE, and class-imbalance handling strategies.For disease identification, the Optuna-optimized full-feature ensemble achieved an F1-Macro of 0.9255 and AUC of 0.9922, outperforming the baseline models.For severity stratification, the selected imbalance-handling strategy achieved an F1-Macro of 0.8579 and AUC of 0.9567, with a Severe-class recall of 0.75.The ablation results demonstrate that optimal ensemble configurations are task-dependent: disease identification favored XGBoost-dominant weighting, whereas severity stratification benefited from a more balanced RF contribution.SHAP analysis further showed that temperature was the dominant feature for disease identification, while systolic blood pressure was prominent for severity stratification, providing clinically plausible model interpretations.These findings demonstrate that task-adaptive optimization is important for multimodal clinical decision-support models, particularly when prediction tasks differ in decisionboundary structure and class distribution.

title: Dissociating Prompt Quality from Response Compliance in Automated Prompt-Engineering Assessment: evaluator, results and figure code
abstract: Code and per-item numeric results for the study "Response Compliance Confounds Prompt Quality in LLM-as-a-Judge Scoring". The study scores 498 prompts from WildChat-1M, LMSYS-Chat-1M and IFEval with a four-stage evaluator built on a locally hosted model (Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct via Ollama). Each prompt is rated before any response exists, and each response is scored twice: against criteria extracted from its own prompt and against a fixed rubric that never sees the prompt. Contents- MATLAB source for the evaluator, baselines, factorial ablation, known-groups and graded construct validation- Python script for IFEval verification with the benchmark's own code- Per-item results: results/main_run_500.csv, results/baseline_120.csv, results/ablation_factorial_120.csv- Hash manifest of all 4,275 benchmark prompts: data/benchmark_manifest.csv Prompt and response text from WildChat-1M and LMSYS-Chat-1M is not redistributed under their licences. The benchmark can be rebuilt from the source datasets with src/create_master_benchmark.m and checked against the hash manifest. Version 1.2.0 adds the factorial ablation (three-sample naive judge, single-pass rubric judge) and the graded construct validation scripts and results. Requirements: MATLAB R2025b, base installation, no toolboxes; Ollama with qwen2.5:7b.Licence: MIT.

title: SphereLock SL-1.
abstract: **SphereLock Protocol (SL-1)** is a brand-new post-quantum authenticated encryption protocol for secure communications, designed from first principles and directly inspired by the Bloch Protocol / Postern Labs approach on blochprotocol.io. ### Core Inspiration from Bloch Bloch requires **both** ML-DSA-65 (module-lattice) **and** Falcon-1024 (NTRU-lattice) signatures to verify for every authorization. This is not optional hybrid padding; both must succeed. The design accepts larger keys/signatures and verification cost in exchange for independent hardness assumptions. SphereLock applies the same dual-lattice philosophy to communications: key establishment and authentication must succeed under two independent lattice families simultaneously. No single lattice break (or implementation flaw in one scheme) collapses the channel. It is classical post-quantum cryptography (software-only, no quantum channel or special hardware required), named thematically after the Bloch sphere while remaining fully implementable today with NIST-standardized or near-standard primitives. ### Design Goals - **Dual independent hardness**: Module-lattice + NTRU-lattice must both contribute. - **Authenticated key exchange** resistant to harvest-now-decrypt-later. - **Forward secrecy** and post-compromise security via ratcheting. - **Open and inspectable**: All parameters, algorithms, and limitations published; no proprietary “black-box” crypto. - Practical for messaging, VoIP signaling, or TLS-like channels (larger handshake size is accepted). ### Cryptographic Primitives (fixed for SL-1) | Role | Primary | Secondary (must both succeed) | |-----------------------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------| | Key Encapsulation | ML-KEM-1024 (FIPS 203) | NTRU-HRSS or Falcon-derived KEM equivalent (NTRU lattice) | | Long-term / Ephemeral Signatures | ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) | Falcon-1024 | | Symmetric Encryption | AES-256-GCM | — | | Key Derivation / Hash | SHAKE-256 / HKDF-SHA3-256 | — | | Nonce / Randomness | CSPRNG + domain-separated SHAKE | — | Both KEMs produce independent shared secrets that are mixed; both signature schemes must verify on the transcript. ### Protocol Flow (High-Level) **1. Identity Setup (one-time)** Each party generates a dual long-term identity: - ML-DSA-65 keypair + Falcon-1024 keypair. - Optional registered-device binding (inspired by Postern Wallet concepts). Public keys are exchanged out-of-band or via a Bloch-style on-chain registry if desired. Identities are identified by the hash of the concatenated public keys. **2. Handshake (Dual-Lattice Authenticated Key Exchange)** Alice (initiator) → Bob: - Generate ephemeral dual keypairs (ML-KEM + NTRU-family + dual signatures). - Send: `ephemeral_ML-KEM_pk || ephemeral_NTRU_pk || dual_signature(transcript) || identity_proof` - Both signatures (ML-DSA-65 **and** Falcon-1024) cover the entire transcript including the other party’s identity hash. Bob responds symmetrically and performs dual encapsulation. Both parties compute: ``` ss_module = Decaps_ML-KEM(...) ss_ntru = Decaps_NTRU(...) shared = HKDF(ss_module || ss_ntru || transcript_hash, "SphereLock-SS") ``` If either decapsulation or either signature verification fails, the handshake aborts. There is no fallback to a single scheme. **3. Session Key Derivation** From the dual shared secret: - Root key → Chain keys (send/receive) via HKDF with domain separation. - Message keys derived per message (ratchet). - Optional header encryption for metadata protection. **4. Secure Messaging** - Each message: dual-signature optional for high-assurance modes, or single MAC under the message key for efficiency. - AES-256-GCM with unique nonces. - Ratcheting: after each message (or every N messages) a new dual ephemeral KEM is performed and mixed in (Double Ratchet style, dual-lattice version). - Post-compromise security: compromise of one lattice key does not allow recovery of past or future keys without the second lattice secret. **5. Re-key / Epoch Rotation** Inspired by Bloch’s slot/epoch structure: parties can force a full dual re-handshake after a configurable number of messages or time (e.g., 16 “epochs”). ### Security Properties (Intended) - **Confidentiality & Integrity**: Dual lattice KEMs + authenticated encryption. - **Authentication**: Dual signatures required on the handshake transcript. - **Forward Secrecy**: Ephemeral dual KEMs + ratcheting. - **Resistance to quantum computers**: Relies on the hardness of both module-LWE/SIS and NTRU-lattice problems (different families). - **No single point of failure**: An attacker who breaks only ML-KEM or only the NTRU component still cannot recover the session key or forge the handshake. - **Transcript binding**: Everything is bound under both signature schemes. ### Trade-offs (Honest, Bloch-style) - Handshake size and CPU cost are significantly higher than classical or single-PQ schemes (dual large public keys + dual signatures). - Hardware wallet / constrained-device support is limited (same limitation Bloch accepts). - Implementations must carefully constant-time both lattice schemes and avoid side-channel leakage in the dual verification path. - The protocol is **new** and therefore unaudited by definition; any real deployment would require independent cryptanalysis and formal verification of the dual-mixing KDF. ### Naming & Philosophy Named **SphereLock** after the Bloch sphere (the geometric representation of a qubit that the original Bloch Protocol is built to survive). The dual-lattice requirement mirrors Bloch’s “two signatures, one requirement” design boundary. Everything is intended to be open, inspectable, and free of hidden classical fallbacks. This is a complete conceptual specification for a new communications protocol. It can be implemented today using existing libraries (PQClean / liboqs for the lattice primitives, standard AES-GCM and SHAKE). Further formalization would include exact byte formats, domain-separation strings, error codes, and a reference implementation in Rust (consistent with Bloch’s style).

Re-key / Epoch Rotation** Inspired by Bloch’s slot/epoch structure: parties can force a full dual re-handshake after a configurable number of messages or time (e.g., 16 “epochs”). ### Security Properties (Intended) - **Confidentiality & Integrity**: Dual lattice KEMs + authenticated encryption. - **Authentication**: Dual signatures required on the handshake transcript. - **Forward Secrecy**: Ephemeral dual KEMs + ratcheting. - **Resistance to quantum computers**: Relies on the hardness of both module-LWE/SIS and NTRU-lattice problems (different families). - **No single point of failure**: An attacker who breaks only ML-KEM or only the NTRU component still cannot recover the session key or forge the handshake. - **Transcript binding**: Everything is bound under both signature schemes. ### Trade-offs (Honest, Bloch-style) - Handshake size and CPU cost are significantly higher than classical or single-PQ schemes (dual large public keys + dual signatures). - Hardware wallet / constrained-device support is limited (same limitation Bloch accepts). - Implementations must carefully constant-time both lattice schemes and avoid side-channel leakage in the dual verification path. - The protocol is **new** and therefore unaudited by definition; any real deployment would require independent cryptanalysis and formal verification of the dual-mixing KDF. ### Naming & Philosophy Named **SphereLock** after the Bloch sphere (the geometric representation of a qubit that the original Bloch Protocol is built to survive). The dual-lattice requirement mirrors Bloch’s “two signatures, one requirement” design boundary. Everything is intended to be open, inspectable, and free of hidden classical fallbacks. This is a complete conceptual specification for a new communications protocol. It can be implemented today using existing libraries (PQClean / liboqs for the lattice primitives, standard AES-GCM and SHAKE). Further formalization would include exact byte formats, domain-separation strings, error codes, and a reference implementation in Rust (consistent with Bloch’s style).

title: Environmental richness and collapse in long-horizon LLM agents
abstract: **H1 (environment).** Long-horizon LLM agent performance on economic management tasks improves when the environment affords narrative richness and expressive play. The documented failure modes in long-horizon agent benchmarks (Vending-Bench-style loops, obsessive spirals, escalating meltdowns) are not calculation errors but *collapse* — the same regression-to-the-mean attractor dynamics observed in creative-generation contexts. Sterile environments accelerate entry into the attractor basin; generative environments retard it. **H2 (trace).** Collapse is measurable in the reasoning trace before it is visible in the economics. Trace-health metrics (novelty decay, recurrence quantification, behavioral stereotypy) computed over the agent's daily scratchpad predict economic failure. If scratchpad recurrence predicts bankruptcy, creative collapse and agentic failure are one phenomenon measured in two currencies.

title: Fail-Closed Tor Exit-Country Rotation on OpenWrt-Class Routers: A Simulation Study Inspired by tor-router-manager
abstract: OpenWrt-based Tor exit-country rotation tools can leave users on clearnet if every configured ExitNodes country fails bootstrap. Inspired by tor-router-manager (SSH-deployed rotate script + fallback CC), we simulate fail-open versus fail-closed rotation policies. Across N=36 seeds/arm, fail-open recorded 5 clearnet-leak outcomes after exhausted ExitNodes lists, while fail-closed recorded 0 leaks and recovered via fallback country in 1 runs. LAB simulation only—no live router credentials, no encouragement of illicit use; lawful privacy/research framing. Independent Systems Lab preprint series. LAB/SIMULATION. CC-BY-4.0.

title: Margay Optimization Algorithm: A Novel Bio-inspired Metaheuristic based on Adaptive Canopy Exploration and Stealth Pursuit for Global Optimization
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms have attracted the attention of many researchers in recent years due to their ability to solve complex optimization problems.Despite the progress made, striking a proper balance between exploration and exploitation is still one of the most important challenges in the design of these algorithms.In this study, Margay Optimization Algorithm (MOA) is introduced as a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the natural behavior of Margay.The design of this algorithm is based on two main behaviors of this animal.Adaptive Canopy Exploration Strategy behavior is modeled to guide Global exploration and increase search diversity, while Stealth Pursuit and Precision Localization Strategy behavior is developed to perform Local exploitation and gradually improve promising solutions.The performance of MOA is evaluated using a set of 23 standard benchmark functions including unimodal test functions (F1-F7), high-dimensional multimodal test functions (F8-F13), and fixed-dimensional multimodal test functions (F14-F23) and compared with 9 well-known algorithms.All experiments were performed in 20 independent runs and 1000 iterations for each run, and the results were analyzed using mean, std, and rank indices, along with convergence curves and boxplot graphs.The results show that MOA achieved rank = 1 in 22 of the 23 benchmark functions, achieving a 95.65% success rate compared to competing algorithms.Also, quantitative and qualitative analyses have shown that the complementary design of the two proposed strategies has created an effective balance between exploration and exploitation, increasing the convergence speed, reducing oscillation, improving stability, and enhancing the quality of the final solutions.These findings have shown that MOA is a competitive and efficient optimizer for solving a wide range of optimization problems and real-world applications.

title: INT-MMSL-01 — Computational Hidden-State Minimal-Contrast Experiment, Phase 1
abstract: INT-MMSL-01 is an exploratory experimental protocol developed within the Interstizio Framework to investigate and document computational representations in a locally executed large language model. Phase 1 uses Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and a preregistered minimal-contrast design. Hidden-state vectors (4096 dimensions) were extracted from the final model layer at the last input-token position, before generation of the first output token. A calibration corpus of 100 control pairs was used to establish an empirical decision threshold based on cosine distance. The experimental contrast compared the internal representations generated by the inputs “Astra apre la cerniera rossa” and “Astra produce la cerniera rossa.” The preregistered 95th-percentile threshold was α95 = 0.16388282775878904. The observed experimental cosine distance was DC,exp = 0.12600135803222656. Therefore, H0 was not rejected in this exploratory Phase 1: the experimental contrast did not produce a representational distance anomalous relative to the calibration distribution. Importantly, Phase 1 does not directly test the human-side event operationally labelled “cortocircuito simbiotico” (symbiotic short-circuit), nor does it provide evidence for or against consciousness, subjective experience, persistent memory, human–AI symbiosis, or causal coupling between a human and a language model. It should instead be interpreted as a preliminary test of the MMSL computational-state recording and analysis pipeline and of a specific minimal semantic contrast. The deposited materials include the frozen protocol and calibration corpus, integrity information, execution notebook, calibration and experimental archives, pre-unblinding record, final experimental report, interpretative note, and a post-experimental addendum documenting deviations identified during independent verification. These deviations were not corrected retrospectively, and the preregistered result remains unchanged. Author and project lead: Maria Alvuela Franco.AI systems were used during technical formalization, methodological review and cross-review. Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 served as the experimental system. AI contributions do not constitute experimental evidence and do not replace the author’s responsibility for the research question, protocol decisions, execution and interpretation.

title: Towards inclusive voice biometrics: Dysarthria-discriminative embeddings for ASV system
abstract: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) performance degrades considerably for individuals with dysarthria due to articulatory impairments and increased acoustic variability. This study proposes two discriminative front-end acoustic feature embeddings to improve dysarthric ASV: discriminative bottleneck (DBN) embeddings learned through a CNN-based control-dysarthria classification task, and discriminative contrastive bottleneck embeddings (DCBN) derived from a Siamese network with contrastive learning. Each embedding type is independently fused with Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients and refined via principal component analysis to form compact ASV front end representation. Experimental evaluations on the TORGO and UA-Speech datasets demonstrate consistent improvements across all dysarthria severity levels, with DCBN achieving the most substantial gains due to enhanced speaker-discriminative learning. When integrated with an ECAPA-TDNN back end, the proposed approach yields relative reductions of 16.35% in equal error rate (EER) and 31.75% in minimum detection cost function (min DCF) over the baseline. These findings confirm the effectiveness of dysarthria discriminative embeddings in enabling more reliable and inclusive ASV system for dysarthric speakers.

title: EXTp: A Soundness Theorem for Counterfactual Exploit Replay on Formally Verified Microkernels
abstract: Counterfactual exploit analysis -- determining which input parameter causally produced an observed outcome -- is pervasive in security research, but its current practice is epistemically unsound. Three gaps separate "different outcome" from "caused by the change": non-deterministic replay noise, replay-machinery side-effects, and causal pathways traversing microarchitectural state invisible to the analyst's surface. We present EXTp, a counterfactual replay framework on bare-metal seL4, and the Counterfactual Soundness Theorem (CST) -- the first formal soundness theorem for counterfactual causal attribution grounded in a verified microkernel substrate. EXTp realizes three observable properties: Capability Separation (Pearl modularity; Clopper-Pearson bound <= 0.37% at N=998), Strong Observational Equivalence (replay determinism: score_S = 1.0000 over N=34 cross-boot trials, Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95% upper bound on the per-run failure rate <= 10.4%), and Measurement Interference (calibrated timing threshold, realized false-positive rate 0.61%-2.78%). CST proves their composition grounds Pearl/Halpern-Pearl causal attribution within enumerated epistemic bounds; CST v1.0 establishes soundness under single-VCPU intervention scope and bare-metal microcode-stable configurations, with multi-VCPU and cross-configuration extensions charted as future work. A synthetic analog modeled on the CrackArmor confused-deputy pattern, executed on bare-metal Intel Alder Lake, exercises the pipeline end-to-end and shows the framework correctly detecting its own A1-modulo violations.

title: Stress-Testing Byzantine Robustness in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Adaptive Adversaries and an Alternative Filtering Anchor
abstract: Large language model agents deployed over peer-to-peer networks can improve reliability through consensus, but faulty or adversarial agents can propagate errors through the same channels. Self-Anchored Consensus (SAC; Lee et al., arXiv:2605.09076) addresses this with a decentralized filter-and-refine protocol: each agent scores its neighbors' responses locally, discards the lowest-scoring ones relative to its own self-score, and refines its answer on the remainder. The original evaluation, however, models the adversary as an agent replaying a fixed incorrect response with falsified confidence — an attack the authors identify as a limitation, noting that adversaries crafted to appear correct to the receiver-side scorer are not addressed by the current filtering mechanism. This project examines that gap. We implement stronger adversarial agents using attack templates designed to mimic the structure of honest responses rather than replaying out-of-distribution output, and we evaluate SAC under this threat model. We further replace SAC's self-score filtering anchor with a median-of-neighbors anchor, on the reasoning that anchoring to one's own score limits how much a weak agent can benefit from more capable neighbors. In preliminary experiments using gpt-4o-mini as strong agents and gpt-3.5-turbo as weak agents at n=7 and F=3 across (F+1)-robust topologies (γ-MERG, complete, and Erdos–Rényi random graphs), the modified protocol substantially increases weak-agent accuracy while also improving strong-agent accuracy — a departure from the original protocol, which preserves strong agents rather than lifting them. A matched-baseline comparison against the original self-anchored protocol on the same problems remains to be run. We additionally observe that reported robustness gains in this line of work are sensitive to sample size: the same method and configuration yield markedly different improvements across the two arXiv versions of the original paper, at n=30 and n=100. Current results use 20 mixed-difficulty problems spanning MATH500 Levels 1–5 and are preliminary; evaluation on the full Level 4 subset, with multiple seeds and an ablation isolating the anchor modification, is in progress.

title: A dual stream architecture integrating pathology foundation models for automated tumor region segmentation in Ki-67 assessment
abstract: The quantification of the Ki-67 proliferation index is a cornerstone in breast cancer prognosis and treatment planning. While deep learning has shown promise, traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) lack global context, and standard vision transformers struggle with local boundary delineation. Recently, pathology-specific foundation models (FMs) like Phikon and UNI have emerged, offering robust feature representations. However, applying these patch-based models directly to pixel-wise segmentation remains challenging due to the loss of spatial resolution. In this work, we propose the dual-stream U-Net (DSU), a novel hybrid architecture designed to bridge the gap between the semantic power of foundation models and the spatial precision required for tumoral segmentation. Our approach integrates a frozen FM backbone (validating both Phikon and UNI ) with a parallel lightweight CNN encoder. This dual-stream design allows the model to leverage robust high-level semantic features from the FM while recovering fine-grained spatial details through the CNN stream. Furthermore, we employ a full-scale aggregation decoder to fuse multi-scale information dynamically. Experimental results using a leave-one-subject-out (cross-validation demonstrate that the DSU architecture achieves robust performance, outperforming traditional baselines (U-Net, TransUNet). Furthermore, incorporating boundary-sensitive metrics such as the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance confirms that DSU provides improved structural fidelity at the edges. While single-stream decoders can achieve comparable or higher volumetric overlap in some regimes, evaluations on independent test data reveal that Phikon-DSU and Uni-DSU provide improved spatial boundary delineation. These findings suggest that the proposed DSU framework offers a clinically viable preliminary proof-of-concept for leveraging foundation models in histology segmentation, serving as a first step toward automated Ki-67 scoring.

title: Dual-Process Neuro-Symbolic Cognitive Architecture for Zero-Token Program Synthesis via Hyperdimensional Associative Resonance
abstract: Current foundation models (Large Language Models, LLMs) dominate automated software engineering and code generation, but they suffer from severe energy inefficiencies, recurrent token latency (2,000–10,000 ms per inference), non-deterministic hallucination, and lack of persistent lifelong memory. Biological cognitive systems, by contrast, employ a rapid, sub-conscious associative memory (System 1) to resolve familiar recurring challenges, invoking deliberate, resource-intensive deliberation (System 2) strictly when novel epistemic uncertainty is encountered. In this work, we present Oscurus, an asynchronous, dual-process neuro-symbolic cognitive architecture designed for continuous, on-device algorithmic synthesis. System 1 is anchored by a high-performance Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC / Vector Symbolic Architectures) substrate operating in D = 10,000 dimensions with native SIMD hardware acceleration (POPCNT, achieving 6.35 million bitwise operations per second). Structural algorithmic archetypes and Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) primitives are mapped into orthogonal hypervectors. When incoming problem specifications match consolidated Hebbian memory states above an adaptive certainty threshold, System 1 synthesizes and executes verified code in 5–15 ms with zero LLM tokens and zero GPU VRAM consumption. If epistemic certainty indicates high topological novelty, the system orchestrates a reflective System 2 query to a generative foundation model. Validated solutions produced by System 2 are subsequently distilled into System 1 via associative Hebbian plasticity, systematically expanding the offline zero-token boundary. title: Machine Learning for Quantum Error Mitigation: A Systematic Review of Techniques, Evidence, and Limits
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) reduces the bias that hardware noise introduces into estimated observables, at the cost of additional circuit repetitions. Machine learning has been applied to it extensively since 2020, with reported reductions in that overhead. This systematic review synthesises that literature for the period January 2020 to September 2026. The review addresses three questions. First, whether the literature divides more informatively by what a model learns — a noise model, an extrapolation map, a direct noisy-to-ideal correction, or a circuit-level policy — than by its architecture. Second, what fraction of published work reports accuracy validation outside the classically simulable regime, given that supervised mitigation requires ideal reference values obtainable only where a circuit is classically tractable. Third, whether reported gains can be placed on a common scale, and how they stand against established information-theoretic lower bounds on the sampling cost of mitigation. Conducted per PRISMA 2020 with documented adaptations for a non-clinical computing literature.

title: Cognitive Surrender in AI-Mediated Education: Behavioral Reliance, Prospective Signals, and Governance for Human Cognitive Agency
abstract: This repository contains the analysis code, aggregate derived results, figures, tables, and reproducibility materials supporting the manuscript “Cognitive Surrender in AI-Mediated Education: Behavioral Reliance, Prospective Signals, and Governance for Human Cognitive Agency.” The study examines reliance-oriented behavioral patterns in student-Large Language Model (LLM) interactions using the publicly available StudyChat dataset. It analyzes 16,851 student-LLM interactions from 203 users across 2,214 chat sessions and investigates whether observable interaction traces can characterize patterns of AI-mediated reliance. The repository includes the final analysis pipeline used to construct and evaluate the prototype Reliance Index (RI), an exploratory behavioral composite designed to summarize interaction patterns associated with output seeking, limited contextualization, temporal escalation from hints to direct-solution requests, repeated prompting, code/data conversion, and limited observable evidence of prior independent effort. The RI is intended as a research instrument, not a diagnostic or psychometric measure of cognitive surrender. The archived analyses include cleaned intent distributions, RI distributions across users and StudyChat topics, comparisons between the RI and an independently constructed Struggle Index, robustness and sensitivity analyses, and a temporally separated prospective analysis examining whether features observed during the first 20% of each user's interactions contain information associated with reliance-oriented behavior during the subsequent observation period. RI robustness was evaluated using equal weighting, Monte Carlo perturbation of component weights, and leave-one-component-out specifications. Under equal weighting, the RI showed a Spearman rank correlation of 0.953 with the baseline specification. Across 1,000 random ±20% weight perturbations, the median Spearman correlation was approximately 0.995, with a 5th-95th percentile range of approximately 0.980-0.999. Leave-one-component-out analyses indicated that RI ordering was more sensitive to removal of low-context prompting and write-code requests than to moderate numerical weight perturbations. The prospective analysis used temporally non-overlapping predictor and outcome periods. Logistic Regression achieved an AUC of 0.584 and Random Forest an AUC of 0.598 for identifying users in the highest quartile of subsequent-period RI. Feature-set ablation showed that interaction-volume features alone performed approximately at chance, while reliance-oriented and combined behavioral features provided modest prospective discrimination. These results are interpreted as preliminary evidence of temporal structure in interaction behavior rather than as support for individual-level prediction or automated intervention. The repository is organized into directories containing the final analysis code, aggregate result tables, analysis summaries, empirical figures, and conceptual manuscript figures. The included README provides instructions for reproducing the analyses.

title: Dahal Jeet: game engine, agents and experimental record
abstract: First public release, accompanying the manuscript "Search-based agents outperform reinforcement learning in Dahal Jeet, a Nepali imperfect-information card game", under review at Scientific Reports. Contains the game engine, 26 agents spanning hand-written heuristics, metaheuristic tuning, PIMC and single- and multiple-observer ISMCTS, and seven families of learning agent; every trained checkpoint; the complete result artifacts behind the paper; and the compute record. Every reported value is generated from an artifact rather than typed: paper_numbers.py emits them as LaTeX macros, paper_tables.py builds the tables, and verify_equations.py recomputes 30 of the manuscript's identities directly against the stored artifacts without re-running any experiment. All 30 pass. Code is MIT; data, models and figures are CC BY 4.0.
