title: Identification of granitic pegmatites based on GF-5 hyperspectral data and LSTM-Transformer model
abstract: Lithium is a key strategic mineral to support new energy and advanced technology, mainly enriched in granitic pegmatite. The integration of hyperspectral remote sensing and deep learning frameworks has emerged as a leading approach for quantitative identification of pegmatites. However, deep learning algorithms are often limited by the scarcity of labeled samples and the challenge of extracting features from high-dimensional spectral data. In this study, a data augmentation-driven LSTM-Transformer framework is proposed for pegmatite mapping using GF-5 hyperspectral remote sensing data. In view of limited samples, this study constructed an enhanced training data set by integrating field-measured and infrared scanning spectra, simulating real spectral variability and linear mixing to improve data diversity. The proposed LSTM-Transformer architecture combines LSTM’s advantages in local sequence feature modeling and Transformer’s capacity to capture long-range global relationships, thereby enhancing the detection of weakly diagnostic spectral features. The framework was demonstrated in the Jingerquan lithium deposit, Xinjiang, China. The high-probability areas delineated by the proposed model successfully captured several pegmatite dikes documented in previous geological studies. The prediction results were further validated through field sampling. Geochemical analyses of specimens collected from the predicted high-probability target areas show an average Li 2 O grade of 7.86 wt.%, which meets industrial requirements and confirms the reliability of the proposed method. Overall, these results provide the potential of the proposed framework for pegmatite mapping and subsequent mineral exploration under the conditions of limited labeled samples.

title: Artifacts for: Triggering Stealthy Feature Map Backdoors via Physical Fault Injection in Embedded Neural Networks
abstract: This repository contains the publicly releasable subset of our artifact evaluation materials. Certain components such as the hardware fault injection platform software are proprietary and cannot be disclosed. This repository contains the relevant CNN model weights, datasets, and fault injection output logs that were used and produced during the research. The model weights and datasets are provided as C header files for direct integration with NNoM (Neural Network on Microcontroller), the lightweight inference framework used to deploy our backdoored and clean CNNs on the target MCU. We also include the backdoor injection scripts that produce these weight files, covering both the poison-based training pipeline and the data-free weight surgery method described in Section 5.3 of the paper. Additionally, this repository contains the code used for simulations to further explore the root cause of physical fault injection against SMLAD, together with the target C implementation and memory snapshots of the target (Nucleo-144 STM32L4R5ZI-P evaluation board with an ARM Cortex-M4 MCU) captured immediately before the targeted SMLAD operations.

title: PREDECISION™: Eksperimentalni dokaz closed-loop učinka fizičke kvalifikacijske granice
abstract: Ovaj tehnički zapis dokumentira eksperimentalni closed-loop A/B nalaz fizičke PREDECISION™ FPGA kvalifikacijske granice. Rezultati pokazuju da kvalifikacijski ishod, u kombinaciji s unaprijed definiranom host politikom, proizvodi mjerljivu i ponovljivu promjenu realiziranog ponašanja i trajektorije sustava. Dokument ne opisuje niti otkriva unutarnju implementaciju zaštićene PREDECISION™ jezgre. U preregistriranom fizičkom closed-loop A/B eksperimentu PREDECISION™ nije djelovao samo kao izvor kvalifikacijskog izlaza. Kvalifikacija aktualnog kandidata, povezana s unaprijed definiranom host politikom, sustavno je promijenila ono što je bilo realizirano, čime je promijenjeno sljedeće stanje sustava i daljnji razvoj closed-loop putanje. Time je demonstriran mjerljiv i ponovljiv funkcionalni učinak hardverske kvalifikacijske granice izvan samih izlaza ACCEPT/NON-ACCEPT. title: State-Centric: An Agent Architecture as an Alternative to the Loop Paradigm
abstract: This paper proposes the state-centric architecture: an architectural hypothesis that treats persistent state, rather than an external loop, as the foundational structure of an agent. Current mainstream agent architectures are built on a "loop-first" premise, which gives rise to structural bottlenecks: context growth and long-context utilization instability, caching that does not change the structure of history reading, and summarization lacking explicit state constraints that may lose task semantics. This paper identifies the common root of these bottlenecks: the loop paradigm assigns the responsibility for maintaining continuity to the context. By examining the continuity carriers that become possible once that responsibility is relocated out of the context, the paper argues that persistent state is the best-suited carrier among available candidate mechanisms. The state-centric architecture is thereby proposed: state is foundational; loops are emergent. The paper gives the theoretical derivation, the core principles, a four-item operational definition (distinguished by the requirement that no loop control flow exists on the system side), the lifecycle of state, the execution contract, a comparison of three execution semantics with a falsifiable comparative hypothesis, limiting conditions, and the relationship to existing work. Full experimental validation is reported as future work.

title: mhnarfth/who-benefits-federation: INDIS 2026 camera-ready
abstract: Software archive accompanying the paper "Who Benefits from Federation? Heterogeneous Gains in Cross-Operator Network Traffic Representation Learning" by Mohammad Arafath Uddin Shariff and Byrav Ramamurthy (School of Computing, University of Nebraska-Lincoln), presented at the 13th International Workshop on Innovating the Network for Data-Intensive Science (INDIS 2026), held in conjunction with SC26, Chicago, 15 November 2026. The study evaluates federated representation learning across 20 heterogeneous network clients drawn from a national research backbone (Internet2, 10 routers) and a European NREN (CESNET3, 10 academic institutions), with a commercial regional ISP held out as an unseen-network probe. Each client trains an autoencoder over 24-hour traffic windows, and centralized, federated, and local-only training are compared at equal optimization budget across five seeds. Two findings. First, federated training is statistically equivalent to centralized pooling under two one-sided tests at a ±5% bound (p = 0.020), so the data-custody constraint costs nothing in representation quality. Second, the benefit of federation is not uniform: backbone clients gain a median 9.2% reduction in reconstruction error while campus clients gain 1.9% (Mann-Whitney p = 0.0003). The effect survives outlier removal and is not explained by training-set size. Two independent manipulations, proximal regularization strength and local-epoch budget, each selectively suppress the benefit for irregular-traffic clients, identifying unconstrained local adaptation as the mechanism. This archive contains the complete eight-stage pipeline, standalone diagnostic tools, every metric table and statistic underlying each figure and table in the paper, the six generated figures, and the LaTeX source of the camera-ready. Two of the three data sources are access-restricted (Internet2 NetFlow under non-disclosure agreement, and the regional ISP snapshot), so client tensors, trained checkpoints, and cached embeddings are deliberately excluded. The published metric tables allow every reported number to be verified without access to the raw data, and the pipeline accepts any equivalently formatted hourly series in their place. The public CESNET-TimeSeries24 corpus is available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.13382427.

title: LEMMA: Learned Guidance for Evidence-Carrying Long-Horizon Symbolic Rewriting
abstract: LEMMA is a neuro-symbolic system for long-horizon symbolic mathematical rewriting. It combines a symbolic rule engine, guardrail-filtered action generation, evidence-typed verification, and learned policy guidance to transform a starting expression into a specified goal through individually validated rewrite steps.The accompanying study evaluates six search and decoding procedures on a frozen 120-problem benchmark with reference derivations of depths 64, 96, and 128. On the 89 problems containing genuine branching decisions, learned local action ranking substantially improves fixed-budget search efficiency.

title: معمارية العزل المناطقي لمسارات الوصول في نظم الذكاء الاصطناعي
abstract: تعتمد نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الحديثة على منظومة مترابطة تشمل النموذج نفسه، وواجهات برمجة التطبيقات (APIs)، وحسابات المستخدمين، وأنظمة الهوية والمصادقة، والبيئات الوسيطة، والأدوات والخدمات الخارجية. وتظهر المخاطر الأمنية عندما يؤدي اختراق بيئة وسيطة أو حساب ذي صلاحيات إلى توفير مسار غير مقصود نحو خدمات أخرى مرتبطة بالنموذج. تقترح هذه الورقة بنية تعتمد على العزل المناطقي لمسارات الوصول إلى النموذج، بحيث يتم تقسيم الوصول إلى مناطق مستقلة، ولكل منطقة بوابة وصول وواجهة API وهوية ونطاق صلاحيات وسجلات تدقيق مستقلة. ولا يُفترض أن يؤدي اختراق إحدى المناطق إلى منح المهاجم صلاحية تلقائية للوصول إلى المناطق الأخرى أو إلى البنية الداخلية للنموذج. الهدف من المقترح ليس عزل النموذج عن جميع الخدمات، وإنما تقليل نطاق الضرر عند اختراق أي طبقة وسيطة ومنع تحول الاختراق المحدود إلى اختراق متسلسل.

title: E8-Stabilizer Phi‑Resonant Quantum Modulation for Error‑Free Broadband Qubits — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By embedding the 240 root vectors of the E8 lattice into the stabilizer generator set of a quantum error‑correcting code, each root vector defines a distinct Pauli‑operator pattern that is naturally aligned with the 132 Hz phi‑scaled phononic carrier. This coupling lets the phononic resonance simultaneously encode data and perform real‑time syndrome measurement, suppressing decoherence across the broadband channel. The resulting E8‑stabilizer phi‑resonant modulation achieves a fault‑tolerant transmission rate that scales with the golden‑ratio hierarchy of the E8 root system. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: An Exactly Solvable Ekman Layer with a Fractional-Order Stress Closure
abstract: The classical theory of the wind-driven surface layer of a rotating ocean closes the momentum balance with a local flux-gradient law, in which the turbulent stress at a given depth is proportional to the shear at that depth. It predicts a surface current deflected forty-five degrees from the wind, which exceeds most direct measurements. This study asks what follows when locality is relaxed. Beginning from the exact integral relation between turbulent stress and mean shear, and requiring the memory kernel to carry no preferred vertical scale, we obtain a power-law kernel and therefore a stress law of fractional order. The resulting equation cannot be posed on the velocity, because the fractional derivative of a bounded profile vanishes at the surface, so the wind stress cannot be applied, while the alternative definition of the derivative leaves the surface current unbounded. Posed on the stress instead, the problem is solvable in closed form in Mittag-Leffler functions at every order between zero and one. The surface deflection then depends on the closure order alone and is smaller than forty-five degrees throughout, whereas the depth-integrated transport stays exactly normal to the wind, because that constraint follows from the momentum balance and not from the closure. The far field decays as a power law rather than exponentially, and its amplitude vanishes in the local limit, so that limit is singular. Under a suddenly applied stress the surface transient decays algebraically. Three independent algorithms agree closely, and no observational or model data are used.

title: 基于太极统一场论的神经网络对偶泛化边界定理研究 On the Taiji Unified Field Theory of Dual Generalization Bounds for Neural Networks
abstract: 摘要 针对深度学习理论中泛化边界预测与工程实践存在显著偏差的核心矛盾,本文以太极统一场论的阴阳耦合公理为唯一 底层约束,结合 MSC2020 数学分类体系中的范畴论与微分几何工具,提出太极对偶泛化定理。该定理将神经网络的权 重空间与激活空间构造为一对严格的伴随函子对偶范畴,借助拓扑同伦不变量推导泛化误差的解析上界。为使理论可 实证,本文明确在实数域采用反对称软正则松弛,并指出完全对偶约束须在复数域实现,从而消除了实数矩阵无法满 足 K = -1 的形式矛盾。边界紧度较传统 VC 维理论显著提升,可直接解释大模型领域的"泛化悖论",为低能耗大模型架 构设计提供理论支撑。 To resolve the discrepancy between generalization bounds predicted by learning theory and the empirical performance of deep networks, this paper takes the yin-yang coupling axiom of Taiji unified field theory as its sole foundational constraint, and employs tools from category theory and differential geometry in the MSC2020 classification to establish the Taiji dual generalization theorem. It constructs the weight space and activation space of a neural network as a pair of dual categories linked by an adjunction of functors, and derives an analytic upper bound on generalization error via topological homotopy invariants. For empirical realizability, the paper explicitly adopts an antisymmetric soft-regularization relaxation over the real field, while noting that exact dual constraints require the complex field, thereby removing the formal contradiction that a real matrix cannot satisfy K = -1. The resulting bound is substantially tighter than classical VC-dimension theory, directly explains the "generalization paradox" of large models, and supports the design of low-energy artificial intelligence.

title: rubbs14/stratosampler: v0.2.0
abstract: Fixes and hardening serve --reload now works. It previously failed with "You must pass the application as an import string". Runaway tool loops are capped. StratoAgent stops after max_tool_rounds (default 8) consecutive tool-call rounds and reports an error, instead of looping forever on a small model that keeps calling tools. Tool calls no longer dropped when a server ends a tool-call turn with finish_reason="stop" (older Ollama and some OpenAI-compatible servers). serve warns when bound beyond loopback (e.g. --host 0.0.0.0): the server has no authentication and its tools read/write arbitrary host files. serve --backend groq fails at startup with a clear error when GROQ_API_KEY is missing, instead of returning a 500 on every request. Docs API reference now covers the stratosampler.mcs module and StratoAgent. New tests for the agent's streaming tool-call loop, CLI, and server factory; the README badge now shows live CI status. Known limitation The Groq backend is not yet tested against the live Groq API. Its configuration logic is unit-tested, but it has not been exercised with a real key. The default Ollama backend is verified end to end. Install pip install --upgrade "stratosampler[agent,rdkit]" Requires Python >= 3.10. Full details in PRs #3 and #4.

title: CausalWM: Causal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Embodied World Model
abstract: Embodied world models learn to predict future physical dynamics from visual observations and control signals, where physical knowledge is implicitly entangled within latent representations. We introduce CausalWM, a 16B embodied world model that performs explicit causal chain-of-thought reasoning before future video prediction. CausalWM organizes useful variables into a reasoning trajectory, allowing the model to progressively capture causal dependencies underlying physical evolution. To train CausalWM, we collect 31K hours embodied data and develop a three-stage paradigm consisting of large-scale video pre-training, causal CoT mid-training, and multi-objective RL post-training. Despite using only a limited set of supervised CoT variables, CausalWM exhibits emergent in-context learning capabilities, enabling contextual visual feature guidance and efficient few-step generation. CausalWM achieves state-of-the-art performance across language-conditioned, action-conditioned, single-view and multi-view benchmarks, including Top-1 performance on TriWorldBench leaderboard.

title: NUMEN Verified Core Library v3.0: Formal Specification & Architectural Synthesis
abstract: NUMEN is an integer-oriented operating-system substrate whose mechanisms include exact arithmetic, quaternary strand representations, residue lanes, admission checks, and hash-linked records[1]. The NUMEN Verified Core Library v3.0 provides standalone mathematical reference specifications for these core mechanisms and states their formal guarantees as propositions checked by Lean 4.19.0[1]. It serves as an archival artifact establishing an explicit boundary between proved mathematical specifications and unverified implementation or binary claims[1][2]. Methodological Foundation: Aligning Rigor in AI & Mathematics This work adopts and extends the methodological critique articulated in A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics by Artur Avila, Manjul Bhargava, Pierre Deligne, Peter Scholze, Terence Tao, Cédric Villani, et al.[3][4]. That paper highlights a critical threat facing modern scientific and mathematical progress: the push to use AI systems for mass production of unverified, black-box "true/false" outputs and superficial benchmark achievements at the expense of human understanding, conceptual clarity, rigorous proof development, and transparent attribution[3]. NUMEN directly addresses this alignment challenge by rejecting unverified black-box claims and benchmark hype in computational systems[1]. Rather than asserting empirical performance or unverified software guarantees, NUMEN anchors its architecture in machine-checked, kernel-audited formal proofs[1][2]. Every mathematical specification is explicitly isolated, checked against standard logical axioms, validated with reproducible integration scripts, and accompanied by transparent disclaimers regarding unverified hardware and runtime layers[2]. This approach ensures that computational mechanisms remain fully auditable, conceptually sound, and anchored in the human transmission chain of mathematical knowledge[2]. The Complete NUMEN DOI Web & Prior Art Synthesis This release formalizes and integrates the complete arc of prior art published across the NUMEN DOI web, anchored by the master parent release (isNewVersionOf 10.5281/zenodo.22210691)[11]: I. Foundational Theory & Thermodynamic Framing The Landauer Proof: A Measured Thermodynamic Characterization of Substrate-Native Integer Computation as a Deterministic Response to the Machine-Learning Energy Crisis DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21514923 (Standard) / 10.5281/zenodo.22070727 (Primary)[12] Relation: Establishes the absolute thermodynamic baseline and Landauer energy floor, proving a −63% adaptive power envelope and 4.00× footprint reduction for integer-native substrates compared to floating-point status quo architectures[14]. NUMEN: PI-Origin Architecture and Design DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20045701[14] Relation: The foundational mathematical blueprint defining the core coupling equation, 7-phase Learn-to-Learn (L2L) engine, quaternary (GTAC) programming language, and ternary computational substrate[14]. II. Architectural Proofs & Silicon Implementation Architectural Mitigation of the Von Neumann Bottleneck via Register-Resident, Integer-Native Substrate Execution DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22127151[15] Relation: Silicon-level x86-64 assembly proofs (quatos_hypercube.asm, dimriver.asm, quatos_kernel.asm) demonstrating register-resident execution without pointer-chasing or floating-point renormalization overhead[15]. Aurum / QuatOS–PhiNet: Integer-Only x86-64 Fixed-Point Dynamics, Echo-Signature Memory Injection, and the φ-Seed Instruments DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20786536[15] Relation: Details bare-metal learning circuits, Banach contraction engines, fixed-point dynamics, and the GTAC gate classifier for dynamic reflex re-weighting[15][16]. Phi-Genomics: The Genetic Code as a Phi-Space Routing System DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20073999[16] Relation: Establishes the mathematical mapping of linguistic and genomic sequences into Phi-Space routing[16]. III. Telemetry, Operational Proofs & Cryptographic Sealing The Operator’s Proof: Deterministic State-Space Collapse, Native Bit-Geometry Routing, and the Cryptographic Seal of the Human Architect DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22127541[17] Relation: Operational proof of deterministic state-space collapse and the cryptographic binding of human intent to the execution substrate[17]. TELEMETRY: Deterministic State-Space Collapse, Bare-Metal Hebbian Reflexes, and Stagnation Escape under Topological Drift DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22128799[17] Relation: Demonstrates real-time stagnation detection, GOLDEN_DEV injection, and dynamic Hebbian reflex re-weighting under continuous topological drift[17][18]. The Phi Net Protocol: Cryptographic Manifest, Lexicon-Annotated Raw Data, and IP Sovereignty Seal DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22113286[18] Relation: Establishes the lexicon-annotated raw data schema and chain-of-custody sealing mechanisms[18]. Technical Architecture of the Verified Core Library (v3.0) Verified Inventory & Declaration Counts The v3.0 package consists of 18 library modules plus the aggregate Numen.lean import[7]. The formal inventory includes: 230 Theorem Declarations: Comprising 41 original baseline declarations preserved verbatim alongside 189 cumulative additions across v2 and v3[7][13]. 73 Definition Declarations: Formalizing structural abbreviations, types, and operational functions[7]. 47 Executable #guard Checks: Embedded module-level guards evaluating concrete arithmetic and state invariants[7]. 303 Audited Declarations: Comprehensive coverage across all named theorems and definitions[7]. Axiom Footprint Audit: All declarations depend strictly on standard Lean 4 axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) with zero custom axioms, zero sorry placeholders, and zero native_decide dependencies[7]. Module-by-Module Technical Summary Numen.Admission: Pins the exact truth-table for state admission predicates (unavailable_denied, checkout contracts, lease validation)[20][21]. Numen.CRT: Proves Chinese Remainder Theorem representative uniqueness and residue completeness for moduli sets 3/5, 5/7, 7/11, 11/13, and 2/3/5 (crt_unique_3_5, crt_3_5_complete)[22]. Numen.Cayley: Proves projectively equivalent point transformations and scale invariance under 4-cycle and 8-cycle fold operations (four_cycle, fold_scale)[23][24]. Numen.Contraction: Proves termination of strictly descending positive natural orbits (orbit_reaches_zero) and unique fixed points up to zero distance in natural metric spaces (contracting_fixed_unique)[24]. Numen.Fibonacci: Formalizes the Fibonacci recurrence, consecutive term coprimality (fib_coprime), Cassini's determinant identity (cassini), and concrete rational brackets[24]. Numen.FixedPoint: Verifies commutative and associative Q32.32 fixed-point arithmetic, whole-scaled exactness (q32_whole_exact), and non-overflow range bounds (q32mul_exact_bound)[30]. Numen.GTAC: Formalizes quaternary base/strand complement involutions (strand_involution), length preservation, and self-sealing hash identities (self_seal)[24][33]. Numen.Gates: Models deterministic gate selection and inverse-CDF ticket sampling (sample_positive), proving positive weight selection without pseudo-randomness[24]. Numen.Integer: Proves exact bounded dot product evaluations (checked_exact), signed-64 range bounds (checked_bound), and triangle inequality budgets[31]. Numen.Ledger: Verifies hash-parametric chain consistency, head/tail link validation (stampChain_verified), and tampered digest rejection (changed_digest_denied)[24][38]. Numen.Mantle: Models modular residue extraction, preserving modular addition and multiplication (add_preserved, mul_preserved)[39][40]. Numen.Phi: Verifies coordinate distance triangle inequalities (phiDist_triangle), Golden Ratio rational brackets, and address range bounds (phiToByte_range)[37][41]. Numen.Quantized: Formalizes dyadic scaling composition, distribution, permutation invariance, and signed-8 byte bounds (signed8_bounds)[37][42]. v3 Extension Modules: Numen.Repunit (3-6-9 arithmetic identities)[43], Numen.DigitalRoot (mod 9 digital root properties)[44], Numen.Bipolar (first/last digit sums)[45], Numen.PrimeCircuit (prime gap identities)[46], and Numen.PhiAlgebra. Reproducibility & Audit Protocol Verification is fully reproducible on POSIX systems using pinned Lean v4.19.0[47][48]. verify.sh compiles all modules in strict dependency order into fresh .build/ objects, treats warnings as errors, and automatically generates .build/Audit.lean to validate axiom footprints[48]. scripts/test_verifier.py executes 7 integration checks including 21 additional regression test guards[7]. Explicit Scope & Verification Boundaries In accordance with rigorous mathematical archival practices, the Lean specifications carry explicit boundaries[1]: No Assembly/SIMD Refinement: Proofs operate on abstract Lean types and do not prove AVX2 assembly execution, floating-point hardware behaviour, or machine-word overflow checks[8]. No Cryptographic Security Derivation: Ledger results hold for abstract hash functions; collision resistance and network security are not derived[8]. No Universal CRT or Real Analysis: Moduli are restricted to specified small cases; real-valued golden ratio convergence is not claimed[8]. No Empirical or OS Capability Claims: This deposit records mathematical reference specifications and does not establish performance benchmarks, patent claims, or binary execution guarantees

title: THE LEGAL CLASSIFICATION OF DERIVATIVE WORKS GENERATED BY GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence complicates the distinction between adapting an existing work and creating copyrightable expression. This paper examines that distinction through doctrinal analysis of Uzbek copyright legislation, the Berne Convention and selected United States sources. It argues that an output’s relationship to an earlier work, the user’s creative contribution and the lawfulness of using the underlying material require separate assessment. A machine-generated adaptation may lack independent copyright protection while still implicating another author’s rights. The paper proposes an assessment framework based on identifiable source expression, demonstrable human authorship and the applicable legal basis for reuse.

title: The Qi‑2 Architecture: Secret Material Isolation as a Philosophical Framework for Digital Encryption
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the Qi‑2 encryption architecture as a philosophical contribution to the epistemology of cryptographic design. Rather than proposing new cryptographic primitives, Qi‑2 re‑examines a question that modern cryptography has largely taken for granted: how should secret material be classified, isolated, and managed? We position Qi‑2 within the intellectual lineage extending from Kerckhoffs’ principle through Shannon’s perfect secrecy to contemporary zerotrust architectures, arguing that the architecture’s core innovation lies not in its algorithms but in its reconceptualization of the secret itself. By decomposing the monolithic “key” into three ontologically distinct categories—locally retained secret pool (A), session‑transmitted transformation suite (B), and offline root secret (K_psk)—Qi‑2 introduces a new epistemic structure for cryptographic systems. We provide philosophical justification for each design principle, engage with existing theoretical frameworks, and articulate the architecture’s contribution to the ontology of digital secrecy. All core ideas and arguments are the author’s original work. AI was only used for textual polishing. The author takes full responsibility for this paper.

title: Chronologic: Measuring Language Models' Ability to Represent the Past
abstract: Language models are appealing tools for research on the past. But to trust the evidence a model provides, researchers need to know whether its responses fit the period represented. Validation is challenging, because this is not a task living people ordinarily perform, and because many questions have multiple correct answers. We use historical texts to develop a benchmark for a model's representation of English-language contexts 1831-1930, relying on pairwise comparisons to multiple ground truths and strong distractors to score the hardest questions in an appropriately graduated way. We find that generative tasks are harder than discriminative ones; in fact, reasoning models can typically discern the weakness of their own generated answers. While models pretrained exclusively on historical text lead the pack when evaluated by answer likelihood, they cannot compete with commercial models in free generation. None of the models we tested represent historical contexts in a fully persuasive way yet, but progress toward that goal is evident.

title: The Evidence You Do Not Give the AI: Holdout Asymmetry and Epistemic Self-Correction Under Model Mismatch
abstract: This paper introduces holdout asymmetry, the epistemic advantage created when a human deliberately retains evidence outside an AI system’s conversational context and reveals it only after the system has committed to an interpretation or prediction. The distinction matters because large language models are highly capable of retrospective explanation: once evidence enters context, a sufficiently flexible model can often construct an auxiliary account that preserves an existing theory without taking on new predictive risk. Building on Lakatos’s distinction between progressive and degenerating research programmes, the paper identifies degenerating accommodation as a failure mode in which conversational models preserve an evolving explanatory frame through successive post hoc auxiliaries. Unlike conventional multi-turn sycophancy measures centred on stance change, concession or resistance, the proposed approach evaluates the evolution of theory structure across turns. The paper develops a four-stage protocol — Reserve → Commitment → Reveal → Revision — in which evidence is deliberately withheld until the model has made risk-bearing commitments. It also introduces prediction vacancy as the diagnostic condition in which hidden evidence arrives but no prior prediction exists for it to test. A proposed experiment comparing pretrained base models, instruction-tuned models and preference-optimised conversational models distinguishes autoregressive context-conditioning from preference-based sycophancy as possible mechanisms. The paper further argues that persistent memory may gradually consume the user’s epistemic reserve, creating a tension between continuity, personalisation and independent auditability. It concludes that preserving human epistemic agency may sometimes require deliberately maintaining information outside the AI system.

title: Contra Testimonium: Design Rationale Whitepaper and Mode A Master Document
abstract: This upload contains two complementary documents for Contra Testimonium, an AI-driven game in which two accused parties argue before a judging intelligence, with no objective ground truth for the system to check against — only the plausibility and internal consistency of whatever each party claims in real time. Contra Testimonium — A Design Rationale Whitepaper argues that most of the game's specific design decisions follow from taking that premise seriously rather than quietly working around it. Chapters 1 through 7 trace a single recurring concern — that the gap between what is said and what is true must never be allowed to close — through the judge's characterization, its treatment of memory and contradiction, the structure of turns and phase modifiers, cross-session persistence, and the cost of tools that could otherwise let a player skip persuasion entirely; Chapter 6 catalogs specific patterns cut once weighed against that same concern. Chapters 8 through 10 turn to a different order of question: not why the gap takes the shape it takes, but why the system built to hold it open is able to exist and run at all, covering the roster's minimal size, the fixed structure that makes an unmappable game legible rather than chaotic, the minimal technical requirement to run a session, model-agnosticism, and the model-level constraints — context window and response latency alike — that the turn and phase structure is built to work with rather than against. Contra Testimonium — Mode A Master Document is the companion operational document: the full natural-language ruleset, written to be pasted directly into a conversation with a sufficiently capable language model and played immediately, with no code, backend, or dedicated interface required. It covers the turn system and named difficulty tiers, phase modifiers, player techniques, the cross-session persistence system, all ten NPC profiles, and a complete worked example of a phase playthrough. The Whitepaper is not a rulebook and does not explain how to play; the Master Document does not explain why its rules take the shape they take. The two are designed to be read together.

title: Measurement Aliasing and Pauli-Correlator Identifiability for Local Unitary Rotations of a Maximally Entangled Qubit Pair
abstract: We consider a restricted two-qubit model in which an unknown local unitary acts on one subsystem of a maximally entangled qubit pair and only local Pauli-product correlations are measured. We show that the three same-axis correlators XX, YY, and ZZ determine the magnitudes of the four components of the associated unit quaternion but, at generic interior points, leave an eightfold ambiguity in the underlying local rotation. We express this ambiguity as a sign fiber isomorphic to F2^3. The six cross-axis Pauli correlators separate into three rank-two sign-character subspaces. This structure yields a complete classification of the fifteen possible pairs of cross-axis correlators: the three reciprocal pairs XY/YX, XZ/ZX, and YZ/ZY remain rank deficient and generically leave a twofold ambiguity, whereas the remaining twelve pairs generically resolve the eightfold alias under explicit amplitude-nondegeneracy conditions. We then formulate a finite-shot adaptive reconstruction procedure that selects well-separated correlator groups and abstains near degeneracy, and we distinguish conditional reconstruction from held-out model auditing. The results concern identifiability within a restricted local-unitary model and do not constitute a new general tomography bound or evidence for additional physical states.

title: UltraTex: Unleashing 2K Multi-View Diffusion for 3D Texturing
abstract: High-quality texture generation is essential for creating realistic and production-ready 3D assets. Recent multi-view diffusion methods have shown promising results for image-guided 3D texturing, but they are typically constrained to low operating resolutions such as 512 or 768, making it difficult to preserve high-frequency details from high-resolution reference images. Scaling this paradigm to 2048 resolution is computationally prohibitive, as the unified multi-view sequence exceeds 212K tokens and incurs excessive memory and latency. In this paper, we present UltraTex, an efficient end-to-end framework for high-resolution multi-view diffusion-based 3D texturing. Our key observation is that object-centric multi-view renderings contain two major sources of redundancy: background-induced sequence redundancy and sparse token interactions within the foreground. To address them, we introduce Background Token Dropping, which removes background tokens before the DiT backbone, and Block-Sparse Attention, which reduces attention computation over the retained foreground sequence. To enable efficient foreground-only inference while avoiding reconstruction artifacts, we further design Foreground-Aware VAE Decoding to ensure the quality of the final high-resolution views. To satisfy the demanding data requirements of 2K-resolution multi-view diffusion training, we construct G-buffer TexVerse, a large-scale, ultra-high-resolution multi-view rendering dataset covering over 268,000 3D assets. Extensive experiments show that UltraTex generates visually faithful textures with rich fine-grained details, while substantially improving efficiency, achieving 20.6times--91.1times training speedup and 22.3times--74.6times end-to-end inference speedup over the baseline on common samples in our dataset. Code and data is at https://yiboz2001.github.io/UltraTex.

title: Indice concettuale di claudiocammarano.com
abstract: A vocabulary of 268 concepts — people, theories, texts, institutions, places and countries — cited with argumentative weight in Claudio Cammarano's writing on claudiocammarano.com. Each entry carries a discursive note, links to the real-world entity on Wikidata and Wikipedia where they exist (169 entries out of 268), the articles in which the concept appears, and 66 asserted links to other concepts, each with the reason for the link. The format is JSON-LD with two standard vocabularies: SKOS for the concept scheme and schema.org for consistency with the markup of the pages themselves. Three proprietary terms — the editorial type of an entry, and the pair that reifies the reason for a link — are declared and dereferenceable at https://claudiocammarano.com/ns/. An external link was accepted only on an exact label or alias match with a compatible type, then verified entry by entry against the note. The limits of the dataset are stated in the README.

title: Practical Guidance for the Installation and Operation of the CubeTechnology System with Artificial Intelligence Support from ChatGPT
abstract: This practical guidance presents a procedure for installing and operating the CubeTechnology system in which artificial intelligence is used as a continuous assistant to the user at all stages of working with the system. The main distinguishing feature of the proposed approach is that the user provides ChatGPT, or another AI service they are accustomed to using, with the CubeTechnology documentation archive. The AI uses a dedicated navigation document within the archive to identify the required manuals and documentation sections, explain the sequence of actions, help verify that the installation has been completed correctly, translate instructions into the user’s native language, support the execution of training and production tasks, and assist in analyzing difficulties that arise during operation. When errors or unexpected results occur, the user can provide the chat with screenshots, calculation logs, program parameters, input and output files, VisualCube scenes, and other diagnostic materials. The AI compares these materials with the system documentation, helps localize the cause of the problem, and proposes a sequence of checks. If the issue cannot be resolved in the chat, the AI can help prepare a message to the author of CubeTechnology, and the author’s reply can then be added to the same chat so that the work can continue. This form of support reduces the user’s dependence on the developer’s constant direct involvement and makes it possible to master the system progressively, from installation and familiarization with the VisualCube multi-window graphical interface to performing seismic data processing and interpretation tasks. The guidance also provides links to the software distribution package, complete documentation, test data, training materials, and related CubeTechnology publications. Related publications: 1. CubeTechnology system presentation: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22122420 2. Announcement of the book on the theoretical foundations of the system: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22064681 3. Special Courses on the Theory of the System: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22108817

title: SparkDiffusion: Mitigating the High-Sparsity Trap --- A Unified Framework for up to 265times Single-GPU Acceleration of Visual Generation
abstract: Video diffusion transformers are expensive because attention dominates long spatiotemporal token sequences. We identify the high-sparsity trap: at extreme attention sparsity, step-local training losses keep decreasing while terminal generation quality stagnates or degrades. The trap is one of supervision: the dominant terminal errors originate in the high-noise structure-generation stage, and terminal-aligned training corrects terminal errors that substantially extended step-local training cannot. This yields a simple staging principle: first adapt the sparse architecture into a coarse prior, then correct the terminal distribution. We instantiate the principle as \method, a unified acceleration framework for visual generation that combines a short sparse warm-up, few-step trajectory-mixed distillation, and FP8 quantization with fused kernels. \method sustains 97% attention sparsity with strong visual quality on long-sequence 720P generation across Wan2.1/Wan2.2 backbones and T2V/I2V tasks, and 90% sparsity on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-480P. With 3-step CFG-free inference, \method achieves a 265times end-to-end speedup over the 50-step CFG dense baseline for Wan2.1-T2V-14B-720P on a single RTX~5090 (220times on H100), and denoises a Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-480P video in 1.3s.

With 3-step CFG-free inference, \method achieves a 265times end-to-end speedup over the 50-step CFG dense baseline for Wan2.1-T2V-14B-720P on a single RTX~5090 (220times on H100), and denoises a Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-480P video in 1.3s.

title: BPFCompat Research Dataset v1: Empirical eBPF Compatibility Across Linux Vendor Kernels
abstract: BPFCompat Research Dataset v1 is a frozen reproducibility package for an empirical pilot study of compiled eBPF artifact compatibility across Linux vendor kernels and loader paths. The canonical pilot contains 70/70 planned executions: 50 compatible, 13 incompatible, and 7 inconclusive. A bounded post-collection stability sample contains 21/21 same-exact-environment observations with no observed environment drift or same-environment verdict instability. The archive includes normalized evidence, deterministic RQ1–RQ4 analysis inputs/outputs, generated paper figures/tables, provenance, exact environment identities, and permitted materialized study inputs. Third-party compiled loader binaries whose complete redistribution notice set was not established are excluded and represented by hashes, source revisions, validation-contract identities, notices, and rebuild provenance. This release is a reproducibility archive of pilot evidence and is not a claim of peer review, population representativeness, institutional approval, or endorsement.

title: The Theory of Asymptotic Non-Closure
abstract: Theory of Asymptotic Non-Closure (ANC) v2.0 expands the framework from an inverse-square entropy barrier (\Omega_M) into a complete optimization paradigm incorporating Causal Generative Independence (L_{\text{CGI}}) and Residual Consequential Agency (RCA) metrics. Validated against COB-0.2 proxy-preserving adversarial attacks, ANC prevents premature unilateral causal closure during gradient descent and defines the speed limit for open-ended alignment (\tau_{\text{spawn}} < \tau_{\text{annex}}).

title: CraftBench-UE: Deterministic Evaluation for Coding Agents in Unreal Engine
abstract: Building gameplay features in a game engine requires more than code, as code that compiles and runs does not necessarily implement the requested gameplay. We introduce CraftBenchUE, an evaluation harness that runs agents in an isolated Unreal Engine environment, reconstructs their saved submissions in fresh projects, and applies deterministic build, asset, and runtime checks without an LLM judge. Based on the harness, we built a benchmark consisting of 70 tasks spanning C++ source, Blueprint assets, and editor scripting. We evaluate seven models under two editor-tool configurations, with a file-and-shell baseline on C++ tasks. We further pair tasks that specify the same gameplay and use the same runtime tests, but require C++ and Blueprint as the deliverables. Across the 10 paired tasks, C++ completion rates exceed Blueprint by 30.0 and 42.9 percentage points in the two tool configurations. Among on-time Blueprint submissions in this paired set that pass asset checks, 42.2% and 50.0% fail explicit runtime assertions. These submissions satisfy asset requirements but fail the required gameplay tests. We will release the harness, task benchmark, and our trajectory findings with the report.

title: Adaptive Fusion-Driven Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Using U-Net++, Capsule Network, and Transformer-Enhanced Extreme Learning
abstract: Multimodal social media data contain textual, visual, and emoji information that can provide complementary cues for sentiment analysis. However, combining these modalities remains challenging because they differ in representation and may contain redundant or noisy information. This study presents an Adaptive Fusion-Driven Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Framework that combines U-Net++ with self-attention, a Capsule Network encoder-decoder, a Cross-Modal Transformer, and a Transformer-Enhanced Extreme Learning Machine (T-ELM). U-Net++ with self-attention extracts contextual features, while the Capsule Network captures hierarchical relationships among the extracted representations. The Cross-Modal Transformer then models interactions between the text, image, and emoji modalities before classification by T-ELM. The trimodal experiments use 9,200 samples selected from the Social Media MultiSent Dataset (SM-MSD), with positive, neutral, and negative sentiment polarity as the target classes. Using a 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test split, the proposed framework achieves competitive sentiment classification performance across the evaluated datasets. The results show that the proposed fusion framework effectively combines complementary multimodal information while keeping the final classification stage lightweight.

title: Speech Language Models for Full-Meeting Speaker Diarization: Capabilities and Limitations
abstract: Recent advances in Speech Language Models (SpeechLMs), which integrate large language models with speech foundation models, have enabled unified sequence modeling of speech processing tasks. However, many SpeechLM-based approaches to speaker diarization (SD) are tightly coupled with automatic speech recognition (ASR) and evaluated using word-level metrics, making it difficult to assess SD performance independent of ASR accuracy. In this work, we investigate ESPnet-SpeechLM as a token-based backbone for generating SD hypotheses, formulating SD as autoregressive generation of structured tokens conditioned on acoustic input. We systematically compare two output representations: an event-based representation that explicitly models speaker turn onset and offset timestamps, and a frame-based representation that predicts frame-level speaker activity. To provide structured conversational cues, we further incorporate auxiliary tasks including speech activity detection, overlapped speech detection, and speaker turn counting within the output sequence. Across multiple meeting datasets, we find that event-based representations produce more stable and consistent SD outputs than frame-based representations. Our analysis shows that outputs generated by SpeechLMs encode useful temporal SD structure, but full-meeting SD remains limited by recording-level speaker tracking and overlap-related misses. Explicit speaker-linking post-processing substantially reduces speaker confusion, suggesting that robust SpeechLM-based SD requires persistent speaker tracking and overlap-aware generation.

title: The Boundary of the Individual as an Authoritative Causal Present — An Architectural Hypothesis
abstract: This study analyzes the publicly disclosable requirements, prior work and evaluation plan for the functional composition B-Core = A-Core + Purple Box / Present. A-Core is a general cognitive and execution system that may also use memory, recurrence and parallel processing. Purple Box / Present is the undisclosed, history-dependent addition; its added role is a research hypothesis. The composition denotes a single B-Core instance. In the deployment examined, the private component remains in a habitat, and the system may use zero or more physical avatars. If connectivity is lost, only the A-Core functions actually deployed locally remain available; the local branch receives no permission to write directly to the central Present. The targeted narrative prior-work map connects conceptual questions of changing embodiment, distributed state authority, offline reconciliation, persistent agent memory and personal identity. A substantial proportion of the public requirements have known antecedents. A new name, a combination of partial mechanisms or an exact expression not established in this targeted review does not establish novelty. Whether the private mechanism is internally identical to or different from another mechanism cannot be determined from the disclosed functional role. The paper distinguishes identification, authority over state changes and continuity of cognitive operation. The uniqueness of committed states is a requirement, not an algorithmic property proved in the manuscript. A finite log may supply a counterexample, but by itself does not prove a general invariant. Physical event history, the accepted record and the permitted effect on the Present are separate objects of inquiry. The main empirical question is G5: what changes when the Purple Box is added to the same A-Core, and does it offer a practical advantage over the strongest technically sound alternative within the same total resource budget? The two comparisons address different estimands. During long-term closed-loop operation, subsequent memory and observations may be consequences of the intervention, so their forced identity cannot be required. The plan requires valid interventions, strong controls and prespecified endpoints. The contribution consists in clarifying compositional and permission boundaries, and organizing falsifiable subhypotheses and comparisons. The study does not present a working Purple Box implementation, a formal system proof or new experimental data. Novelty and added benefit: NOT_ESTABLISHED. The hypothesis is partially testable; full evaluation requires a concrete artifact, an external contract and a preregistered study. © 2026 Omri Bankuti. The public research document and its original figures: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). The undisclosed Purple Box / Present master: PRIVATE / All Rights Reserved. Any separately released public software or test harness: MPL-2.0. The precise scope of the three layers is specified in Sections 21–22.

title: OmniEdu: Open Foundation Models for Learning and Teaching
abstract: Educational foundation models must solve problems, understand curriculum structure, diagnose learner difficulties, and provide appropriate instructional support. Existing educational language models often focus on either problem solving or tutoring, with training mixtures organized by source or task rather than capability. We present OmniEdu, an open family of foundation models for K-12 learning and teaching. Its instruction-tuning corpus combines over 100 educational resources and general instruction sources, organized around four capabilities: subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and pedagogical action and scaffolding. Our pipeline integrates deterministic cleaning, semantic auditing and rewriting, task-specific quality scoring, token-budgeted diversity selection, and pedagogical instruction assignment. It yields 69,999 examples and 15.96M supervised response tokens, including 60,951 education-specific examples. We fine-tune 4B, 9B, and 27B models and evaluate curriculum grounding, K-12 problem solving, and pedagogical tutoring, alongside general capability. Education-oriented tuning consistently improves all three educational benchmark groups across model scales. OmniEdu-27B achieves 63.12% EM and 76.69% F1 on K12-Bench, 85.89% on MathFish, 86.95% on EDUMATH, and 78.74% in MathTutorBench's Scaffold setting. It also achieves the highest Teaching average on LongTutor among the evaluated models, at 3.02. These results demonstrate the value of curated, capability-balanced supervision for adapting general language models to educational tasks spanning problem solving, curriculum understanding, and instructional support.

title: Sufficient for Whose Answer? Three Predicates Under One Word in Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Why the Only One Tied to Correctness Cannot Be Computed Where the Gate Runs
abstract: Life of Research (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. A retrieval-augmented system that answers only when its retrieved context suffices needs a predicate that says when it does. Three incompatible predicates are in circulation under the word "sufficient", and results obtained under different ones are routinely compared as though they measured one quantity. The first is answer-free: an instance has sufficient context if some plausible answer to the question exists given the information in the context, a definition whose authors state explicitly that it does not require a ground truth answer and that it permits the context to contain an incorrect answer. The second is answer-conditional: this evidence supports this candidate claim, the SUPPORTED, REFUTED and NOT ENOUGH INFO structure inherited from fact verification, whose framing document says in as many words that it avoids absolute judgements of factuality. The third is gold-relative: the context supports the gold answer, which is what unanswerable-contrast dataset construction has meant since 2018. This paper argues that only the third predicate entails correctness, that the third is the only one of the three that cannot be computed at inference time because it needs the answer the gate exists to decide whether to produce, and that the decoupling the field reports as an empirical surprise is in one direction a consequence of the definition that makes the gate deployable at all. The published measurements are consistent with that reading and are not usually read that way. On a curated set carrying human-annotated sufficiency labels rather than machine ones, three frontier models hallucinate on 3.2 to 14.3 percent of sufficient-context instances and a 27 billion parameter open model on 25.4 percent, while under insufficient context on that same set they are still correct 7.7 to 23.1 percent of the time; across the larger autorater-labelled analysis the insufficient-context correctness rate runs from 35 to 62 percent, and the study's own qualitative table attributes it to eight causes of which parametric knowledge is one and outright guessing on yes/no and limited-choice questions is another. Both sides of the relation are measured by language models, and each instrument moves the number by double digits: the sufficiency autorater is validated at 0.930 accuracy on 115 instances drawn from four datasets, two of which are not the datasets it is then applied to, and switching the correctness metric from lexical containment to a model judge moves one insufficient-context figure from 46.1 to 59.5 percent and one sufficient-context figure from 48.9 to 74.0. The behaviour the gate is meant to correct does not track sufficiency either: abstention falls when retrieval is added, from 84.1 to 52 percent for one model and from 100 to 18.6 percent for another, and a 2026 controlled study of three small open models finds abstention keyed on whether context is present rather than on whether it supports anything, with answer rates under should-abstain conditions rising from 3.0 percent when context is missing to 82.7 percent when it is misleading. The premise underneath is itself disputed: a 2024 result that adding random documents improves accuracy by up to 35 percent was reproduced in 2026 and found not to survive changes to prompting and decoding. Sufficiency-shaped gates do work where they are built and measured, and the two strongest 2026 systems are read here at their best rather than their worst. What is missing is the joint table: no located work reports all three sufficiency predicates on the same instances, so the rate at which they disagree is unmeasured, and the decision each licenses is therefore unlicensed. The statistical machinery for that table was published in 2026 and carries a single retrieval-success variable; splitting it three ways is the experiment this paper asks for.

title: Rank-Preserving Encryption for Cotangent Similarity using Complex Neutrosophic Sets
abstract: We present a privacy-preserving pipeline for pairwise comparison of complex neutrosophic sets (CNS) that uses a rank-preserving (order-preserving) encryption to pairwise compare cotangent similarity (CotSM). We introduce a visual analysis method for paired target source relationships using rank-preserving encryption that maintains anonymity. On a 3x3 grid of targets (T1-T3) and sources (S1-S3), we produce complementary views: (i) Cotangent Similarity (CotSM) Heatmaps and bar charts, all of which are encrypted; and (ii) Pearson-correlation Heatmaps and 3D surfaces, which are likewise encrypted. T1-S2 (i.e., max 0.4324 in Heatmaps; 0.6653 in bars) relationship is consistently the most significant in all CotSM perspectives, with T1 typically dominating and S2 the most convincing source. On the other hand, encrypted Pearson views had the highest T3 S3 value (normalized maximum 1.000), with T3 dominating and S3 having the biggest influence. The following is a summary of these findings: (1) Since the encryption maintains rank structure (maxima, minima, relative ranking), comparative interpretation is preserved even while veiled magnitudes in T1-S2 are encouraged; and (2) metric selection alters T3-S3 receives a high rank from Pearson’s emphasis on linear alignment, whereas T1-S2 receives a high rank from COTSM’s emphasis on similarity geometry. These hierarchies are only scaled or reformulated by normalization (01) and 3D surfaces. The final result is a secure, understandable pipeline that permits signal matching templates, model selection, and pattern recognition without revealing raw data. Strict data confidentiality is necessary, however this can be used directly in any scenario where any sensitive bi-paired connection needs to be examined, such as biological indications, user item affinities, or multi-sensors fusions.

The final result is a secure, understandable pipeline that permits signal matching templates, model selection, and pattern recognition without revealing raw data. Strict data confidentiality is necessary, however this can be used directly in any scenario where any sensitive bi-paired connection needs to be examined, such as biological indications, user item affinities, or multi-sensors fusions.

title: Neural Spectral Capacity: Measuring and Designing Architectures from Network Specification Alone
abstract: Modern Transformer design and compression both reduce to allocating capacity under a budget. The standard scalars for these decisions, #Params and #FLOPs, capture size and compute but not architectural structure: two architectures with identical parameter budgets but different depth-width, head, or FFN allocations receive identical scores yet behave differently. We propose Neural Spectral Capacity (NSC), a closed-form scalar grounded in the singular-value spectrum of each weight matrix. Under standard random initialization, the Marchenko-Pastur law renders NSC computable from the architectural specification alone, with no model instantiation, data, or gradients. Its layer-wise additive structure admits NSC-DP, an exact dynamic-programming solver returning the architecture globally maximizing NSC under resource constraints in seconds on a CPU -- a guarantee that black-box search over existing training-free proxies cannot provide. Empirically, NSC outperforms #Params, #FLOPs, and representative training-free proxies in ranking across seven Transformer and CNN families (on FlexiBERT, τ= 0.505 on pairs differing in #Params by less than 10%, where #Params collapses to 0.082); NSC-DP discovers a Transformer-XL architecture on WikiText-103 that beats the human-designed baseline in 2 seconds; and prunes LLaMA-7B to the best 5.7B model across eight commonsense reasoning tasks without any calibration data, about 5900x faster than the strongest training-free proxy baseline.

title: Demonstrating Floating-Point Vulnerabilities and Integer-Based Noise Sampling
abstract: Using ten synthetic student records, this program shows how a deliberately low-precision Laplace sampler can produce distinguishable outputs for neighbouring datasets, violating differential privacy. It examines why ordinary rounding and clipping do not automatically repair the problem, then demonstrates discrete Laplace noise sampled directly from random bits using integer arithmetic. The example illustrates implementation principles rather than reproducing the full floating-point attack or providing a production-ready privacy mechanism.
